intro.en: Disillusionment is disillusion plus -ment; the base goes back to Latin illusio, a deceptive appearance, from illudere, to mock, from ludere, to play.
intro.cn: disillusionment 由 disillusion（使醒悟）加 -ment（状态名词后缀）构成；词根上溯拉丁语 illusio「假象」，来自 illudere「戏弄」，再来自 ludere「玩」。

items.en: Latin ludere means to play.
items.cn: 拉丁语 ludere 意为玩。

items.en: Illusio meant a mocking or deceptive appearance.
items.cn: illusio 意为嘲弄或骗人的外观。

items.en: Illusion entered English for a false appearance.
items.cn: illusion 进入英语，表示虚假的外观。

items.en: Dis- gave disillusion, to remove the illusion.
items.cn: dis- 造出 disillusion，意为把幻觉去掉。

items.en: The suffix -ment gave the noun for the resulting state.
items.cn: 后缀 -ment 造出表示结果状态的名词。

items.en: The word is common in writing on politics and work.
items.cn: 这个词在关于政治与工作的论述中很常见。

note.en: Disillusionment is the state left by disillusion; its neighbours share the play root or name lost belief.
note.cn: disillusionment 是 disillusion 留下的状态；它的邻居要么同「玩」词根，要么指失去的信念。

senses.title: The official ending of a law or system
senses.titleCN: 废除：把一条法律从册子上拿掉
senses.definition: the act of ending a law or system by official decision, so that it can no longer operate
senses.definitionCN: 通过官方决定终止某项法律或制度，使其不再运作
senses.example: The abolishment of the licensing system opened the trade to small producers.
senses.exampleCN: 许可制度的废除向小生产者打开了这个行业。
senses.why: Abolishment names the completed act, not the campaign. The law is gone from the books, and the noun records that fact.
senses.whyCN: abolishment 指完成的动作，而不是运动本身。法律已从法典中消失，这个名词记录的就是这一事实。

senses.title: The ending of a long-standing practice
senses.titleCN: 废止：让一种老做法停下来
senses.definition: the act of putting an end to a custom or habit that has been followed for a long time
senses.definitionCN: 终止一种长期沿用的习俗或习惯
senses.example: The abolishment of the daily roll call changed the mood of the school.
senses.exampleCN: 每日点名制度的废止改变了学校的气氛。
senses.why: Here the object is not a statute but a habit. The word treats a custom as something that can be struck out like a rule.
senses.whyCN: 这里废除的对象不是法令，而是习惯。这个词把习俗当作一条可以划掉的规则来处理。

senses.title: The cancellation of a tax or charge
senses.titleCN: 取消：把收费那一行划掉
senses.definition: the removal of a tax, fee, or charge so that it is no longer collected
senses.definitionCN: 取消某项税、费或收费，使其不再征收
senses.example: The abolishment of the tax took effect on the first of January.
senses.exampleCN: 该税种的废除于一月一日生效。
senses.why: Money gives the word a concrete edge: a line in the revenue book is crossed out, and people stop paying.
senses.whyCN: 钱让这个词有了具体的锋刃：收入簿上的一行被划掉，人们不再缴这笔钱。

senses.title: The elimination of an institution
senses.titleCN: 废除制度：把一整套机构撤掉
senses.definition: the ending of an institution such as slavery, a monarchy, or a privileged order
senses.definitionCN: 终止奴隶制、君主制或某种特权等级这样的制度
senses.example: The abolishment of slavery was written into the new constitution.
senses.exampleCN: 废除奴隶制被写进新宪法。
senses.why: This is the word's most famous use, because an institution is exactly what abolishment is built to remove.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词最著名的用法，因为“制度”正是 abolishment 天生要移除的对象。

senses.title: A legal annulment of a statute
senses.titleCN: 撤销：法庭把条文判为无效
senses.definition: the annulment of a statute or regulation by a body with legal authority
senses.definitionCN: 由有法律权限的机构宣布某法令或规章无效
senses.example: The court ordered the abolishment of the disputed regulation.
senses.exampleCN: 法院下令撤销那项有争议的规章。
senses.why: Law treats abolishment as a technical act with a date and a signature, distinct from merely ignoring a rule.
senses.whyCN: 法律把 abolishment 当作有日期、有签字的技术性行为，与单纯“不理这条规则”不同。

senses.title: The state of having been abolished
senses.titleCN: 被废：废除之后留下的空位
senses.definition: the condition of something that no longer exists as an active rule or body
senses.definitionCN: 某事物已不再作为有效规则或机构存在的状态
senses.example: After the abolishment of the office, its files sat unread for years.
senses.exampleCN: 该机构被撤销后，它的档案多年无人翻阅。
senses.why: The -ment noun can name either the act or its result, as with many English nouns of action. Here it names the resulting emptiness.
senses.whyCN: 像许多英语动作名词一样，-ment 名词既可指动作，也可指结果。这里它指结果留下的空位。

senses.title: A formal declaration that something is void
senses.titleCN: 宣告作废：当众宣布它不再算数
senses.definition: a public or formal proclamation that a rule, title, or arrangement has no further force
senses.definitionCN: 公开或正式宣告某规则、头衔或安排不再有效
senses.example: The council issued a formal abolishment of the old charter.
senses.exampleCN: 议事会正式宣告旧特许状作废。
senses.why: The noun can stand for the document or ceremony of ending, not only the ending itself; the declaration is the visible form of the act.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词也可指“终止的文件或仪式”，而不只是终止本身；宣告是这一动作看得见的形式。

senses.title: The removal of an office or post
senses.definition: the ending of a position or office, usually in older administrative writing
senses.definitionCN: 取消某个职位或机构编制，多见于较早的行政文本
senses.example: The abolishment of the post of town crier saved little money but ended a tradition.
senses.exampleCN: 裁撤街头公告员一职省不了多少钱，却终结了一项传统。
senses.why: An office is a small institution, and the word treats it the same way: the post is struck from the list of established positions.
senses.whyCN: 一个职位就是一个小制度，这个词照样处理：把它从在编职位的清单上划掉。

intro.en: Abolishment is an English-made noun: the verb abolish plus -ment. Its twin abolition came straight from Latin abolitio, which is why English has two near-identical words for one act.
intro.cn: abolishment 是英语自造的名词：动词 abolish 加 -ment。它的孪生词 abolition 直接来自拉丁语 abolitio，所以英语为一个动作留下了两个几乎相同的词。

items.en: To grow or be nourished, related to alere 'to feed'. Its exact contribution to abolere is debated, so the common gloss 'destroy so that it can grow no more' is a reconstruction rather than a certainty.
items.cn: 意为生长、得到滋养，与 alere“喂养”相关。它在 abolere 中究竟起什么作用仍有争论，因此常用解释“毁掉使其不能再生长”只是构拟，并非定论。

items.en: Away, off, from. Added to a verb of growth it suggests removing the conditions under which something could continue.
items.cn: 离开、去掉、脱离。加在表示生长的动词上，暗示移除某物得以继续的条件。

items.en: To efface, destroy, annul. The word is used of blotting out a name, cancelling a law, and wiping out a memory.
items.cn: 抹去、毁灭、废止。这个词可用于抹掉一个名字、取消一条法律、清除一段记忆。

items.en: A cancelling or abolishing, and also a pardon. The Latin noun is the direct source of the English doublet abolition.
items.cn: 取消、废除，也有“赦免”之义。这个拉丁名词正是英语孪生词 abolition 的直接来源。

items.en: To abolish, recorded in the 13c and carried into Middle English as abolisshen. French supplied the verb shape that English kept.
items.cn: 废除，13 世纪已有记录，并以 abolisshen 进入中古英语。法语提供了英语保留下来的动词形态。

items.en: English adds -ment to the French-derived verb and produces abolishment. Abolition enters separately from Latin, so the two nouns divide the work by register: abolition is the standard term, abolishment the formal or legal variant.
items.cn: 英语在法语来源的动词后加 -ment，造出 abolishment。abolition 另从拉丁语进入，于是两个名词按语体分工：abolition 是标准词，abolishment 是正式或法律变体。

note.en: The first group is the abolish family, where the -ment and -ion twins sit side by side; the second compares other words for ending something officially.
note.cn: 第一组是 abolish 词族，-ment 与 -ion 两个孪生词并列其中；第二组比较其他表示“正式终止”的词。

entries.definition: to end a law, system, or practice officially. The verb names the act; the noun names it or its result.
entries.definitionCN: 正式终止法律、制度或做法。动词指动作，名词指动作或其结果。

entries.definition: the ending of a system, especially slavery. It is the standard noun and carries the historical weight of the anti-slavery movement.
entries.definitionCN: 制度的终止，尤指奴隶制。它是标准名词，承载废奴运动的历史重量。

entries.definition: a person who campaigns for an institution to be abolished. The -ist marks the agent, not the act.
entries.definitionCN: 主张废除某项制度的人；-ist 标记行动者，而非动作。

entries.definition: able to be abolished. It is a legal and administrative word rather than an everyday one.
entries.definitionCN: 可以被废除的；属于法律与行政用语，而非日常词。

entries.definition: the formal cancellation of a law by the body that made it. It is the precise legal partner of abolishment.
entries.definitionCN: 由立法机关对法律作出的正式取消；是 abolishment 精确的法律伙伴。

entries.definition: the taking back of a licence, right, or permission. It withdraws an authorisation rather than ending a system.
entries.definitionCN: 收回执照、权利或许可；它撤回的是授权，而不是终止一套制度。

entries.definition: a declaration that something never had valid force. It erases the act retrospectively.
entries.definitionCN: 宣告某事物从一开始就无效；它是追溯性地抹掉那个行为。

entries.definition: the complete removal of something unwanted. It is broader and less legal than abolishment.
entries.definitionCN: 彻底移除不想要的东西；比 abolishment 更宽泛，也更少法律色彩。

entries.definition: the same act under its Latin-derived name. In modern writing it is the default choice.
entries.definitionCN: 同一动作的拉丁语来源名称；在现代写作中它是默认选择。

normalIntro.en: Real parts only: Latin abolere 'to wipe out', Old French abolir, English abolish, plus -ment. The Latin twin abolition came by a separate road.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：拉丁语 abolere“抹去”，古法语 abolir，英语 abolish，再加 -ment。拉丁语孪生词 abolition 走的是另一条路。

normal.en: -ment turns the verb into the act: abolish plus -ment is the doing of it.
normal.cn: -ment 把动词变成动作名词：abolish 加 -ment 就是“废除这件事”。

normal.en: Abolition and abolishment are twins: one from Latin abolitio, one made in English.
normal.cn: abolition 与 abolishment 是孪生：一个来自拉丁语 abolitio，一个在英语里造出。

normal.en: To abolish is to blot a line out of the book, not just to stop obeying it.
normal.cn: 废除，是把那一行从册子上抹掉，而不只是不再遵守它。

normal.en: The most famous abolishment is the ending of slavery, an institution struck from the constitution.
normal.cn: 最著名的 abolishment 是废除奴隶制：一整套制度被从宪法中划掉。

normal.en: Abolishment is rarer than abolition: when you see it, the text is usually legal or formal.
normal.cn: abolishment 比 abolition 少见：看到它时，文本通常偏法律或正式。

abstract.en: To abolish is to decide that something must stop being possible.
abstract.cn: 废除，就是决定让某件事不再可能发生。

abstract.en: Every abolishment leaves a blank line where an institution used to be.
abstract.cn: 每一次废除，都在制度曾经所在的地方留下一行空白。

abstract.en: A society is partly described by what it has chosen to abolish.
abstract.cn: 一个社会，部分地由它选择废除的东西来描述。

examples.en: The abolishment of the old tariff was welcomed by the port towns.
examples.cn: 旧关税的废除受到港口城镇的欢迎。

examples.en: Historians still argue about the economic effects of the abolishment of slavery.
examples.cn: 历史学家至今仍在争论废除奴隶制的经济影响。

examples.en: The report recommended the abolishment of the post rather than a pay cut.
examples.cn: 报告建议裁撤该职位，而不是减薪。

dict_mnemonic.text: “阿伯利什门特”——阿伯把不利的条款“门”一关、划掉 → abolishment 废除

root: 英语在动词 abolish（← 古法语 abolir ← 拉丁语 abolere“抹去、废止”，ab-“离开”+ olere“生长”）后加 -ment 构成；与直接来自拉丁语 abolitio 的 abolition 是同义孪生词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of abolishment, one gesture: a line is drawn through something and it stops counting. The objects range from a tax to an institution to a single post.
sensesIntro.cn: abolishment 的八个义项只有一个动作：在某样东西上划一道线，它就不再算数。对象从一项税，到一整套制度，再到一个职位。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a clause-covered page crossed out and torn from the book.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张写满条款的纸被划掉，并从册子上撕下。

branches.en: LAW: a system ended by policy and a statute annulled by a court are both struck from the books.
branches.cn: 法律：由政策终止的制度与由法院撤销的法令，都是从册子上划掉的。

branches.en: INSTITUTIONS AND OFFICES: slavery and a town crier's post are the same kind of listed thing, one large and one small.
branches.cn: 制度与职位：奴隶制与街头公告员的职位，是同一种“在册条目”，一大一小。

branches.en: MONEY: a tax is cancelled and the revenue line goes blank.
branches.cn: 钱：一项税被取消，收入簿上的那一行就空了。

branches.en: PRACTICE AND PROCLAMATION: a custom is ended, and the ending is announced so everyone knows it no longer counts.
branches.cn: 习俗与宣告：一种做法被终止，并且当众宣布，让所有人知道它不再算数。

branches.en: THE RESULT: what remains is not the act but the empty place it left.
branches.cn: 结果：留下的不是动作，而是动作腾出的空位。

intro.en: Abolishment is built with the noun suffix -ment on a French-derived verb. Its doublet uses -ion, and the surrounding family adds -ist and -able.
intro.cn: abolishment 由名词后缀 -ment 加在法语来源的动词上构成。它的孪生词用 -ion，周围词族再加 -ist 与 -able。

latinIntro.en: The Latin chain is olere 'to grow', abolere 'to wipe out', and abolitio 'a cancelling'. French abolir sits between Latin and English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语链条是 olere“生长”、abolere“抹去”、abolitio“取消”。法语 abolir 位于拉丁语与英语之间。

items.meaning: to end a law or system officially
items.meaningCN: 正式终止法律或制度（-ish 为英语动词化结尾）
items.example: Parliament voted to abolish the duty.
items.exampleCN: 议会投票废除该税。

items.meaningCN: 废除的行为（-ment 构成动作名词）
items.example: The abolishment of the rule came after years of debate.
items.exampleCN: 该规则的废除在多年辩论之后到来。

items.meaning: the ending of a system, especially slavery
items.meaningCN: 制度的终止，尤指奴隶制（拉丁语动作名词）
items.example: The museum documents the abolition of the slave trade.
items.exampleCN: 博物馆记录了奴隶贸易的废除。

items.meaning: a person who works to abolish an institution
items.meaningCN: 致力于废除某制度的人（-ist 表示行动者）
items.example: The abolitionist wrote pamphlets against the trade.
items.exampleCN: 那位废奴主义者撰写小册子反对奴隶贸易。

items.meaningCN: 可被废除的（-able 表示可能性）
items.example: The committee asked whether the levy was abolishable by decree.
items.exampleCN: 委员会询问该征税能否由法令废除。

items.meaning: still in force; not yet ended
items.meaningCN: 尚未废除的；仍然有效的（un- 表否定）
items.example: Several unabolished statutes still mention the old currency.
items.exampleCN: 若干未废除的法规仍提到旧货币。

items.meaning: the historical ending of the slave system
items.meaningCN: 奴隶制的历史性废除（固定短语）
items.example: The painting commemorates the abolishment of slavery.
items.exampleCN: 这幅画纪念奴隶制的废除。

items.meaningCN: 正式且有记录的废除（固定搭配）
items.example: Only formal abolishment would satisfy the court.
items.exampleCN: 只有正式废除才能让法院满意。

items.meaning: an ending with no exceptions or remnants
items.meaningCN: 无例外、无残留的彻底废除（固定搭配）
items.example: They demanded total abolishment, not a gradual phase-out.
items.exampleCN: 他们要求彻底废除，而不是逐步淘汰。

items.meaning: to demand that something be ended
items.meaningCN: 呼吁废除某事物（动词短语结构）
items.example: Doctors called for the abolishment of the fee.
items.exampleCN: 医生们呼吁取消这项收费。

definition_zh: 等级制度；层级体系；统治集团；阶层
definition_en: a system in which people or things are arranged in ranks, with each level ranking above or below another
core_image: 一座一级一级向上收窄的金字塔，每层只对紧挨着的上一层负责
scene: 这里指「等级制度」。 In the hospital, a strict hierarchy decides who may overrule whom during an emergency.
sceneCN: 这里 hierarchy 是「等级体系」（第 1 个义项：组织内部按上下级排列的层级结构）；句意：在医院里，一套严格的等级体系决定紧急情况下谁可以否决谁。场景要点：手术台旁不同颜色的工牌、由下向上的汇报链、每一层只对紧挨着的上一层负责。

pos.zh: 等级制度；层级体系；阶层
（生物学）分类层级；（计算机）层次结构

derivatives.zh: 等级制的；按等级划分的
等级的；层级式的
等级体系中的高层人物；高级教士
按等级地；按层级地
等级体系的（较少用变体）

senses.title: A ranked organisation of people
senses.definition: a system in which people or positions are arranged in ranks, so that each rank has authority over the one below it
senses.definitionCN: 把人或职位按等级排列的体系，每一级对下一级拥有权威
senses.example: The firm's hierarchy puts every decision through three levels of approval.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司的等级体系让每项决定都要经过三层审批。
senses.why: The core image is a pyramid that narrows as it rises: each level holds authority over the level beneath it, and the shape of the whole depends on that step-by-step arrangement.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是一座向上收窄的金字塔：每一级对下面一级拥有权威，整体的形状就取决于这种逐级排列。

senses.title: A ranking by importance
senses.definition: an ordering of things from most to least important, powerful, or urgent
senses.definitionCN: 按重要、强大或紧急程度从高到低排列的顺序
senses.example: The report sets out a hierarchy of risks, from flooding to noise.
senses.exampleCN: 报告列出了一个风险层级，从洪水一直到噪音。
senses.why: The pyramid can also be built from things rather than people: what sits near the top matters more, and what sits below can wait. The vertical order becomes a scale of value.
senses.whyCN: 这座金字塔也可以由事物而不是人来搭建：靠近顶端的更重要，下面的可以等。垂直顺序由此变成价值尺度。

senses.title: The ruling group at the top
senses.definition: the small group of people who hold the highest positions and control an organisation or society
senses.definitionCN: 占据最高位置、控制某一组织或社会的一小群人
senses.example: Reform was blocked by the party hierarchy.
senses.exampleCN: 改革被党的上层集团阻挠了。
senses.why: By a common shift, the name of the structure comes to mean the people at its narrow top. The pyramid is reduced to its peak, and 'the hierarchy' becomes 'those who decide'.
senses.whyCN: 一种常见的转喻：结构的名称变成了结构顶端那一小群人。金字塔被缩减为塔尖，the hierarchy 也就成了“决定者”。

senses.title: Biological classification ranks
senses.definition: the nested series of categories used to classify organisms, from kingdom down to species
senses.definitionCN: 用于对生物分类的一整套嵌套范畴，从界一直到种
senses.example: Linnaeus arranged living things in a hierarchy of kingdom, class, order, genus and species.
senses.exampleCN: 林奈把生物安排进界、纲、目、属、种这样的层级中。
senses.why: Taxonomy is a pyramid of sets: each rank contains the ranks below it, so a species sits inside a genus, a genus inside a family. The word's vertical shape fits nested classification exactly.
senses.whyCN: 分类学是一个集合的金字塔：每一级都包含下面几级，所以种在属内，属在科内。这个词的垂直形状恰好适合嵌套分类。

senses.title: A layered structure in computing
senses.definition: an arrangement of files, data, or system layers in which each level is contained in or depends on the level above
senses.definitionCN: 文件、数据或系统层次的安排方式，每一层被上一层包含或依赖上一层
senses.example: The folder hierarchy puts every image under its project year.
senses.exampleCN: 这个文件夹层级把每张图片放在对应的项目年份之下。
senses.why: A file tree is a pyramid drawn sideways: one root, branching levels, each item belonging to exactly one parent. The social image survives as containment and dependence rather than authority.
senses.whyCN: 文件树是把金字塔横着画：一个根、逐层分支、每一项只属于一个父项。社会意象在这里保存为包含与依赖，而不是权威。

senses.title: The nine orders of angels
senses.titleCN: 天使九阶：最初的神学义
senses.definition: in Christian theology, the ranked divisions of angels described by Dionysius the Areopagite; the word's earliest English sense
senses.definitionCN: 基督教神学中由伪丢尼修描述的天使等级划分；这是该词最早的英语义项
senses.example: Medieval writers mapped the nine angelic hierarchy onto the nine spheres of heaven.
senses.exampleCN: 中世纪作家把天使九阶对应到九重天球上。
senses.why: The word entered English in the late 14th century as a name for the sacred order of angels. Its first hierarchy was not a company but a cosmos: ranks of being, each closer to the divine than the one below.
senses.whyCN: 这个词在 14 世纪晚期进入英语时，是天使神圣秩序的名称。它最初的层级不是公司，而是宇宙：存在的等级，每一级都比下一级更接近神。

senses.title: The order of the clergy
senses.definition: the ranked order of clergy, from deacon and priest up to bishop and pope
senses.definitionCN: 神职人员的等级秩序，从执事、司铎一直向上到主教与教宗
senses.example: A bishop's place in the hierarchy was fixed by canon law.
senses.exampleCN: 主教在教阶体系中的位置由教会法规定。
senses.why: The Greek source means 'rule of a high priest', so the church is where the word feels most at home. Each rank holds sacred office over the rank below, and the ladder runs up to a single summit.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语源头意为“大祭司的统治”，因此教会是这个词最如鱼得水的地方。每一级对下一级拥有圣职权威，阶梯一直通向唯一的顶端。

senses.title: A hierarchy of knowledge or values
senses.definition: an abstract ordering in which ideas, laws, or values are ranked as more fundamental than others
senses.definitionCN: 把观念、法律或价值按根本程度排列的抽象秩序
senses.example: In legal theory, the constitution sits at the top of a hierarchy of norms.
senses.exampleCN: 在法律理论中，宪法位于规范层级的顶端。
senses.why: Once the image is abstract, anything that can be 'higher' or 'lower' in rank can form a hierarchy: norms, needs, genres, values. The pyramid becomes a way of saying that some things rest on others.
senses.whyCN: 一旦意象抽象化，任何能在等级上分“高下”的东西都能构成 hierarchy：规范、需求、文类、价值。金字塔变成一种说法，表示某些事物依托于另一些事物。

intro.en: Hierarchy began as a word for the ranks of angels, built from Greek words for 'sacred' and 'rule'. Its modern organisational sense is much later. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: hierarchy 最初是天使等级的名称，由希腊语“神圣”与“统治”两个词构成。它现代的组织义要晚得多。年代为大致估计。

items.en: First recorded in English as jerarchie / ierarchie, meaning 'rank in the sacred order' and 'one of the three divisions of the nine orders of angels'; loosely also 'rule, dominion'.
items.cn: 最早以 jerarchie／ierarchie 记录于 14 世纪晚期，意为“神圣秩序中的等级”以及“天使九阶中三大划分之一”；宽泛地也指“统治、管辖”。

items.en: From Old French ierarchie (14c., Modern French hiérarchie), from Medieval Latin hierarchia 'ranked division of angels', the system of Dionysius the Areopagite.
items.cn: 来自古法语 ierarchie（14 世纪，现代法语 hiérarchie），再来自中世纪拉丁语 hierarchia“天使的等级划分”，即伪丢尼修的体系。

items.en: Greek hierarkhia meant 'rule of a high priest', from hierarkhēs 'high priest, leader of sacred rites': ta hiera 'the sacred rites' (from hieros 'sacred') plus arkhein 'to lead, rule'.
items.cn: 希腊语 hierarkhia 意为“大祭司的统治”，来自 hierarkhēs“大祭司、圣礼的主持者”：ta hiera“圣礼”（出自 hieros“神圣”）加 arkhein“引领、统治”。

items.en: The sense 'ranked organisation of persons or things' is recorded in English by the 1610s, at first of the clergy. It was probably reinforced by the unrelated English word higher, which sounds like the start of hierarchy.
items.cn: “人或事物的等级组织”这一义项在 17 世纪 10 年代有记录，最初用于神职人员。它很可能被无关的英语词 higher 强化，因为 higher 听起来像 hierarchy 的开头。

items.en: The word extends to secular institutions, then to natural classification. Taxonomy, army ranks and civil service grades all become hierarchies in ordinary speech.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到世俗机构，再扩展到自然分类。分类学、军衔与文官等级在日常语言中都成了 hierarchy。

items.en: Management theory, linguistics and computing adopt it: chain of command, syntactic hierarchy, folder hierarchy. The Greek sacred order becomes a general model of layered structure.
items.cn: 管理学、语言学与计算机科学采用它：指挥链、句法层级、文件夹层级。希腊的神圣秩序变成了分层结构的一般模型。

note.en: The first group separates the noun from its adjective and person forms, and warns about the unrelated word higher; the second group compares ways of ordering people and things.
note.cn: 第一组把名词与它的形容词、指人形式分开，并提醒注意无关的 higher；第二组比较排列人与事物的不同说法。

entries.definition: arranged in ranks, or organised by levels of authority. It describes the shape; hierarchy is the shape itself.
entries.definitionCN: 按等级排列的，或按权威层级组织的。它描述形状；hierarchy 是形状本身。

entries.definition: a person at the top of a hierarchy, especially a senior cleric. It names one holder of rank, not the system of ranks.
entries.definitionCN: 等级体系顶端的人，尤指高级教士。它命名一位占据等级的人，而不是等级体系。

entries.definition: an uncommon variant of hierarchical. It is best avoided when hierarchical is available, since the two are easily confused in writing.
entries.definitionCN: hierarchical 的不常见变体。既然有 hierarchical，最好避免使用，因为两者在书面上极易混淆。

entries.definition: the comparative of high. It is not related to hierarchy, though its sound probably helped the modern sense of ranked organisation take hold.
entries.definitionCN: high 的比较级。它与 hierarchy 没有词源关系，但它的读音很可能帮助了现代“等级组织”义项扎根。

entries.definition: a single level or position in an order. Rank is one rung; hierarchy is the whole ladder and the rule that connects its rungs.
entries.definitionCN: 秩序中的单个级别或位置。rank 是一级横档；hierarchy 是整架梯子以及连接各横档的规则。

entries.definition: the way things are arranged, or a sequence. Order can be flat and neutral, like alphabetical order; hierarchy always implies higher and lower.
entries.definitionCN: 事物被安排的方式，或序列。order 可以是平铺中性的，如字母顺序；hierarchy 总含高下之分。

entries.definition: the informal ranking of status within a group, originally observed in hens. It is vivid and colloquial; hierarchy is neutral and structural.
entries.definitionCN: 群体内部非正式的位次排序，最初来自对鸡群的观察。它形象而口语化；hierarchy 中性且结构化。

entries.definition: the line through which orders pass from superior to subordinate. It stresses communication and obedience, while hierarchy stresses the whole ranked structure.
entries.definitionCN: 命令由上级传到下级的线路。它强调传达与服从，hierarchy 则强调整个等级结构。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: Greek hieros 'sacred' plus arkhein 'to rule', and the arch- family that still marks rule in English.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：希腊语 hieros“神圣”加 arkhein“统治”，以及英语中仍标记“统治”的 arch- 词族。

normal.en: Hierarchy literally joins 'sacred' and 'rule': its first home was the order of angels, not the office org chart.
normal.cn: hierarchy 字面上把“神圣”与“统治”连在一起：它最初的家是天使的秩序，而不是办公室的组织图。

normal.en: The arch- in hierarchy is the same arch- that rules in monarchy, anarchy and patriarch: arkhein means 'to lead, rule'.
normal.cn: hierarchy 里的 arch- 与 monarchy、anarchy、patriarch 中表示统治的 arch- 相同：arkhein 意为“引领、统治”。

normal.en: Hierarchy and higher are not related. The resemblance is a coincidence that probably helped the modern meaning feel natural.
normal.cn: hierarchy 与 higher 没有词源关系。这种相似是巧合，但它很可能让现代词义显得更自然。

normal.en: A hierarchy of needs is a real fixed phrase from psychology: needs are stacked, with basic ones below and refined ones above.
normal.cn: hierarchy of needs 是心理学中真实的固定说法：需求被堆叠起来，基本需求在下，精致需求在上。

normal.en: In computing, a folder hierarchy is a tree: one root, many branches, every item with exactly one parent.
normal.cn: 在计算机中，文件夹层级是一棵树：一个根、许多分支，每一项只有一个父项。

abstract.en: Picture a pyramid of stone steps: the base is wide, the top is narrow, and each step exists only because the one below holds it up.
abstract.cn: 想象一座石阶金字塔：底部宽，顶端窄，每一级之所以存在，是因为下面一级托着它。

abstract.en: The same pyramid can be made of people, ranks, species, files or values. What stays constant is that some things rest on others and none may float.
abstract.cn: 同一座金字塔可以由人、军衔、物种、文件或价值搭成。不变的是：某些事物依托于另一些事物，没有谁能悬空。

abstract.en: When people say 'the hierarchy', they mean the narrow top of the pyramid: the structure has shrunk to the few who decide.
abstract.cn: 当人们说 the hierarchy，指的是金字塔狭窄的顶端：整个结构被缩减为少数做决定的人。

examples.en: The old monastery kept a hierarchy so precise that even the order of seating was recorded.
examples.cn: 那座古老修道院的等级秩序精确到连座次都被记录下来。

examples.en: Flat teams often claim to have no hierarchy, yet informal rankings reappear within weeks.
examples.cn: 扁平化团队常声称没有等级，但非正式的位次几周内就会重新出现。

examples.en: The database stores every page in a hierarchy of folders rather than a single list.
examples.cn: 这个数据库把每个页面存放在文件夹层级中，而不是一张单层列表里。

dict_mnemonic.text: “海尔拉基”——海尔把员工拉成一级一级的基座，越往上人越少 → hierarchy 等级制度

root: 源自希腊语 hierarkhia“大祭司的统治”，由 hieros“神圣”+ arkhein“统治”构成，核心是“按等级层层向上、每层对下层拥有权威”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of hierarchy, all grown from one shape: a pyramid of ranks in which each level rests on the one below and answers to the one above.
sensesIntro.cn: hierarchy 的八个义项都从同一个形状长出来：一座等级金字塔，每一级依托下一级，并向上一级负责。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a narrowing pyramid of ranks, each level resting on the one below and answering to the one above.
core.cn: 核心意象：一座逐级收窄的等级金字塔，每层依托下层，并对上层负责。

branches.en: ORGANISATION AND POWER: a ranked body of people, and then the narrow group at its top who actually decide.
branches.cn: 组织与权力：先是按等级排列的人群，再是位于塔尖、真正做决定的那一小群。

branches.en: ORDERING: the same vertical shape ranks risks, needs, norms and values by importance or fundamentality.
branches.cn: 排序：同一垂直形状按重要性或根本性排列风险、需求、规范与价值。

branches.en: BIOLOGY: nested sets reproduce the pyramid exactly, since each taxonomic rank contains the ranks below it.
branches.cn: 生物学：嵌套集合精确复制了金字塔，因为每个分类层级都包含下面几级。

branches.en: COMPUTING: a tree is the pyramid laid on its side, with containment and dependency instead of obedience.
branches.cn: 计算机：树是横放的金字塔，用包含与依赖替代了服从。

branches.en: THE SACRED SOURCE: angels and clergy are the word's first home, where rank means proximity to the divine.
branches.cn: 神圣源头：天使与神职人员是这个词最初的家，等级意味着与神更近。

intro.en: Hierarchy is a Greek compound borrowed through Latin and French: hieros 'sacred' + arkhein 'to rule'. English adds -al, -ic, -ically and -arch to the same stem.
intro.cn: hierarchy 是经拉丁语和法语借入的希腊语复合词：hieros“神圣”+ arkhein“统治”。英语在同一词干上加 -al、-ic、-ically 与 -arch。

latinIntro.en: Medieval Latin hierarchia and hierarcha carried the Greek word into church writing. The second element, arkhein, is the source of the productive English combining form -arch, meaning 'ruler'.
latinIntro.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 hierarchia 与 hierarcha 把这个希腊词带进教会写作。第二个成分 arkhein 是英语能产后缀 -arch（意为“统治者”）的来源。

items.meaningCN: 等级制的；按层级划分的（-ical 构成形容词）
items.example: The archive uses a hierarchical system of folders.
items.exampleCN: 这个档案库使用层级化的文件夹系统。

items.meaning: of or relating to a hierarchy
items.meaningCN: 等级体系的；层级式的（-ic 构成形容词）
items.example: The diagram shows the hierarchic links between teams.
items.exampleCN: 这张图显示各团队之间的层级联系。

items.meaning: a chief ruler in sacred matters; a high-ranking member of a hierarchy
items.meaningCN: 高级教士；等级体系中的高层人物
items.example: The hierarch blessed the new chapel.
items.exampleCN: 这位高级教士为新礼拜堂祝圣。

items.meaning: in a ranked or layered way
items.example: The data is organised hierarchically, from region to street.
items.exampleCN: 数据按层级组织，从大区一直到街道。

items.meaningCN: 等级体系的（较少使用的形容词变体）
items.example: Older texts prefer hierarchal to hierarchical.
items.exampleCN: 较早的文本更爱用 hierarchal 而不是 hierarchical。

items.meaningCN: 君主制；一人统治（mono- 单一 + -archy 统治）
items.example: The monarchy survived the revolution in a ceremonial form.
items.exampleCN: 君主制以礼仪形式在革命后存续下来。

items.meaning: a state without government or order
items.meaningCN: 无政府状态；混乱（an- 无 + -archy 统治）
items.example: The power cut left the station in near anarchy.
items.exampleCN: 停电让车站几乎陷入无秩序状态。

items.example: The company drifted into an oligarchy of three directors.
items.exampleCN: 这家公司逐渐变成三位董事的寡头统治。

items.meaning: the male head of a family or church
items.meaningCN: 家长；宗主教（patri- 父 + -arch 统治者）
items.example: The patriarch led the procession.
items.exampleCN: 宗主教带领了游行队伍。

items.meaning: a bishop of the highest rank
items.example: The archbishop convened the council.
items.exampleCN: 大主教召集了会议。

items.meaning: a chief magistrate in ancient Athens
items.example: The archon was chosen by lot each year.
items.exampleCN: 执政官每年以抽签方式选出。

latinEntries.structure: Greek hierarkhia, borrowed into Medieval Latin
latinEntries.meaning: the ranked division of angels; sacred rule
latinEntries.meaningCN: 天使的等级划分；神圣统治

latinEntries.meaning: a high priest, one who rules in sacred things

definition_zh: 对……有影响；对……产生作用；冲击……；影响……的程度
definition_en: to produce an effect on something, whether a strong one or a limited one, and whether intended or not
core_image: 一枚铁球从架上荡下，撞上一块薄板，板面凹进去一小块，凹痕的边缘向外散开
scene: 评估会上，一张曲线图被投到墙上，显示某项补贴实施后几个行业的变化。 The subsidy may have an impact on small farms more than on large ones.
sceneCN: 这里指对某类对象产生作用（第 1 个义项：对结果或群体产生影响）；句意为这项补贴对小农场的影响可能大于对大农场的影响。图中可辨识物件：投影曲线、补贴文件、农场分布图、记号笔。

pos.zh: 对……有影响（及物动词短语，后接受影响的对象）
对……产生作用；冲击……（可用于物理碰撞或抽象作用）

collocations.phrase: have an impact on the environment
have an impact on decision making
have an impact on the outcome

derivatives.zh: 短语中的核心名词兼动词，义为「冲击；影响」
由名词加过去分词词尾构成，义为「受影响的；压紧的」
由名词加形容词尾构成，义为「有冲击力的」，多用于评论语体
由动词加名词尾构成，义为「嵌塞；压紧」，多用于医学

senses.title: Influence an outcome
senses.definition: to change the course or the size of a result
senses.definitionCN: 改变结果的方向或大小
senses.example: A small change in the interest rate can have an impact on housing starts.
senses.exampleCN: 利率的小幅变动，可能对新屋开工产生影响。
senses.why: The noun came from a word for driving something in; an effect that drives into a situation leaves a mark there.
senses.whyCN: 核心名词出自表示「把某物打进去」的词；打进局面的作用会在那里留下痕迹。

senses.title: Change how people work
senses.definition: to alter the way people carry out their work
senses.definitionCN: 改变人们开展工作的方式
senses.example: Automation may have an impact on the number of clerks in the office.
senses.exampleCN: 自动化可能影响办公室职员的人数。
senses.why: A machine driven into an office leaves a dent in the number of hands needed.
senses.whyCN: 机器撞进办公室，在所需人手数目上留下凹痕。

senses.title: Affect living things
senses.definition: to alter the timing, numbers or health of organisms
senses.definitionCN: 改变生物的时序、数量或健康状况
senses.example: Warmer springs should have an impact on the timing of bird migration.
senses.exampleCN: 更暖的春天会对鸟类迁徙的时间产生影响。
senses.why: A warmer spring strikes the timing of migration and leaves a dent in it.
senses.whyCN: 更暖的春天撞在迁徙时序上，并在那里留下凹痕。

senses.title: Shape personal beliefs
senses.definition: to alter what a person thinks or chooses
senses.definitionCN: 改变一个人的想法或选择
senses.example: A single teacher can have an impact on a student's choice of study.
senses.exampleCN: 一位老师就可能影响学生对专业的选择。
senses.why: A teacher's words strike a young mind and leave a dent that lasts.
senses.whyCN: 老师的话撞在年轻的心上，留下持久的凹痕。

senses.title: Sway public opinion
senses.definition: to shift how an audience understands an event
senses.definitionCN: 改变受众对某一事件的理解
senses.example: The broadcast may have an impact on how the audience reads the vote.
senses.exampleCN: 这次播报可能影响受众如何解读那次表决。
senses.why: A broadcast strikes an audience's reading of a vote and bends it.
senses.whyCN: 一次播报撞上受众对表决的解读，并使其弯折。

senses.title: Distort research results
senses.definition: to introduce a change into measurements or estimates
senses.definitionCN: 使测量或估计发生偏差
senses.example: A small error in the scale can have an impact on the final estimate.
senses.exampleCN: 标尺上的一点误差，就可能影响最终的估计。
senses.why: An error in the scale strikes the final number and leaves its mark there.
senses.whyCN: 标尺的误差撞在最终数字上，并在那里留下痕迹。

senses.title: Strike a structure physically
senses.definition: literally to hit a body with force
senses.definitionCN: 字面地以力量撞击一个物体
senses.example: A falling branch can have an impact on the roof during a storm.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风中落下的树枝可能撞击屋顶。
senses.why: This is the oldest layer: the noun first named a collision before it named an influence.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的一层：名词先指「碰撞」，后来才指「影响」。

senses.title: Damage something
senses.definition: to cause harm or loss to a system or a place
senses.definitionCN: 对某个系统或地方造成伤害或损失
senses.example: The spill may have an impact on the shellfish beds.
senses.exampleCN: 这次泄漏可能对贝类养殖区造成损害。
senses.why: A spill strikes a shellfish bed where living things cannot move away.
senses.whyCN: 泄漏撞在贝类养殖区，那里的生物无处避开。

senses.title: Be limited or large in degree
senses.definition: to affect something only slightly or very greatly, with the degree made explicit
senses.definitionCN: 只轻微影响或极大影响，并明确点出程度
senses.example: The new rule should have an impact on only a few small firms.
senses.exampleCN: 新规则应只影响少数小公司。
senses.why: A dent can be shallow or deep; the phrase can say how deep the dent is.
senses.whyCN: 凹痕可深可浅；这个短语可以说出凹痕有多深。

intro.en: The phrase joins the native verb of holding with a noun borrowed from Latin, where it named something driven in by force. The modern sense of influence grew out of that physical collision in the twentieth century.
intro.cn: 这个短语把本族表示「持有」的动词，与借自拉丁语、本指「以力量打入之物」的名词结合。现代「影响」义是在二十世纪从那次物理碰撞里长出来的。

items.en: Pangere meant to fix, to drive in, to fasten, and it stands behind compact and pact as well.
items.cn: 这个词意为「固定、打入、系紧」，紧密的与契约诸词也由它而来。

items.en: In- 'into' plus pangere produced impingere, to drive something into, to strike against.
items.cn: 表示「进入」的前缀加「打入」，构成「把某物撞进去、撞击」的动词。

items.en: The participle named a thing struck against another, and English took it as the noun impact in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 分词指「被撞上之物」，英语在十七世纪把它取作名词「碰撞」。

items.en: The noun first meant a collision or a striking together, and it kept that physical sense for centuries.
items.cn: 这个名词最初指「碰撞、相撞」，这一物理义延续了几个世纪。

items.en: The figurative sense of a strong effect became dominant in the twentieth century and is often criticised as vague in academic writing. The exact first citation is uncertain.
items.cn: 表示「强烈作用」的比喻义在二十世纪占据主导，并常被批评为学术写作中含义模糊。最早书证年代不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin driving-in word and its derivatives; the second group holds other verbs and phrases of influence, including the plainer twin of this phrase.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁「打入」之词及其派生词；第二组是其他表示「影响」的动词与短语，其中包含本短语更朴素的对应说法。

entries.definition: The noun can stand alone as a subject or object, as in the impact was small; the phrase adds the affected party.
entries.definitionCN: 名词可单独作主语或宾语，如「影响很小」；短语则补出受影响的一方。

entries.definition: It describes something already affected or tightly wedged; it is not a substitute for the phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 形容已被影响或紧紧嵌住的东西，不能替代本短语。

entries.definition: A recent coinage for having a strong effect; many style guides prefer a plain alternative.
entries.definitionCN: 晚近造出的形容词，表示「有强烈作用」；许多体例指南更倾向朴素的替代说法。

entries.definition: It is used in medicine and geology for material wedged in place, not for social influence.
entries.definitionCN: 医学与地质学中指尖塞、压紧之物，不用于社会影响。

entries.definition: The standard neutral phrase for influence; it avoids the vagueness that critics find in the impact wording.
entries.definitionCN: 表示「影响」的中性标准短语，避开了批评者认为「冲击」说法含混的问题。

entries.definition: A general verb for shaping decisions or beliefs; it is less physical and less emphatic.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指影响决策或信念的动词，物理意味与强调意味都较弱。

entries.definition: It stresses giving form to a result rather than merely changing it.
entries.definitionCN: 强调给结果以形状，而不只是改变它。

entries.definition: A formal phrase for being relevant to a question; it does not necessarily imply a strong effect.
entries.definitionCN: 正式表示「与某问题相关」，不一定含「作用强烈」之意。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the swinging iron ball, the projected curve, the weather shift and the falling branch.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用摆动的铁球、投影曲线、气候变动与落下的树枝四个场景。

normal.en: An iron ball swings down and dents a thin plate, the rim of the dent spreading outward.
normal.cn: 铁球荡下，把薄板撞出一个凹痕，凹痕边缘向外散开。

normal.en: A curve thrown on the wall at an evaluation meeting.
normal.cn: 评估会上，一张曲线被投到墙上。

normal.en: A warmer spring, and birds arriving a week early.
normal.cn: 春天更暖，鸟早来了一周。

normal.en: One teacher who changes what a student wants to study.
normal.cn: 一位老师，改变了学生想学的专业。

normal.en: A branch falling on a roof during a storm.
normal.cn: 暴风中一根树枝落在屋顶上。

abstract.en: Impact is a dent left by something else, never a property of the thing alone.
abstract.cn: 影响是别的东西留下的凹痕，从不是某物自身的属性。

abstract.en: The word first meant collision, and every figurative use still carries a trace of force.
abstract.cn: 这个词先指碰撞，每个比喻用法都还带着一点力。

abstract.en: An effect named as impact invites the question: how large, on whom, for how long?
abstract.cn: 用「冲击」来命名的作用，会招来三个问题：多大、对谁、多久。

examples.en: The new tariff may have an impact on the price of imported steel.
examples.cn: 新关税可能影响进口钢材的价格。

examples.en: A long drought can have an impact on the following year's seed crop.
examples.cn: 长期干旱可能影响下一年的种子收成。

examples.en: The report should state how large an impact the policy can have on rural incomes.
examples.cn: 报告应说明该政策能对农村收入产生多大影响。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「哈夫 恩 因帕克特 昂」：把「打入」记成铁球撞薄板，板上留下凹痕——凹痕就是影响

root: 前半为本族动词，意为「持有、具有」；后半名词出自拉丁语，由表示「进入」的前缀加表示「打入、固定」的动词构成，本义是「撞击、碰撞」，现代「影响」义为晚近引申。短语后接介词引出受影响的一方。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one dent: an outcome, a workplace, a species, a belief, an audience, an estimate, a roof, a shellfish bed, and a stated degree.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项都跟着同一处凹痕：结果、工作场所、物种、信念、受众、估计、屋顶、贝类养殖区与明确的程度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an iron ball swinging down onto a thin plate, a dent forming, its rim spreading outward.
core.cn: 核心意象：铁球荡下撞上薄板，板上出现凹痕，凹痕的边缘向外散开。

branches.en: THE MEASURED EFFECT: a rate change, an office of clerks, a rule touching few firms, all with a size to state.
branches.cn: 可测的作用：利率变动、职员人数、只触及少数公司的规则，都有大小可说。

branches.en: THE LIVING AND THE FRAGILE: migrating birds and shellfish beds take the blow.

branches.en: THE MIND MOVED: a teacher shapes a choice, a broadcast shapes a reading.
branches.cn: 被推动的心：老师塑造选择，播报塑造解读。

branches.en: THE DISTORTED NUMBER: an error in the scale bends the final estimate.
branches.cn: 被扭偏的数字：标尺误差使最终估计走形。

branches.cn: 物理的一击：暴风中树枝撞上屋顶。

latinIntro.en: Latin pangere and impingere supplied the noun impactus, which English borrowed directly in the seventeenth century.

senses.title: Land that bears no crops
senses.definition: producing little or no vegetation
senses.definitionCN: 几乎不生草木的
senses.example: Sheep nibbled at barren hillsides.
senses.exampleCN: 羊群啃食着荒瘠的山坡。
senses.why: The root meant bare, sterile: nothing clings to it.
senses.whyCN: 词根义为「光秃、不生」：什么也长不住。

senses.title: Unable to bear young
senses.definition: of women or animals, not producing offspring
senses.definitionCN: 指妇女或动物不能生育
senses.example: In old tales, a barren queen was a tragedy.
senses.exampleCN: 在古老传说里，无嗣的王后是一场悲剧。
senses.why: What is true of fields is said of wombs.
senses.whyCN: 田地之语移用于子嗣。

senses.title: Plants that bear no fruit
senses.definition: of plants, not producing fruit or seed
senses.definitionCN: 指植物不结果实或种子
senses.example: The orchard's barren trees were cut down.
senses.exampleCN: 果园里不结果的树被砍掉了。
senses.why: The sterile field extends to the single tree.
senses.whyCN: 瘠土之义延及单株之树。

senses.title: Empty of interest or content
senses.definition: dull, without interest or value
senses.definitionCN: 缺乏趣味或价值
senses.example: The novel is stylish but barren of ideas.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说时髦却思想贫乏。
senses.why: Nothing grows in a mind so stripped.
senses.whyCN: 被剥光的心田同样寸草不生。

senses.title: Without results
senses.definition: producing no useful result
senses.definitionCN: 不产生任何有用结果
senses.example: Their search proved barren.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的搜寻一无所获。
senses.why: Effort spent on sterile ground feeds no one.
senses.whyCN: 瘠土上的汗水养不活人。

senses.title: Stripped or bare appearance
senses.definition: bare, as a landscape without shelter or ornament
senses.definitionCN: 指景色光秃、无遮无饰
senses.example: Barren rocks ran down to the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 光秃的岩石直延伸入海。
senses.why: The visual bareness is the root's first face.
senses.whyCN: 视觉上的光秃正是词根的第一面孔。

senses.title: The noun: a stretch of barren land
senses.definition: barrens, an area of unproductive land
senses.definitionCN: 指荒瘠地带，常用复数 barrens
senses.example: Caribou cross the barrens each autumn.
senses.exampleCN: 驯鹿每年秋天穿越荒原。
senses.why: The adjective hardened into a place name.
senses.whyCN: 形容词固化成地名。

senses.title: Barren of
senses.definition: completely lacking something
senses.definitionCN: 全然缺乏某物
senses.example: The report is barren of any evidence.
senses.exampleCN: 报告没有任何证据。
senses.why: Of-names what the sterile ground does not hold.
senses.whyCN: of 点名瘠土所无之物。

intro.en: Barren comes from Old French barain, of a woman or beast, barren, of uncertain deeper origin; some link it to a Vulgar Latin form from a Celtic or Germanic root meaning bare.
intro.cn: barren 出自古法语 barain「（女子或牲畜）不孕的」，更深来源不确定；一说与「光秃」义的通俗拉丁或凯尔特、日耳曼词根有关。

items.en: Etymologists mark the deeper root as unknown.
items.cn: 词源学家标记其更深词根不明。

items.en: A proposed Vulgar Latin brachus, sterile, has been suggested.
items.cn: 一说经通俗拉丁语 brachus「不生的」。

items.en: barain described sterile women, animals, and land.
items.cn: 古法语 barain 形容不孕者与瘠地。

items.en: English took the word with both the womb and the field senses.
items.cn: 英语借入时兼有子嗣与田地二义。

items.en: The figurative senses of emptiness and futility now dominate writing.
items.cn: 如今「空洞、徒劳」的比喻义主导书面语。

abstract.en: Hear the wind pass over nothing.

examples.en: Years of drought left the plateau barren.
examples.cn: 连年干旱使高原沦为荒地。

examples.en: The experiments proved barren of breakthroughs.

examples.en: A barren winter tree scratched at the window.

branches.en: Bare land and bare view are the visible start.
branches.cn: 瘠土与光秃是可见的起点。

definition_en: relating to the production of offspring, or to the copying and playback of something already made
core_image: 解剖图上的鱼腹被轻轻揭开，一排细小的卵粒沿腹腔排成两列，等着被排出体外。
scene: 生物课上，老师指着鱼腹解剖图里成串的卵粒说，这些器官的唯一任务是保证后代产生。 These organs serve a reproductive function: they exist to produce the next generation.
sceneCN: 这里 reproductive 是“与生殖有关的”（第 1 个义项）；句意：这些器官专门服务于繁殖。

senses.title: To do with breeding
senses.titleCN: 生殖的：与产生后代有关
senses.definition: relating to the biological production of offspring
senses.definitionCN: 与生物产生后代有关的
senses.example: Warmer water shortens the reproductive season of many fish.
senses.exampleCN: 水温升高会缩短许多鱼类的生殖季。
senses.why: The adjective adds -ive to reproduce: what is reproductive is what tends to bring the kind forth again.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词在 reproduce 后加 -ive：凡是倾向于把同类再次产出的，就是 reproductive。

senses.title: The organs involved
senses.titleCN: 生殖系统的：身体里负责繁殖的器官
senses.definition: belonging to the organs and structures used in breeding
senses.definitionCN: 属于繁殖所用的器官与结构
senses.example: The drug can damage the reproductive organs of young fish.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药物会损害幼鱼的生殖器官。
senses.why: An organ is called reproductive by its function, not its tissue; the adjective sorts body parts by the job they serve.
senses.whyCN: 器官因功能而非组织类型被称为 reproductive；这个形容词按所司之职给身体部位分类。

senses.title: Capable of breeding
senses.titleCN: 有繁殖能力的：到了能生育的阶段
senses.definition: mature enough or healthy enough to produce young
senses.definitionCN: 成熟或健康到足以产生后代
senses.example: Only reproductive adults carry the bright breeding plumage.
senses.exampleCN: 只有具备繁殖能力的成鸟才长有鲜艳的婚羽。
senses.why: Here the adjective marks a stage of life: an individual becomes reproductive when its body can complete the cycle.
senses.whyCN: 这里标记的是生命阶段：当身体能完成整个周期时，个体才成为有繁殖能力的。

senses.title: To do with copying
senses.titleCN: 复制的：与翻制、翻印有关
senses.definition: relating to the mechanical copying of images, documents, or recordings
senses.definitionCN: 与图像、文件或录音的机械复制有关的
senses.example: The library's reproductive services are limited to out-of-copyright works.
senses.exampleCN: 图书馆的复制服务只限版权过期的作品。
senses.why: The same suffix covers making a second object; what is reproductive here serves duplication rather than breeding.
senses.whyCN: 同一后缀也覆盖“制造第二个物件”；这里服务于复制，而不是生育。

senses.title: Judged by fidelity
senses.titleCN: 还原的：以保真度衡量的
senses.definition: describing equipment or processes measured by how faithfully they recreate sound or colour
senses.definitionCN: 描述以还原声音或色彩的忠实度来衡量的设备或过程
senses.example: Reproductive accuracy matters more than loudness in a concert hall.
senses.exampleCN: 在音乐厅里，还原的准确比音量更重要。
senses.why: Fidelity is the standard by which a copy is judged; the adjective names whatever is assessed on that standard.
senses.whyCN: 保真度是评判复制品的标准；这个形容词命名的是按该标准受评判的对象。

senses.title: Work that renews workers
senses.titleCN: 再生产性的：维持劳动力所需的劳动
senses.definition: in economics and social theory, describing unpaid work that sustains and renews people able to work
senses.definitionCN: 经济学与社会理论中，描述维持并更新劳动人口的无偿劳动
senses.example: Cooking and caregiving are forms of reproductive labour.
senses.exampleCN: 做饭与照护属于再生产劳动。
senses.why: Such work does not make goods; it remakes the worker, so the label borrows the biological image of renewing a kind.
senses.whyCN: 这类劳动不制造商品，而是重新造出劳动者，因此这个标签借用了“更新同类”的生物学意象。

senses.title: Health and rights around birth
senses.titleCN: 生殖健康与生育权：围绕生育的公共议题
senses.definition: used in phrases about access to fertility care, contraception, and related rights
senses.definitionCN: 用于指生育照护、避孕及相关权利的短语中
senses.example: Reproductive health services were expanded in rural clinics.
senses.exampleCN: 农村诊所的生殖健康服务得到扩展。
senses.why: The adjective becomes a policy label: it gathers medical, legal, and social questions under the single fact of reproduction.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词变成了政策标签：它把医学、法律与社会问题都收拢到“繁殖”这一事实之下。

senses.title: Repeatable by design
senses.titleCN: 可复现的：能被别人照样做一遍
senses.definition: describing a method or result that another person can repeat exactly
senses.definitionCN: 描述他人能够完全照样重复的方法或结果
senses.example: The protocol was designed to be reproductive across laboratories.
senses.exampleCN: 该实验规程被设计成可在各实验室复现。
senses.why: Science calls a study reproductive when its outcome returns in other hands; repeatability is treated as the mark of a real effect.
senses.whyCN: 当结果在别人手里重现时，科学界就说这项研究可复现；可重复性被视为真实效应的标志。

intro.en: Reproductive is reproduce plus -ive. Reproduce is re- plus produce, from Latin producere, to lead forth, built on ducere, to lead.
intro.cn: reproductive 由 reproduce 加 -ive 构成。reproduce 是 re- 加 produce，后者出自拉丁语 producere“引出”，其词基为 ducere“引导”。

items.en: Ducere meant to lead or draw along; the image is of something being drawn out of a source.
items.cn: ducere 意为“引导、牵引”；其形象是把某物从源头拉出来。

items.en: Producere put pro-, forward, before ducere, giving the sense of bringing something out into view or into existence.
items.cn: producere 把 pro-“向前”放在 ducere 前，表示把某物带到眼前或带入存在。

items.en: The English verb kept the outward sense of yielding goods, crops, or effects.
items.cn: 英语动词保留了“产出货物、作物或效果”这一向外生长的含义。

items.en: Adding re- makes the yielding a second one: a species yields its own kind again, or a workshop yields a copy.
items.cn: 加上 re- 就使产出成为第二次产出：物种再次产出同类，或作坊产出复制品。

items.en: The suffix -ivus formed adjectives meaning tending towards or serving for an action; it points to the function rather than the act.
items.cn: 后缀 -ivus 构成表示“倾向于、用于某动作”的形容词；它指向功能而非动作本身。

items.en: Reproductive first described organs and processes of breeding, and was later extended to copying and to repeatable methods.
items.cn: reproductive 最初描述繁殖的器官与过程，后来扩展到复制以及可重复的方法。

note.en: The first group shares the produce root with different endings; the second compares words about breeding, copying, and repeatability.
note.cn: 第一组共享 produce 词根而词尾不同；第二组比较关于繁殖、复制与可重复性的词。

entries.definition: to breed or copy. It is the action that the adjective describes.
entries.definitionCN: 繁殖或复制；是形容词所描述的那个动作。

entries.definition: the process or result of producing again. It names the event or the copy.
entries.definitionCN: 再次产出的过程或结果；命名的是事件或复制品。

entries.definition: yielding a good amount of results. It lacks re- and so says nothing about a second round.
entries.definitionCN: 产出效果多的；没有 re-，因此不涉及第二轮。

entries.definition: having the power to produce or originate new things, especially in language or art.
entries.definitionCN: 具有产生或创造新事物的能力，尤用于语言或艺术。

entries.definition: relating to the controlled mating of animals. It stresses human management of reproduction.
entries.definitionCN: 与动物受控交配有关；强调人对繁殖的管理。

entries.definition: tending to make an exact second copy. It stresses sameness rather than biological renewal.
entries.definitionCN: 倾向于做出完全相同的第二份；强调同一性而非生命更新。

entries.definition: able to be done or obtained again by the same or another person.
entries.definitionCN: 能够被同样的人或他人再次做出或得到的。

normalIntro.en: Real parts only: re-, produce, -ive. The suffix makes an adjective of function, so reproductive describes what serves the bringing forth again.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：re-、produce、-ive。该后缀构成表功能的形容词，因此 reproductive 描述的是服务于“再次产出”的事物。

normal.en: Re plus produce plus ive: the adjective of things that serve a second bringing forth.
normal.cn: re 加 produce 加 ive：服务于第二次产出的形容词。

normal.en: Reproductive organs exist for one job: making the next generation.
normal.cn: 生殖器官只为一件差事存在：造出下一代。

normal.en: A reproductive adult is one whose body can complete the cycle.
normal.cn: 有繁殖能力的成体，就是身体能跑完整个周期的个体。

normal.en: Unpaid cooking and caregiving is reproductive labour: it remakes the worker.
normal.cn: 无偿的做饭与照护是再生产劳动：它重新造出劳动者。

normal.en: A reproductive experiment is one that still works when someone else repeats it.
normal.cn: 可复现的实验，就是换个人重做仍然成立的实验。

abstract.en: Calling work reproductive quietly asks who is expected to renew the renewers.
abstract.cn: 把某种劳动称为“再生产”，其实是在问：谁又来更新那些更新者。

abstract.en: An organ is named by its function, so the body is read as a set of purposes.
abstract.cn: 器官按功能命名，身体因此被读成一组目的。

abstract.en: Repeatability is trust in science made procedural.
abstract.cn: 可重复性是科学信任被程序化后的样子。

examples.en: The reproductive cycle of the eel takes it from river to ocean and back.
examples.cn: 鳗鲡的生殖周期让它从河流到海洋，再返回河流。

examples.en: Reproductive health clinics reported a sharp rise in visits after the campaign.
examples.cn: 宣传活动之后，生殖健康诊所的就诊人数大幅上升。

examples.en: The team published a reproductive protocol so other labs could copy the result.
examples.cn: 团队公布了可复现的实验规程，让其他实验室能复制该结果。

dict_mnemonic.text: re（再）+ product（产品）+ ive——能再产生一次产品的，就是生殖的、复制的。

root: 由 reproduce（繁殖、复制）加 -ive（倾向于、用于……的）构成；reproduce 为 re-（再）加 produce（产出，源自拉丁语 producere“引出”，词基 ducere“引导”），本义为“用于再次产出同类的”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of reproductive, all circling one idea: what serves the return of the same form. The service may be breeding, an organ, a mature body, copying, fidelity, unpaid renewal work, health policy, or repeatable method.
sensesIntro.cn: reproductive 的八个义项都围绕一个观念：服务于同一形制的再次出现。这种服务可以是繁殖、器官、成熟个体、复制、保真、无偿的更新劳动、健康政策，或可重复的方法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fish dissection chart, two rows of eggs along the belly, every organ pointed at the next generation.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张鱼类解剖图，腹腔两侧排着卵粒，每个器官都指向下一代。

branches.en: BODILY BREEDING: the process, the organs, and the mature state that makes it possible.
branches.cn: 身体层面的繁衍：过程、器官，以及使之可能的成熟状态。

branches.en: COPYING AND FIDELITY: mechanical reproduction and the measured faithfulness of the copy.
branches.cn: 复制与保真：机械复制，以及复制品被测量的忠实度。

branches.en: SOCIAL RENEWAL: unpaid work that remakes the people who work.
branches.cn: 社会性更新：重新造出劳动者本人的无偿劳动。

branches.en: PUBLIC POLICY: health, contraception, and rights gathered under one adjective.
branches.cn: 公共政策：健康、避孕与权利被收拢在同一个形容词下。

branches.en: METHOD: a study counts as reproductive when other hands can repeat it.
branches.cn: 方法：当别人的手能重复时，一项研究才算可复现。

intro.en: Reproductive joins re-, produce, and -ive. The same pieces also build reproduce, reproduction, and reproducible, each ending marking a different grammatical job.
intro.cn: reproductive 由 re-、produce 与 -ive 组合。同样的成分也构成 reproduce、reproduction 与 reproducible，各词尾标记不同的语法任务。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is ducere, extended in producere. The -ive ending comes from Latin -ivus, shared with a large family of English adjectives.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词基是 ducere，在 producere 中扩展。-ive 词尾出自拉丁语 -ivus，与英语中大批形容词共享。

items.meaning: to yield, make, or bring into being
items.example: The orchard produces pears even in poor soil.
items.exampleCN: 这片果园即使在贫瘠土壤里也产梨。

items.meaning: to breed or make a copy
items.example: The pattern reproduces itself in every generation of the fabric.
items.exampleCN: 这一图案在每一代织物上都会复制自身。

items.meaning: breeding, copying, or renewal of conditions
items.example: The lab keeps a reproduction of the original slide.
items.exampleCN: 实验室保存着原始玻片的复制品。

items.meaning: relating to breeding or to copying
items.example: Reproductive success depends on finding a mate in time.
items.exampleCN: 繁殖成功取决于及时找到配偶。

items.example: The image reproduced here is half the size of the original.
items.exampleCN: 此处复制的图像尺寸只有原件的一半。

items.meaning: in terms of breeding or copying
items.example: The two species are reproductively isolated by timing.
items.exampleCN: 这两个物种因繁殖时间不同而生殖隔离。

items.meaning: able to be repeated or copied
items.example: The experiment is reproducible with ordinary glassware.
items.exampleCN: 这个实验用普通玻璃器皿即可重复。

items.example: Poor reproducibility has damaged trust in the field.
items.exampleCN: 可重复性差已损害了该领域的信任。

items.meaning: not involved in breeding, as of worker bees
items.example: Non-reproductive workers defend the colony instead.
items.exampleCN: 不繁殖的工蜂转而保卫群体。

definition_zh: 几何的；几何图形的；按几何级数增长的；规整对称的
definition_en: relating to geometry or to shapes built from points, lines and surfaces, or increasing by a constant multiplying factor
core_image: 一把圆规与一把直尺压在六边形瓷砖的接缝上
scene: 这里指「几何的」。 The tiles form a geometrical pattern of hexagons that fit together without gaps.
sceneCN: 这里 geometrical 是「几何图形的」（第 2 个义项：由规则图形拼成）；句意：这些瓷砖构成一个由六边形拼成、无缝相接的几何图案。图中可辨识物件：六边形瓷砖、圆规、直尺、角度标记、网格线。

pos.zh: 几何的；几何图形的；按几何级数增长的；规整对称的（多作定语）

derivatives.zh: 几何学；几何形状；空间布置
几何的（较短变体）
在几何上；按几何方式
几何学家；（古）土地测量员
几何学家

senses.title: Of the science of geometry
senses.titleCN: 几何学的：属于这门学科
senses.definition: belonging to the branch of mathematics that deals with points, lines, angles and figures
senses.definitionCN: 属于研究点、线、角与图形的数学分支
senses.example: The proof uses purely geometrical reasoning, with no algebra.
senses.exampleCN: 这个证明只用纯几何推理，不含代数。
senses.why: geōmetria in Greek meant 'land measurement', built from gē 'earth' and metron 'measure'; -ical makes the relational adjective.
senses.whyCN: 希腊 geōmetria 意为“土地测量”，由 gē“大地”与 metron“测量”构成；-ical 构成关系形容词。

senses.title: Built from regular shapes
senses.titleCN: 几何图形的：由规则图形拼成
senses.definition: made of or resembling regular figures such as circles, triangles and polygons
senses.definitionCN: 由圆、三角形、多边形等规则图形构成或形似的
senses.example: The façade is covered in a geometrical grid of squares and circles.
senses.exampleCN: 立面覆满由方形与圆形组成的几何网格。
senses.why: When drawing replaces measuring land, the adjective comes to describe anything whose outline is a figure from the textbook.
senses.whyCN: 当绘图取代丈量土地后，这个形容词便用来描述任何轮廓取自教科书的图形之物。

senses.title: Multiplying by a fixed factor
senses.titleCN: 按几何级数增长的：倍数递增
senses.definition: increasing or decreasing by a constant ratio at each step, as in a geometrical progression
senses.definitionCN: 每一步按固定比例增减，如等比数列
senses.example: Bacteria in a flask grow in a geometrical progression, doubling every twenty minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 瓶中的细菌按几何级数增长，每二十分钟翻一番。
senses.why: Ancient mathematicians compared arithmetic growth, which adds a constant, with geometrical growth, which multiplies by a constant; the metaphor survives in the adjective.
senses.whyCN: 古代数学把每次加常数的算术增长与每次乘常数的几何增长相对照，这一比喻留存于该形容词中。

senses.title: Regular and precisely ordered
senses.titleCN: 规整对称的：精确而有秩序
senses.definition: having a regular, balanced and precisely ordered arrangement
senses.definitionCN: 具有规则、均衡且精确有序的排布
senses.example: The garden's geometrical layout is best seen from the air.
senses.exampleCN: 这座园林的规整布局从空中看最清楚。
senses.why: Figures drawn with compass and rule look exact, so the adjective transfers from the drawing to anything that shares its regularity.
senses.whyCN: 用圆规与直尺画出的图形看上去精确，因此这个形容词从图纸转移到任何具有同样规则性的事物。

senses.title: Proved by construction
senses.titleCN: 几何证明的：靠作图与推理
senses.definition: in mathematics, handled by construction and logical deduction from axioms rather than by algebra
senses.definitionCN: 数学中指通过作图与由公理出发的逻辑演绎来处理，而非用代数
senses.example: The ancients solved the problem by a geometrical construction with compass and rule.
senses.exampleCN: 古代人用圆规与直尺的几何作图解决了这个问题。
senses.why: Classical geometry allowed only compass and straightedge; the adjective marks that restricted, constructive style of proof.
senses.whyCN: 古典几何只允许圆规与直尺；这个形容词标记的正是这种受限的作图式证明风格。

senses.title: Of spatial relations
senses.titleCN: 空间关系的：位置与角度
senses.definition: relating to the spatial relations of position, distance and angle
senses.definitionCN: 关于位置、距离与角度等空间关系的
senses.example: The software checks the geometrical fit of every joint before cutting.
senses.exampleCN: 软件在下料前检查每个接头的几何配合。
senses.why: Geometry is the mathematics of space, so the adjective names spatial fit even when no textbook figure is drawn.
senses.whyCN: 几何学是关于空间的数学，因此即使没有画出教科书图形，这个形容词也可指空间上的配合。

senses.title: Reduced to basic shapes in art
senses.titleCN: 几何抽象的：艺术中简化为基本形
senses.definition: in art, describing work built from basic shapes rather than from observed forms
senses.definitionCN: 艺术中指以基本形而非观察所得形态来构建作品
senses.example: The movement preferred geometrical abstraction to any trace of landscape.
senses.exampleCN: 这一流派偏爱几何抽象，而不是任何风景痕迹。
senses.why: Modern painters removed representational detail until only squares and circles remained, and critics named the result with this adjective.
senses.whyCN: 现代画家删去再现性细节，直到只剩方块与圆圈，评论者便用这个形容词命名结果。

senses.title: Of land survey
senses.titleCN: 土地测量的：历史上的丈量术
senses.definition: in historical use, relating to the measuring and dividing of land
senses.definitionCN: 历史用法中指对土地进行丈量与划分
senses.example: The old geometrical method divided the field into equal strips.
senses.exampleCN: 旧的测量方法把这块田划分成等宽的条带。
senses.why: The original geōmetria was literally field measurement, and the adjective preserves that earliest practical meaning.
senses.whyCN: 最初的 geōmetria 字面就是田地丈量，这个形容词保留了那一最早的实用含义。

intro.en: Geometrical comes from Greek geōmetria 'land measurement', gē 'earth' plus metron 'measure', with the adjective ending -ical. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: geometrical 出自希腊 geōmetria“土地测量”，由 gē“大地”加 metron“测量”构成，再加形容词词尾 -ical。年代为约数。

items.en: geōmetria joined gē 'earth' with metron 'measure'. The practice came first: Egyptian and Greek surveyors re-divided farmland after the Nile floods each year.
items.cn: geōmetria 把 gē“大地”与 metron“测量”结合。实践在先：埃及与希腊的测量员每年尼罗河泛滥后重新划分农田。

items.en: Latin borrowed the word as geometria, and Old French formed geometrie. English geometry appears in the 14th century.
items.cn: 拉丁语借作 geometria，古法语构成 geometrie。英语 geometry 于 14 世纪出现。

items.en: Between the 6th century BC and Euclid's Elements (around 300 BC), measurement became deductive proof, and the subject's name stayed even after the fields were left behind.
items.cn: 从公元前 6 世纪到欧几里得《几何原本》（约公元前 300 年），丈量变成演绎证明，而学科名称在离开田地之后仍然保留。

items.en: -ical comes from Latin -icalis, from Greek -ikos. English already had geometric from Latin geometricus; geometrical arose as the longer variant.
items.cn: -ical 来自拉丁 -icalis，后者出自希腊 -ikos。英语已有来自拉丁 geometricus 的 geometric，geometrical 是较长的变体。

items.en: Geometrical progression kept the multiplier sense, geometrical optics and geometrical abstraction extended the shape sense into physics and art.
items.cn: geometrical progression 保留了“倍数”义，geometrical optics 与 geometrical abstraction 则把“形状”义延伸到物理与艺术。

items.en: The date when geōmetria first shifted from surveying to proof is inferred from fragmentary sources, and the deeper origin of metron is reconstructed rather than recorded.
items.cn: geōmetria 从丈量转为证明的确切时间只能从零散材料推断；metron 的更深来源属重构而非有记录。

note.en: The first group contains shortened forms and word relatives that are often confused; the second contains adjectives for related mathematical or spatial ideas.
note.cn: 第一组易混的是截短形式与同族词；第二组是相关数学或空间概念的形容词。

entries.definition: The shorter adjective, overwhelmingly preferred in technical terms such as geometric mean and geometric series. The difference is convention, not sense.
entries.definitionCN: 较短形容词，在 geometric mean、geometric series 等术语中占绝对优势；差别在惯例而非词义。

entries.definition: The discipline or the shape and arrangement of a space. It cannot modify a noun as the adjective does.
entries.definitionCN: 指学科，或某空间中的形状与布置；不能像形容词那样修饰名词。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning 'in geometric terms' or 'by geometric growth'. It modifies verbs and adjectives.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，意为“从几何上”或“按几何方式增长”，修饰动词与形容词。

entries.definition: A specialist in places and distribution. It shares geo- but its second element means 'write', not 'measure'.
entries.definitionCN: 研究地点与分布的专家；共用 geo-，但第二构件意为“书写”而非“测量”。

entries.definition: Having matched parts on opposite sides; it shares metron but stresses balance rather than measurable shape.
entries.definitionCN: 两侧部件相互对应；同含 metron，但强调均衡而非可测量的形状。

entries.definition: Relating to space and position without implying measurement or proof.
entries.definitionCN: 关于空间与位置，但不含测量或证明之意。

entries.definition: Having angles or sharp corners; more specific than geometrical, which covers all regular figures.
entries.definitionCN: 有角或尖角的；比覆盖一切规则图形的 geometrical 更具体。

entries.definition: Increasing together at a constant ratio; it names the relationship, while geometrical progression names the pattern of steps.
entries.definitionCN: 按固定比例一同增减；它命名关系，而几何级数命名的是逐级模式。

entries.definition: Evenly arranged or shaped; it describes the impression of order that a geometrical figure produces.
entries.definitionCN: 排布或形状均匀；描述几何图形给人的秩序感。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词。

normal.en: geo- 'earth' + metron 'measure' + -ical: measurement of the earth, then the mathematics of shape.
normal.cn: geo-“大地”+ metron“测量”+ -ical：丈量土地，后指关于形状的数学。

normal.en: geometrical progression is the fixed-ratio sense; geometrical pattern is the shape sense.
normal.cn: geometrical progression 是固定比例义；geometrical pattern 是形状义。

normal.en: The family is geometry, geometer, geometric, geometrical, geometrically, geometrician.
normal.cn: 同族词是 geometry、geometer、geometric、geometrical、geometrically、geometrician。

normal.en: Compass and straightedge are the classical tools, which is why sense 5 means proof by construction.
normal.cn: 圆规与直尺是古典工具，这正是第 5 个义项意为“作图证明”的原因。

normal.en: geology reads layers, geometry measures shapes: -logy versus metron.
normal.cn: geology 读岩层，geometry 量形状：-logy 对 metron。

abstract.en: Picture a tiled floor where every hexagon touches six others exactly.
abstract.cn: 想象一片地砖，每个六边形恰好与六个相邻者相接。

abstract.en: Picture one bacterium becoming two, two becoming four, the count doubling faster than the eye can follow.
abstract.cn: 想象一个细菌变两个、两个变四个，数目翻倍快到眼睛跟不上。

abstract.en: Picture an artist erasing a landscape until only a square and a circle remain.
abstract.cn: 想象一位画家不断擦去风景，直到只剩一个方块和一个圆。

examples.en: The hall's ceiling is a geometrical arrangement of intersecting vaults.
examples.cn: 大厅的天花板是由交叉拱顶构成的几何排布。

examples.en: In a geometrical progression, each term is the previous one multiplied by the same number.
examples.cn: 在几何级数中，每一项都是前一项乘同一个数。

examples.en: The artist turned to geometrical abstraction after abandoning portraits.
examples.cn: 这位艺术家在放弃肖像之后转向几何抽象。

dict_mnemonic.text: “地（geo）上有米（metr）尺”——量地用的尺，量出形状 → geometrical 几何的、规整的

root: 希腊 gē“大地”+ metron“测量”→ geōmetria“土地丈量”；拉丁 geometria + 英语 -ical（关系形容词）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses start from measuring land, pass through the drawn figure, and end in ratios, order, proof, spatial fit, abstract art and survey.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从丈量土地开始，经过画出的图形，最终落在比例、秩序、证明、空间配合、抽象艺术与测量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: compass and rule pressed onto a floor of touching hexagons.
core.cn: 核心意象：圆规与直尺压在一片彼此相接的六边形地面上。

branches.en: MEASUREMENT: the science and its oldest field practice are the same root seen in classroom and field.
branches.cn: 测量：这门学科与它最古老的田间实践，是同一词根在课堂与田野的两种样子。

branches.en: THE DRAWN SHAPE: regular figures, visible order and abstract art all rest on the primacy of the outline.
branches.cn: 画出的形：规则图形、可见秩序与抽象艺术都以轮廓为先。

branches.en: RATIO: multiplying by a fixed factor is the numerical twin of drawing to scale.
branches.cn: 比例：按固定倍数增长，是按比例作图的数值孪生。

branches.en: PROOF: compass and straightedge turn measurement into deduction.
branches.cn: 证明：圆规与直尺把测量变成演绎。

branches.en: SPATIAL FIT: geometry governs whether parts meet, clear or collide.
branches.cn: 空间配合：几何决定部件是相接、让开还是相撞。

intro.en: Geometrical splits into geo- 'earth', metr- 'measure' and -ical 'relating to'. The middle element also builds meter, symmetry and parameter.
intro.cn: geometrical 可拆为 geo-“大地”、metr-“测量”与 -ical“与……有关”。中间构件也构成 meter、symmetry、parameter。

latinIntro.en: Greek metron reached English through Latin in a wide family: metre, meter, symmetry, asymmetry, parameter, diameter and perimeter.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 metron 经拉丁语进入英语，形成宽泛词族：metre、meter、symmetry、asymmetry、parameter、diameter、perimeter。

items.meaning: relating to shape, measurement or fixed ratios
items.meaningCN: 与形状、度量或固定比例有关的
items.example: The mosaic follows a strict geometrical plan.
items.exampleCN: 这幅镶嵌画遵循严格的几何方案。

items.meaning: the mathematics of shape and space
items.meaningCN: 研究形状与空间的数学
items.example: Geometry tells you that the three angles sum to two right angles.
items.exampleCN: 几何学告诉你，这三个角之和等于两个直角。

items.example: The geometric mean of 4 and 9 is 6.
items.exampleCN: 4 与 9 的几何平均数是 6。

items.example: The two curves are geometrically similar.
items.exampleCN: 这两条曲线在几何上相似。

items.meaning: a geometry specialist; formerly a surveyor
items.meaningCN: 几何学家；古义为测量员
items.example: The ancient geometer measured the pyramid by its shadow.
items.exampleCN: 古代测量者用影子测量金字塔。

items.meaningCN: 各部分均衡的度量关系
items.example: The flower's symmetry is obvious from above.
items.exampleCN: 从上方看，这朵花的对称很明显。

items.meaning: a measured value that defines a system
items.meaningCN: 界定系统的测量值；参数
items.example: Each model has three adjustable parameters.
items.exampleCN: 每个模型有三个可调参数。

items.example: The pipe's diameter is forty centimetres.
items.exampleCN: 这根管子的直径是四十厘米。

definition_zh: 不确定；不确定性；疑虑；未知之事；测量的不确定度；风险与不可预测性
definition_en: the state of not being sure or not being known, and the range within which a measurement or forecast may vary
core_image: 一根指针停在两个刻度之间，微微抖动，既不落在这边也不落在那边
scene: 预报员看着云图，风向在半天之内改了三次，他只能说周末可能下雨也可能不下。 The uncertainty in the forecast kept the organizers from booking the outdoor stage.
sceneCN: 这里指预报结果无法确定的状态（第 3 个义项：不可预测、结果未定）；句意为预报中的不确定性让主办方无法预订露天舞台。场景图取象：指针停在两个刻度之间微微抖动。

pos.zh: 不确定；疑虑（不可数，指心理状态）
不确定之事；变数（可数，常用复数）
不确定度（测量学，指结果可能波动的范围）
（经济与管理）不可预测性、风险

derivatives.zh: 不确定的；不肯定的（加表示否定的前缀，指不处于已被判定的状态）
确定性；必然之事（去掉否定前缀后由「已被判定」的形容词加名词词尾构成）
确定的；某个的（由拉丁语「已判定」义而来，经由表示「筛定」的动词）
没有把握地；迟疑地（在形容词后加副词词尾）
确信；笃定（与 certain 同源的名词，多指主观上的确定感）

senses.title: Not knowing for sure
senses.definition: the state of not knowing whether something is true or what will happen
senses.definitionCN: 不知道某事是否为真、或将会如何的状态
senses.example: Her uncertainty about the answer was obvious.
senses.exampleCN: 她对答案没有把握，这一点很明显。
senses.why: The word negates a Latin adjective meaning settled, so it names the condition of not being settled.
senses.whyCN: 这个词否定了一个意为「已判定」的拉丁形容词，因此指未被定下来的状态。

senses.title: Something not yet decided
senses.definition: a matter whose outcome is not yet fixed, often counted in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 结果尚未确定的事情，常用复数计数
senses.example: The plan has too many uncertainties to price.
senses.exampleCN: 这个计划变数太多，无法定价。
senses.why: Uncertainty can be a thing as well as a mood, and business counts the things rather than the mood.
senses.whyCN: 不确定性既能是心情，也能是事情，商界数的是事情而非心情。

senses.title: What cannot be predicted
senses.definition: the part of a situation that cannot be forecast, as in weather or markets
senses.definitionCN: 局面中无法预报的部分，如天气或市场中的情形
senses.example: The uncertainty in the forecast kept the organizers from booking the outdoor stage.
senses.exampleCN: 预报中的不确定性让主办方无法预订露天舞台。
senses.why: Forecasting separates what is known from what remains open, and the open part takes this name.
senses.whyCN: 预报把已知与仍未定的部分分开，仍未定的那部分就用这个名字。

senses.title: The spread of a measurement
senses.definition: the range within which the true value of a measurement is expected to lie
senses.definitionCN: 测量的真值预期落在其中的范围
senses.example: The result was reported with an uncertainty of two per cent.
senses.exampleCN: 结果报告时附有百分之二的不确定度。
senses.why: Metrology refuses to give a bare number; every figure comes with the width of its doubt.
senses.whyCN: 计量学不肯给出光秃秃的数字，每个数都带着它那份怀疑的宽度。

senses.title: The quantum limit
senses.definition: the limit on how precisely certain paired properties of a particle can be known at once
senses.definitionCN: 粒子的某些成对属性无法同时被测得足够精确的限度
senses.example: The uncertainty principle is about knowledge, not about laboratory clumsiness.
senses.exampleCN: 不确定性原理讲的是知识限度，而不是实验室笨手笨脚。
senses.why: Physics found a doubt built into nature itself, and borrowed the everyday word for it.
senses.whyCN: 物理学发现怀疑被造进了自然本身，于是借用了日常的词来称它。

senses.title: Economic unpredictability
senses.definition: unpredictability in prices, demand or policy that makes planning difficult
senses.definitionCN: 价格、需求或政策上的不可预测，使规划变得困难
senses.example: Uncertainty over tariffs froze new investment.
senses.exampleCN: 关税上的不确定让新投资停滞。
senses.why: Firms do not react to bad news so much as to not knowing, which is why the word dominates economics.
senses.whyCN: 企业反应的与其说是坏消息，不如说是「不知道」，所以这个词在经济领域举足轻重。

senses.title: Hesitation in a person
senses.definition: a feeling of doubt that makes a person hesitate or speak cautiously
senses.definitionCN: 使人迟疑或说话谨慎的怀疑感
senses.example: He answered with a slight uncertainty in his voice.
senses.exampleCN: 他回答时声音里带着一点迟疑。
senses.why: The inner sense is the oldest: an unsettled judgement shows in the voice before it shows in the data.
senses.whyCN: 内心的义项最古老：未定的判断先露在声音里，然后才露在数据里。

senses.title: Risk that cannot be counted
senses.definition: a situation whose probabilities are unknown, distinguished from risk in which odds can be assigned
senses.definitionCN: 概率未知的处境，与可以给出赔率的「风险」相区别
senses.example: Decision theory separates uncertainty from measurable risk.
senses.exampleCN: 决策理论把不确定性与可计量的风险分开。
senses.why: If the odds are known it is risk; if they are not, it is uncertainty, and the distinction matters to insurers.
senses.whyCN: 赔率已知的是风险，未知的是不确定性，这一区分对保险业至关重要。

senses.title: The open future
senses.definition: the general condition of the future being undecided, a theme in philosophy and literature
senses.definitionCN: 未来尚未定局的一般状况，是哲学与文学的常见主题
senses.example: The novel turns uncertainty into a kind of freedom.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说把不确定变成了一种自由。
senses.why: If the future were closed, choice would be pointless; the word can name that openness rather than a lack.
senses.whyCN: 若未来已经闭合，选择便无意义；这个词也能指那种敞开，而不只是一种缺失。

intro.en: Uncertainty is the negative of certainty, from Latin certus 'settled', itself from cernere 'to sift, to decide'. The root history is generally accepted; only the exact date of the English noun is uncertain.
intro.cn: uncertainty 是 certainty 的否定形式，certainty 出自拉丁语 certus「已定的」，而 certus 又出自 cernere「筛、判定」。词根历史一般认为可靠，只有这个英语名词的确切年代不确定。

items.en: Cernere meant to sift or to separate, and from sifting came the sense of deciding a matter.
items.cn: cernere 意为筛、分开，从筛选中引出判定一件事的意思。

items.en: Certus meant settled or decided, said of a thing no longer in doubt.
items.cn: certus 意为已定、已决，用于不再有疑问之事。

items.en: Latin added the negative prefix to make incertus, not settled, the direct ancestor of uncertain.
items.cn: 拉丁语加上否定前缀构成 incertus「未定的」，正是 uncertain 的直接祖先。

items.en: Old French uncertain and the noun forme carried the word into English in the Middle Ages.
items.cn: 古法语的形式把这个词与名词形态在中世纪带入英语。

items.en: In the nineteenth and twentieth centuries the word was given a numeric sense, the band around a measured value.
items.cn: 十九与二十世纪，这个词获得数量含义，指测量值周围的那一条带。

items.en: Quantum theory and modern finance both made uncertainty a technical quantity, one in nature and one in markets.
items.cn: 量子理论与现代金融都把不确定性做成了技术量，一个在自然里，一个在市场里。

note.en: The first group shares the settled root or looks similar; the second group names neighbouring states that are often folded into uncertainty.
note.cn: 第一组或共享「已定」词根，或字形相近；第二组是常被并入「不确定性」的邻近状态。

entries.definition: The adjective: not sure, not settled.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词：不确定的、未定的。

entries.definition: The positive noun: the state of being settled.
entries.definitionCN: 肯定形式的名词：已被确定的状态。

entries.definition: A feeling of complete sureness, usually subjective.
entries.definitionCN: 完全的确定感，通常指主观上的。

entries.definition: To find out for certain; it shares cernere but not the negative prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 查明、确定；共享「筛定」词根，不含否定前缀。

entries.definition: Strange in a way that unsettles; it looks like the same negative but comes from ken, knowledge.
entries.definitionCN: 怪得令人不安；看似同一否定前缀，其实出自表示「知晓」的词。

entries.definition: A feeling of not being convinced, the personal side of uncertainty.
entries.definitionCN: 未被说服的感觉，是不确定性在个人身上的那一面。

entries.definition: Having more than one possible meaning, a property of statements rather than of the future.
entries.definitionCN: 存在不止一种可能含义，是陈述的属性而非未来的属性。

entries.definition: Exposure to a loss whose probability can be estimated.
entries.definitionCN: 暴露于损失之中，而其概率可以估算。

entries.definition: The tendency of a quantity to change, which produces uncertainty in measurement.
entries.definitionCN: 数量容易变动的倾向，正是它造成测量上的不确定。

entries.definition: The rate at which prices swing, a market measure of uncertainty.
entries.definitionCN: 价格摆动的幅度，是市场对不确定性的度量。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real sifting root, the real family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的「筛定」词根、真实同族词与真实固定搭配。

normal.en: Certain comes from a Latin verb meaning to sift, so certainty is what survives the sieve and uncertainty is what does not.
normal.cn: certain 出自意为「筛」的拉丁动词，确定性是筛后留下之物，不确定性是没留下的。

normal.en: The family pairs neatly: certain and certainty against uncertain and uncertainty.
normal.cn: 同族词成对出现：确定的、确定性，对不确定的、不确定性。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: measurement uncertainty, economic uncertainty, the uncertainty principle.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出用法：测量不确定度、经济不确定性、不确定性原理。

normal.en: In decision theory risk has countable odds, uncertainty does not.
normal.cn: 在决策理论里，风险有可数的赔率，不确定性没有。

normal.en: The plural uncertainties names concrete open questions, not a mood.
normal.cn: 复数形式指一件件还没定的事，而不是一种心情。

abstract.en: Uncertainty is the space in which a decision is still a decision.
abstract.cn: 不确定性是那块空间，决定在其中还算得上决定。

abstract.en: A number without an uncertainty is a claim pretending to be a fact.
abstract.cn: 没有不确定度的数字，是假装成事实的主张。

abstract.en: Uncertainty is not the enemy of knowledge; it is the shape knowledge takes at its edges.
abstract.cn: 不确定性不是知识的敌人，而是知识在边缘处呈现的形状。

examples.en: Uncertainty about the funding delayed the whole project.
examples.cn: 资金上的不确定拖住了整个项目。

examples.en: Every measurement carries an uncertainty that must be stated.
examples.cn: 每次测量都带有必须说明的不确定度。

examples.en: She learned to work despite the uncertainty of the outcome.
examples.cn: 她学会了在结果未定之时照样做事。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「安色滕提」——心里那根针迟迟不落定：不确定

root: certainty 的否定形式；certain 出自拉丁语 certus「已定」← cernere「筛、判定」，加否定前缀构成 incertus「未定」，经古法语进入英语。二十世纪起在测量学、量子物理与金融中获得技术含义。名词进入英语的确切年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses move from a private doubt to a public quantity: not knowing, an open question, an unpredictable part, the spread of a measurement, the quantum limit, economic unpredictability, personal hesitation, uncountable risk, and the openness of the future.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从私人的疑虑走到公共的量：拿不准、尚未定的事、无法预测的部分、测量的不确定度、量子限度、经济上的不可预测、个人的迟疑、无法计数的风险，以及未来的敞开。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a needle resting between two marks and trembling, belonging to neither.
core.cn: 核心意象：指针停在两个刻度之间微微抖动，哪一边都不属于。

branches.en: THE UNSETTLED MIND: a judgement not yet made, showing as hesitation in a voice.
branches.cn: 未定的心：尚未作出的判断，先从声音里的迟疑露出来。

branches.en: THE OPEN QUESTION: a matter whose outcome is still unfixed and can be counted.
branches.cn: 未决的问题：结果尚未确定、还可以数出来的一件事。

branches.en: THE UNFORECASTABLE: weather that may or may not hold, tariffs that may or may not change.
branches.cn: 无法预报之物：可能下也可能不下的雨，可能改也可能不改的关税。

branches.en: THE WIDTH OF A NUMBER: the band around a measured value, and the quantum limit on knowing two things at once.
branches.cn: 数字的宽度：测量值周围那一条带，以及同时知道两件事的量子限度。

branches.en: THE OPEN FUTURE: risk without countable odds, and the freedom of a future not yet closed.
branches.cn: 敞开的未来：没有可数赔率的风险，以及尚未闭合的未来的自由。

intro.en: Uncertainty negates a Latin adjective of settledness and turns it into an abstract noun.
intro.cn: uncertainty 否定一个表示「已定」的拉丁形容词，并把它变成抽象名词。

latinIntro.en: The base is certus from cernere, with the negative prefix and the noun ending added in turn.
latinIntro.cn: 基础是出自 cernere 的 certus，先后加上否定前缀与名词词尾。

items.meaning: the state of not being settled
items.example: The noun covers both a mood and a measured range.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词既指心情，也指测量出的范围。

items.example: It turns certain into uncertain.
items.exampleCN: 它把确定的变成不确定的。

items.example: It comes from the verb for sifting.
items.exampleCN: 它出自表示筛的动词。

items.meaning: to sift, to separate, to decide
items.example: The image is a sieve that leaves only what is sure.
items.exampleCN: 意象是一只筛子，只留下确定的东西。

items.example: It builds certainty and uncertainty.
items.exampleCN: 它构成确定性与不确定性。

items.example: The adjective also means a particular one.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词也有「某一个」的意思。

items.example: The pair makes a clean positive and negative.
items.exampleCN: 这一对构成干净的正与负。

items.example: It shares the root without the negative.
items.exampleCN: 它共享词根，却没有否定。

items.example: The noun names the feeling rather than the fact.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指感觉而非事实。

latinEntries.example: Latin incertus means not settled, doubtful.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 incertus 意为未定的、可疑的。

latinEntries.structure: Latin adjective certus (settled, sure), from cernere
latinEntries.example: Latin certus means settled or sure.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 certus 意为已定的、可靠的。

latinEntries.structure: Latin verb cernere (cern-, cretum; to sift, decide)
latinEntries.example: Latin cernere means to sift, and so to decide.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁语 cernere 意为筛，因而也指判定。
