definition_zh: 宇宙辐射；来自外太空的高能粒子与射线
definition_en: high-energy particles and rays that reach the earth from outer space
core_image: 高原上的探测器，计数灯在黑暗中一闪一闪，屋顶上方划过细密的虚线
scene: 高原观测站里，闪烁体探测器的计数灯明明灭灭，说明有看不见的粒子穿过了屋顶。 Cosmic radiation passes through the station roof and leaves faint flashes in the detector.
sceneCN: 这里指来自外太空、能穿透屋顶的高能粒子（第 1 个义项：宇宙辐射的总体）；句意为宇宙辐射穿过观测站屋顶，在探测器里留下微弱闪光。图中可辨识物件：闪烁体探测器、计数灯、屋顶、夜空。

pos.zh: 名词短语：多作不可数，指来自太空的高能粒子与射线；强调来源而非单一粒子

derivatives.zh: 由希腊语表示「宇宙、秩序」的名词加形容词词尾构成，义为「宇宙的」
同一词根的名词，义为「宇宙；有序的整体」
以本短语第一成分构成的近义术语，指单个高能粒子
本短语第二成分的动词形式，义为「辐射；发散」
由动词加表示「作用、过程」的词尾构成，义为「辐射」
由本短语第二成分加形容词词尾构成，义为「辐射的」

senses.title: High-energy particles from space
senses.definition: the general name for energetic particles and rays arriving at the earth from outside its atmosphere
senses.definitionCN: 对从大气层之外到达地球的高能粒子与射线的总称
senses.example: Cosmic radiation arrives at the top of the atmosphere from every direction.
senses.exampleCN: 宇宙辐射从各个方向到达大气层顶部。
senses.why: A single umbrella term was needed once balloon flights showed that ionisation increased with altitude.
senses.whyCN: 当气球观测显示电离随高度增加后，就需要一个统称。

senses.title: Primary cosmic radiation
senses.definition: the original particles arriving from space before they interact with the atmosphere
senses.definitionCN: 在与大气发生作用之前从太空到达的原始粒子
senses.example: Primary cosmic radiation consists mostly of protons stripped of their electrons.
senses.exampleCN: 初级宇宙辐射主要由失去电子的质子组成。
senses.why: Dividing primary from secondary separates what space sends from what the air makes.
senses.whyCN: 把初级与次级分开，就把太空送来的东西与空气生成的东西区别开来。

senses.title: Secondary cosmic radiation
senses.definition: the cascade of particles produced when primary radiation strikes air molecules
senses.definitionCN: 初级辐射撞击空气分子时产生的粒子级联
senses.example: Secondary cosmic radiation forms a shower of particles when the primary hits air.
senses.exampleCN: 当初级粒子撞上空气时，次级宇宙辐射形成粒子簇射。
senses.why: By the time radiation reaches sea level almost none of it is primary, so the distinction matters for measurement.
senses.whyCN: 当辐射到达海平面时几乎已没有初级粒子，因此这一区分对测量很重要。

senses.title: Galactic cosmic radiation
senses.definition: the component accelerated elsewhere in the galaxy, arriving steadily from outside the solar system
senses.definitionCN: 在银河系其他地方被加速、从太阳系之外稳定到达的成分
senses.example: Galactic cosmic radiation comes from outside the solar system and varies slowly.
senses.exampleCN: 银河宇宙辐射来自太阳系之外，变化缓慢。
senses.why: Its steadiness makes it a baseline against which solar outbursts stand out.
senses.whyCN: 它的稳定使它成为基准，太阳爆发在对比下便显得突出。

senses.title: Solar cosmic radiation
senses.definition: the particles accelerated by the sun, especially during flares and coronal mass ejections
senses.definitionCN: 由太阳加速的粒子，尤其在耀斑与日冕物质抛射期间
senses.example: Solar cosmic radiation surges during a large flare.
senses.exampleCN: 在一次大耀斑期间，太阳宇宙辐射会骤增。
senses.why: The sun is a local and variable source, so its contribution is named separately.
senses.whyCN: 太阳是局部的、变化的源，因此它的贡献被单独命名。

senses.title: Dose in aviation and spaceflight
senses.titleCN: 航空与航天的辐射剂量
senses.definition: the accumulated exposure received by aircrews and astronauts from cosmic radiation
senses.definitionCN: 机组人员与航天员从宇宙辐射中累积受到的照射
senses.example: Aircrews receive more cosmic radiation than people on the ground.
senses.exampleCN: 机组人员受到的宇宙辐射比地面人员更多。
senses.why: Shielding by air is thinner at altitude, so the same sky delivers a larger dose.
senses.whyCN: 高空的空气屏蔽更薄，同一片天空因此送来更大的剂量。

senses.title: Effects on electronics
senses.definition: single-particle upsets in circuits caused by an energetic particle strike
senses.definitionCN: 高能粒子撞击引起的电路单粒子翻转
senses.example: A single particle of cosmic radiation can flip a bit in a memory chip.
senses.exampleCN: 一个宇宙辐射粒子就能翻转存储芯片中的一位。
senses.why: Miniaturised circuits hold so little charge that one strike now matters.
senses.whyCN: 微型化电路所存电荷极少，一次撞击便足以造成影响。

senses.title: Cosmogenic nuclides and dating
senses.definition: rare isotopes produced in rock by cosmic radiation, used to date exposure surfaces
senses.definitionCN: 岩石中由宇宙辐射产生的稀有同位素，用于给暴露面测年
senses.example: Cosmogenic nuclides produced by cosmic radiation allow surfaces to be dated.
senses.exampleCN: 由宇宙辐射产生的宇宙成因核素使地表得以测年。
senses.why: The sky leaves a slow chemical clock in stone, and the clock can be read.
senses.whyCN: 天空在石头里留下一只缓慢的化学钟，而这钟可以被读出。

senses.title: Ultra-high-energy cosmic radiation
senses.definition: the rarest particles, carrying energies far beyond anything built on earth can produce
senses.definitionCN: 最稀少的粒子，其能量远超地球上任何人造装置所能产生
senses.example: Ultra-high-energy cosmic radiation is rare but carries more energy than any accelerator can reach.
senses.exampleCN: 超高能宇宙辐射很稀少，却携带比任何加速器都高的能量。
senses.why: At the far end of the energy range, the rarity itself becomes the scientific problem.
senses.whyCN: 在能量范围的最远端，稀少本身成了科学问题。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Greek adjective for the ordered universe to a Latin noun for the act of sending out rays. Both halves are well attested; the phrase itself dates from the era when balloon flights first detected the radiation, so its first use is approximate.
intro.cn: 这个短语把一个表示有序宇宙的希腊形容词，与一个表示发出射线的拉丁名词组合起来。两半来源均有据；短语本身产生于气球升空首次探测到该辐射的年代，确切首见为约数。

items.en: Kosmos meant order, ornament and, by extension, the world as an ordered whole.
items.cn: 这个词表示秩序、装饰，引申指作为有序整体的世界。

items.en: The adjective described anything belonging to that ordered whole.
items.cn: 这个形容词描述属于那个有序整体的事物。

items.en: Radius meant a spoke of a wheel and then a ray of light.
items.cn: 这个词先指车轮的辐条，后指光线。

items.en: The verb meant to emit rays or to shine.
items.cn: 这个动词意为发出射线或发光。

items.en: English formed the noun for the emission and for the energy emitted.
items.cn: 英语由此构成名词，指发射行为与被发射的能量。

items.en: Before the First World War, balloon flights showed that ionisation rose with altitude, and the phrase for the source soon followed.
items.cn: 在第一次世界大战之前，气球飞行显示电离随高度上升，指称这一来源的短语随即出现。

note.en: The first group shares the adjective cosmic or is easily confused with it; the second group names the same or related energetic particles.
note.cn: 第一组共享形容词「宇宙的」，或容易与之混淆；第二组指相同或相关的高能粒子。

entries.definition: A single high-energy particle from space.
entries.definitionCN: 来自太空的单个高能粒子。

entries.definition: Tiny solid grains drifting between the stars.
entries.definitionCN: 在星际间飘浮的微小固体颗粒。

entries.definition: Funny, or relating to comedy.
entries.definitionCN: 滑稽的，或与喜剧相关的。

entries.definition: Relating to beauty treatment or superficial change.
entries.definitionCN: 与美容或表面修饰相关的。

entries.definition: The universe as an ordered whole.
entries.definitionCN: 作为有序整体的宇宙。

entries.definition: Radiation energetic enough to strip electrons from atoms.
entries.definitionCN: 能量足以从原子中剥离电子的辐射。

entries.definition: The radiation environment beyond the atmosphere.
entries.definitionCN: 大气层之外的辐射环境。

entries.definition: Radiation originating within the galaxy.
entries.definitionCN: 源自银河系内部的辐射。

entries.definition: Particles travelling at close to the speed of light.
entries.definitionCN: 以接近光速运动的粒子。

entries.definition: The ordinary low-level radiation present in an environment.
entries.definitionCN: 环境中普遍存在的低强度辐射。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations follow the particle from space to the ground; abstract ones treat the word as an invisible rain that never stops.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想沿着粒子从太空到地面的路径展开；抽象联想把这个词看作一场永不停歇的看不见的雨。

normal.en: A balloon rises and the ionisation meter climbs: that is cosmic radiation.
normal.cn: 气球升高，电离计读数上升，那就是宇宙辐射。

normal.en: Primary particles come from space; secondary ones are made in the air.
normal.cn: 初级粒子来自太空，次级粒子在空气中生成。

normal.en: The galaxy sends a steady background; the sun sends sudden surges.
normal.cn: 银河送来稳定的背景，太阳送来突发的骤增。

normal.en: At cruising altitude the thin air shields less, so the dose rises.
normal.cn: 在巡航高度空气稀薄、屏蔽更弱，因此剂量上升。

normal.en: One stray particle can flip a bit in a memory chip.
normal.cn: 一个游离的粒子就能翻转存储芯片中的一位。

abstract.en: Cosmic radiation is a rain with no clouds and no shelter.
abstract.cn: 宇宙辐射是一场没有云也没有屋檐的雨。

abstract.en: Anything that arrives from everywhere at once becomes a background rather than an event.
abstract.cn: 凡从各处同时到达者，便成了背景而非事件。

abstract.en: The rarest particles carry the largest questions.
abstract.cn: 最稀少的粒子承载着最大的问题。

examples.en: High-altitude flights increase the crew's exposure to cosmic radiation.
examples.cn: 高空飞行增加了机组人员受到的宇宙辐射。

examples.en: The detector recorded cosmic radiation throughout the night.
examples.cn: 探测器整夜记录着宇宙辐射。

examples.en: Thick rock shields underground labs from cosmic radiation.
examples.cn: 厚实的岩层为地下实验室屏蔽了宇宙辐射。

dict_mnemonic.text: cosmic（宇宙的）+ radiation（辐射）——来自宇宙的辐射，即宇宙辐射

root: 由 cosmic 与 radiation 组合。前者源自希腊语 kosmos「秩序、世界」；后者源自拉丁语 radius「辐条、光线」及其动词 radiare「发光、发射线」。短语随二十世纪初气球观测发现高空电离增强而出现，确切首见年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one shower of particles from its origin to its effects: the whole flux, its primary and secondary parts, its galactic and solar sources, its doses, its damage, its clock and its rarest end.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项跟踪同一场粒子雨，从来源追到影响：整体通量、初级与次级、银河与太阳来源、剂量、损伤、测年之钟与最稀少的一端。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a detector on a plateau, counting invisible arrivals.
core.cn: 核心意象：高原上的探测器，在数着看不见的来客。

branches.en: THE CORE SPLIT: one arriving flux, divided into what space sent and what the air made.
branches.cn: 核心划分：同一股到达的通量，分为太空送来的与空气生成的。

branches.en: THE TWO SOURCES: a steady galactic background and sudden solar surges.
branches.cn: 两个来源：稳定的银河背景与突发的太阳骤增。

branches.en: THE HUMAN DOSE: aircrews and astronauts receive more of it.
branches.cn: 人体剂量：机组与航天员受到更多照射。

branches.en: THE TWO TRACES: flipped bits in circuits and rare isotopes in stone.
branches.cn: 两种痕迹：电路中翻转的位与石头中的稀有同位素。

branches.en: THE EXTREME: particles too energetic for any earthly machine.
branches.cn: 极端一端：能量高到任何地球装置都无法产生的粒子。

intro.en: A Greek noun of order and a Latin noun of rays supply both halves, each with its own small family.
intro.cn: 一个表示秩序的希腊名词与一个表示射线的拉丁名词提供了两半，各自带一小族词。

latinIntro.en: Greek supplies kosmos and its adjective; Latin supplies radius, its verb and the noun of emission.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语提供了「宇宙」及其形容词；拉丁语提供了「辐条、光线」、其动词以及表示发射的名词。

items.example: It named the universe as something arranged rather than random.
items.exampleCN: 它把宇宙命名为被安排而非随机的东西。

items.example: The adjective passed into English as cosmic.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词以「宇宙的」形式进入英语。

items.example: It forms the adjective from the Greek noun.
items.exampleCN: 它把希腊名词变成形容词。

items.example: The word moved from a wheel's spoke to a beam of light.
items.exampleCN: 这个词从车轮辐条转到光束。

items.example: The verb supplies the English verb and noun of radiation.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供了英语的动词与名词形式。

items.example: It names the act of sending out energy.
items.exampleCN: 它命名发出能量的行为。

items.example: The noun covers both the process and what is emitted.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词既指过程也指被发出的东西。

items.example: The compound narrows the mass noun to a countable particle.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词把不可数的总称收窄为可数的粒子。

derivatives.zh: 由希腊语表示「宇宙、秩序」的名词加形容词词尾构成，义为「宇宙的」
同一词根的名词，义为「宇宙；有序的整体」
以本短语第一成分构成的近义术语，指单个高能粒子
本短语第二成分的动词形式，义为「辐射；发散」
由动词加表示「作用、过程」的词尾构成，义为「辐射」
由本短语第二成分加形容词词尾构成，义为「辐射的」

definition_zh: 杂食性的；什么都吃的；兴趣广泛的
definition_en: describing an animal or person that consumes both plant and animal material, or more broadly one with very wide tastes
core_image: 一张餐桌上同时摆着谷物、浆果、鱼与昆虫，一把叉子伸向每一种
scene: 这里指「杂食性的」。 The omnivorous bear eats berries in July and salmon in September.
sceneCN: 这里 omnivorous 指「杂食性的」（第 1 个义项：植物与动物性食物都吃）；这只杂食性的熊七月吃浆果，九月吃鲑鱼。图中可辨识物件：餐桌、谷物、浆果、鱼、昆虫。

pos.zh: 杂食性的；什么都吃的；兴趣广泛的（比较级 more omnivorous，最高级 most omnivorous）

collocations.zh: 什么都想知道的求知欲

senses.title: Eating both diets
senses.titleCN: 杂食性：植物与动物性食物兼食
senses.definition: describing an animal that eats both plant and animal material in substantial amounts
senses.definitionCN: 描述大量食用植物与动物性材料两者的动物
senses.example: The omnivorous diet of the fox includes fruit, insects and small mammals.
senses.exampleCN: 狐狸的杂食食谱包括果实、昆虫与小型哺乳动物。
senses.why: The adjective marks the mixed-diet class, which is neither herbivorous nor carnivorous.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词标出混合食性类别，既非植食也非食肉。

senses.title: Bears and other switch eaters
senses.definition: describing animals such as bears that shift between plant and animal foods as seasons change
senses.definitionCN: 描述熊这类随季节在植物性与动物性食物之间切换的动物
senses.example: Omnivorous bears gain weight on berries before the salmon run.
senses.exampleCN: 杂食的熊在鲑鱼洄游前靠浆果增重。
senses.why: Seasonal switching is the practical advantage of the class: the animal is never stuck with one failing food.
senses.whyCN: 季节切换是这一类的实际优势：动物不会困在单一失败的食物上。

senses.title: Omnivorous birds
senses.titleCN: 杂食鸟类：谷物、昆虫与腐肉都吃
senses.definition: describing birds that take seeds, fruit, insects, eggs or carrion depending on opportunity
senses.definitionCN: 描述视机会取食种子、果实、昆虫、卵或腐肉的鸟类
senses.example: Omnivorous birds adapt quickly when a crop fails.
senses.exampleCN: 作物歉收时，杂食鸟类能迅速适应。
senses.why: Flight lets birds sample many patches, which makes a mixed diet especially efficient.
senses.whyCN: 飞行让鸟类能采样许多斑块，因此混合食性尤其高效。

senses.title: Omnivorous insects
senses.titleCN: 杂食昆虫：既取食植物也取食动物
senses.definition: describing insects that feed on plant tissue and on other animals or carrion
senses.definitionCN: 描述既取食植物组织、也取食其他动物或腐肉的昆虫
senses.example: Omnivorous ants scavenge seeds, insects and dead vertebrates.
senses.exampleCN: 杂食蚂蚁取食种子、昆虫与死亡脊椎动物。
senses.why: Many ants are the clearest examples, because a colony can exploit several food channels at once.
senses.whyCN: 许多蚂蚁是最清楚的例子，因为一个蚁群能同时利用多条食物通道。

senses.title: The human mixed diet
senses.titleCN: 人类混合饮食：谷物与肉并用
senses.definition: describing the human species' capacity to live on a combination of plant and animal foods
senses.definitionCN: 描述人类物种靠植物与动物性食物组合生活的能力
senses.example: Human beings are omnivorous and can survive on many different food mixes.
senses.exampleCN: 人类是杂食性的，能靠许多不同的食物组合生存。
senses.why: The adjective is used at species level in nutrition, describing a capacity rather than a recommended diet.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词在营养学中用于物种层面，描述一种能力，而不是推荐食谱。

senses.title: An omnivorous reader
senses.titleCN: 什么书都读的人：阅读范围极广
senses.definition: figuratively describing a person who reads widely across genres, subjects and levels of difficulty
senses.definitionCN: 比喻描述跨越体裁、主题与难度广泛阅读的人
senses.example: She is an omnivorous reader who moves from biology to detective novels.
senses.exampleCN: 她是个什么书都读的人，从生物学读到侦探小说。
senses.why: The dietary metaphor turns reading into eating: the reader consumes every kind of text.
senses.whyCN: 饮食比喻把阅读变成进食：读者消耗各种文本。

senses.title: Omnivorous curiosity
senses.titleCN: 无所不包的求知欲：什么都想了解
senses.definition: figuratively describing an appetite for knowledge that ranges across unrelated fields
senses.definitionCN: 比喻描述横跨不相关领域的求知欲望
senses.example: His omnivorous curiosity led him from fossils to finance.
senses.exampleCN: 他无所不包的求知欲把他从化石带到金融。
senses.why: The metaphor extends from texts to questions, where the 'food' is any subject at all.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻从文本扩展到问题，这里的「食物」可以是任何主题。

senses.title: Cultural and media omnivorousness
senses.titleCN: 文化杂食：品味与平台都不设限
senses.definition: in sociology and media studies, describing a taste or usage pattern that crosses highbrow, popular and multiple platforms
senses.definitionCN: 社会学与媒介研究中描述跨越高雅、通俗与多种平台的品味或使用模式
senses.example: The study found an omnivorous pattern of news consumption across print, video and social media.
senses.exampleCN: 研究发现了一种跨纸媒、视频与社交媒体的杂食型新闻消费模式。
senses.why: The adjective has become a technical term for boundary-crossing, not merely for eating everything.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词已成为描述跨界的技术术语，不再只是「什么都吃」。

intro.en: Omnivorous is a scientific Latin adjective from omnis 'all' and vorare 'devour', older than the English noun omnivore.
intro.cn: omnivorous 是科学拉丁语形容词，由 omnis「全部」与 vorare「吞食」构成，比英语名词 omnivore 更早。

items.en: Omnis meant all or every, and its prefix form omni- spread into words about power, knowledge and transport.
items.cn: omnis 意为全部、每个，其前缀形式 omni- 扩散到关于权力、知识与交通的词中。

items.en: Vorare meant to devour, the eating verb shared with herbivorous and carnivorous.
items.cn: vorare 意为吞食，与 herbivorous、carnivorous 共用的吃的动词。

items.en: Omnivorus was the adjective for a mixed diet in modern scientific Latin. Its exact first use is uncertain.
items.cn: omnivorus 是近代科学拉丁语中表示混合食性的形容词；确切首用存疑。

items.en: English omnivorous is recorded in the seventeenth century and was soon used figuratively for broad reading. The exact first citation is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语 omnivorous 见于 17 世纪，很快被比喻用于广泛阅读；确切首见书证存疑。

items.en: Sociology and media studies turned omnivorous into a term for crossing cultural and platform boundaries in the late twentieth century.
items.cn: 20 世纪后期，社会学与媒介研究把 omnivorous 变成描述跨越文化与平台边界的术语。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the -vorous ending; the near-meaning group separates mixed diet from wide interest and technical breadth.
note.cn: 形近组共享 -vorous 结尾；近义组区分混合食性、广泛兴趣与技术性广度。

entries.definition: The animal or person itself. It is a count noun, so a bear is an omnivore with an omnivorous diet.
entries.definitionCN: 指动物或人本身。它是可数名词，因此熊是 omnivore，其食谱是 omnivorous。

entries.definition: Describes a plant-only diet. The stem herba- replaces omni- and reverses the class.
entries.definitionCN: 描述纯植食。词干 herba- 替换 omni-，类别随之相反。

entries.definition: Describes a flesh-only diet. The stem caro- replaces omni-, and the diet narrows.
entries.definitionCN: 描述纯肉食。词干 caro- 替换 omni-，食性随之收窄。

entries.definition: A species or person that uses many resources. It is broader than omnivorous, which is specifically about food.
entries.definitionCN: 指利用多种资源的物种或人。它比 omnivorous 更宽，后者专指食物。

entries.definition: Describes tastes drawn from many sources. It matches the figurative sense of omnivorous but is used of style and choice, not diet.
entries.definitionCN: 描述从多种来源汲取的品味。它对应 omnivorous 的比喻义，但用于风格与选择，而非食性。

entries.definition: A technical adjective for feeding on many kinds of food, mostly used of insects. It overlaps with omnivorous but belongs to entomology.
entries.definitionCN: 技术形容词，指取食多种食物，多用于昆虫。它与 omnivorous 重叠，但属昆虫学用语。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real suffixes, real collocations and real relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实后缀、真实搭配与真实同族词。

normal.en: omni 'all' + -vorous 'eating': eating everything.
normal.cn: omni「全部」+ -vorous「吃……的」：什么都吃。

normal.en: Typical phrases: omnivorous animal, omnivorous diet, omnivorous reader, omnivorous curiosity.
normal.cn: 典型搭配：杂食动物、杂食食谱、什么书都读的人、无所不包的求知欲。

normal.en: The family runs omnivore, omnivory, omnibus and omni- words such as omnipotent.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 omnivore、omnivory、omnibus，以及 omnipotent 这类 omni- 词。

normal.en: Swap the stem to change the class: omni-, herbi-, carni-.
normal.cn: 换词干就换类别：omni-、herbi-、carni-。

normal.en: In sociology, omnivorous means boundary-crossing taste, not literal eating.
normal.cn: 在社会学中，omnivorous 指跨界的品味，而非字面进食。

abstract.en: Picture one table holding grain, berries, fish and insects, with a fork reaching everywhere.
abstract.cn: 想象一张桌上摆着谷物、浆果、鱼与昆虫，叉子伸向每一处。

abstract.en: Picture a reader with a biology paper and a detective novel open at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一位读者同时摊开一篇生物学论文和一本侦探小说。

abstract.en: Picture one person reading news in print, on video and on a phone before noon.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人在中午前就从纸媒、视频与手机上读新闻。

examples.en: The omnivorous bear moves from berries to salmon as autumn arrives.
examples.cn: 秋天到来时，这只杂食的熊从浆果转向鲑鱼。

examples.en: Omnivorous ants exploit both seeds and dead insects.
examples.cn: 杂食蚂蚁既利用种子也利用死昆虫。

examples.en: Her omnivorous reading made her hard to surprise in conversation.
examples.cn: 她什么书都读，交谈时很难被难住。

dict_mnemonic.text: omnivore（杂食动物）+ ous（……的）→ 杂食的 → omnivorous

root: 拉丁 omnis「全部」+ vorare「吞食」→ 科学拉丁语 omnivorus「各类食物都吃的」→ 英语 omnivorous。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses apply one adjective to diet, seasonal switching, birds, insects, human capacity, reading, curiosity and cultural breadth.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把同一个形容词用于食性、季节切换、鸟类、昆虫、人类能力、阅读、求知欲与文化广度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one table holding grain, berries, fish and insects, reached from every side.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张桌上摆着谷物、浆果、鱼与昆虫，四面都能取用。

branches.en: DIET: mixed eating is the base, and seasonal switching is its practical payoff.
branches.cn: 食性：混合取食是基本义，季节切换是它的实际收益。

branches.en: ANIMALS: birds and insects show the class across very different body plans.
branches.cn: 动物：鸟类与昆虫展示了这一类在差异极大的体型中的表现。

branches.en: HUMANS: the adjective describes a species-level capacity, not a menu plan.
branches.cn: 人类：这个形容词描述物种层面的能力，而非一份菜单。

branches.en: METAPHOR: reading and curiosity become forms of eating.
branches.cn: 比喻：阅读与求知欲变成进食的形式。

branches.en: TECHNICAL: sociology uses the word for taste that crosses every boundary.
branches.cn: 技术用法：社会学用这个词描述跨越一切边界的品味。

intro.en: Omnivorous is the adjective branch of the 'all-eating' family, and omni- is one of the most transparent prefixes in English.
intro.cn: omnivorous 是「什么都吃」词族的形容词支，omni- 是英语中最透明的前缀之一。

latinIntro.en: Omnis means all, vorare means devour, and -vorus is the scientific adjective ending used across diet words.
latinIntro.cn: omnis 意为全部，vorare 意为吞食，-vorus 是各类食性词共用的科学形容词词尾。

items.meaningCN: 什么都吃的；兴趣广泛的
items.example: The omnivorous fish takes plants and larvae.
items.exampleCN: 这种杂食鱼既吃植物也吃幼虫。

items.example: The omnivore samples every food patch.
items.exampleCN: 这只杂食动物尝试每一处食物斑块。

items.example: Omnivory is common among ants.
items.exampleCN: 杂食性在蚂蚁中很常见。

items.example: Omni- also forms omnipotent and omniscient.
items.exampleCN: omni- 还构成 omnipotent 与 omniscient。

items.example: The omnibus edition collects all four novels.
items.exampleCN: 合集版收录了全部四部小说。

items.example: Herbivorous animals have fermentation chambers.
items.exampleCN: 植食动物有发酵腔。

items.example: Carnivorous animals have shearing teeth.
items.exampleCN: 食肉动物有剪切齿。

items.example: Omnivorous species are often habitat generalists.
items.exampleCN: 杂食物种常常也是生境广适种。

definition_zh: 双方同意的；合意的；（法律）仅以合意成立的
definition_en: resting on the agreement of the people involved, or formed by consent alone without further formality
core_image: 同一张纸的两栏各有一个签名，没有人站在身后催促
scene: 合同末尾的两栏签名都是自愿写下的，桌边没有第三个人。 The contract is consensual, so either party may end it by giving notice.
sceneCN: 这里 consensual 指「只凭当事人同意即成立」（第 2 个义项：法律上仅以合意成立的合同）；句意为这是一份合意合同，任何一方通知即可终止。可辨识物件：两栏签名、合同纸、桌边的空椅、钢笔。

pos.zh: 双方同意的；合意的
（法律）仅以合意成立的

经双方同意地

senses.title: Resting on mutual agreement
senses.definition: of an arrangement, based on the agreement of everyone involved rather than on force or decree
senses.definitionCN: 指某种安排建立在所有相关方同意之上，而非靠强制或命令
senses.example: The settlement was consensual, not imposed by the court.
senses.exampleCN: 这项和解是双方同意的，并非法院强加。
senses.why: the adjective turns the noun for shared feeling into a property of arrangements: what rests on consent is consensual.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词把表示「同感」的名词变成安排的一种性质：建立在同意之上的，就是 consensual。

senses.title: A contract formed by consent alone
senses.titleCN: 仅凭合意即成立的合同
senses.definition: in civil law, of a contract that arises from the parties' agreement without delivery or ceremony
senses.definitionCN: 在大陆法系中，指无需交付或仪式、仅由当事人合意即成立的合同
senses.example: The contract is consensual, so either party may end it by giving notice.
senses.exampleCN: 这是一份合意合同，任何一方通知即可终止。
senses.why: law divides contracts by what makes them binding, and consent alone is one of those makers.
senses.whyCN: 法律按「什么使合同有约束力」来分类，而仅有同意就是其中一种来源。

senses.title: Sexual activity with consent
senses.definition: of sexual activity, engaged in with the free agreement of those taking part
senses.definitionCN: 指性行为是在参与者自由同意之下发生的
senses.example: The film portrays a consensual relationship between two adults.
senses.exampleCN: 这部影片描绘两个成年人之间自愿的关系。
senses.why: modern law and public speech needed a clear adjective to separate agreement from assault, and this one was chosen.
senses.whyCN: 现代法律与公共讨论需要一个清楚的形容词，把「同意」与「侵犯」分开，选中的就是它。

senses.title: Accepted across a group
senses.definition: of a decision or a norm, accepted by all the parties concerned
senses.definitionCN: 指某项决定或规范被所有相关方接受
senses.example: The change was consensual across all departments.
senses.exampleCN: 这项变动在所有部门都获得了认可。
senses.why: when consent spreads from two people to a whole body, the adjective describes the breadth of acceptance.
senses.whyCN: 当同意从两个人扩展到整个机构，这个形容词描述的就是接受的广度。

senses.title: A reality a community shares
senses.definition: in psychology, of what a community treats as real because its members agree on it
senses.definitionCN: 心理学用语：一个群体因其成员一致认可而视为真实的东西
senses.example: Consensual reality is what a community treats as real.
senses.exampleCN: 所谓共同认定的现实，就是一个群体当作真实的东西。
senses.why: psychology asks what makes something real for people, and shared agreement is one of the answers.
senses.whyCN: 心理学追问「对人而言什么算真实」，而共同的同意正是答案之一。

senses.title: A reflex on the other side
senses.titleCN: 医学上对侧的同感反应
senses.definition: in medicine, of a reaction in one part of the body that follows a stimulus applied to the other side
senses.definitionCN: 医学用语：身体一侧受刺激后，另一侧出现的相应反应
senses.example: The pupil shows a consensual reaction to light in the other eye.
senses.exampleCN: 一只眼受光时，另一只眼的瞳孔会出现同感反应。
senses.why: the oldest borrowed sense survives in clinical language, where two sides of the body are said to feel together.
senses.whyCN: 最早的借入义在临床用语中留存：身体两侧被说成「一同感受」。

senses.title: Voluntary rather than forced
senses.definition: of an individual's participation, given freely and without pressure
senses.definitionCN: 指个人的参与出于自由意志，没有受压
senses.example: Participation in the survey was consensual and anonymous.
senses.exampleCN: 参与这项调查是自愿且匿名的。
senses.why: the focus shifts from the arrangement to the person: nothing was taken from anyone without a yes.
senses.whyCN: 焦点从「安排」移到「人」：没有在缺少一个「愿意」的情况下从任何人那里拿走什么。

senses.title: Settled by convention, not by proof
senses.titleCN: 靠约定而非靠论证确定
senses.definition: of a definition or a standard, fixed by shared usage rather than by authority or demonstration
senses.definitionCN: 指定义或标准由共同用法确定，而非由权威或证明确定
senses.example: The boundary of the term is consensual among practitioners.
senses.exampleCN: 这个术语的边界在从业者之间是约定俗成的。
senses.why: some questions cannot be proved, only agreed, and the adjective marks that kind of settlement.
senses.whyCN: 有些问题无法证明，只能约定，这个形容词标记的正是这类了结方式。

intro.en: Consensual is built on the Latin noun consensus 'agreement' plus the adjective ending -al, which continues Latin -alis. Its root is sentire 'to feel'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: consensual 由拉丁名词 consensus「一致」加形容词词尾 -al 构成，后者延续拉丁 -alis。其词根是 sentire「感受」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Sentire meant 'to feel, perceive, think'; it is the root behind sense, sentiment, consent and consensus.
items.cn: sentire 意为「感觉、知觉、思考」，是 sense、sentiment、consent 与 consensus 共同的词根。

items.en: The noun consensus, from consentire 'to feel together', named agreement or accord as a state.
items.cn: 名词 consensus 出自 consentire「一同感受」，命名作为状态的「一致」或「同心」。

items.en: The ending -alis formed adjectives of relation, as in naturalis and legalis; English keeps it as -al.
items.cn: 词尾 -alis 构成表示关系的形容词，如 naturalis 与 legalis；英语以 -al 保留它。

items.en: The adjective appears in English in the eighteenth century, first in legal and philosophical writing about agreements and shared perception.
items.cn: 这个形容词在十八世纪出现于英语，最初见于论述协议与共同感知的法律、哲学文字。

items.en: Psychologists extended it to shared reality, physicians kept it for sympathetic reflexes, and modern law applied it to sexual consent.
items.cn: 心理学家把它扩展到共同认定的现实，医生把它保留给同感反射，现代法律则把它用于性方面的同意。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and formation): dictionaries date the first English use differently, and it is unsettled whether the word was coined in English or already existed in medieval Latin.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与构词地）：各家词典对最早的英语用例说法不一，也无法确定这个词是在英语中造出，还是中古拉丁语里已有。

note.en: Group one holds words close in shape, one of which shares the root but not the meaning; group two holds adjectives for what people freely accept.
note.cn: 第一组收形近的词，其中一个与本词同根而不同义；第二组收表示「人们自愿接受」的形容词。

entries.definition: The noun this adjective comes from: general agreement in a group.
entries.definitionCN: 本形容词所出的名词：群体中的普遍一致。

entries.definition: Also from consentire, but it names permission itself, and it is a noun and a verb, not an adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 同出 consentire，但它命名许可本身，且是名词与动词，不是形容词。

entries.definition: From Latin sensualis, built on sensus 'sense, feeling': it means devoted to bodily pleasure, not based on agreement.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 sensualis，由 sensus「感觉」构成；意为沉于肉体享乐，与「同意」无关。

entries.definition: From censere 'to assess': a population count; it looks close but belongs to another Latin verb.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 censere「评估」：人口清点；形近，却属于另一个拉丁动词。

entries.definition: Done by one's own choice; it stresses the absence of compulsion rather than the presence of two agreeing parties.
entries.definitionCN: 出于自己选择而做；侧重「无强制」，而非「两方相合」。

entries.definition: Held or done by each toward the other; a mutual feeling need not be formally agreed.
entries.definitionCN: 双方各自对对方持有或做出的；相互的情感不必经过正式同意。

entries.definition: Created by or arising from a contract; it needs a document, where consensual needs only assent.
entries.definitionCN: 由合同产生或与合同有关；它需要一份文书，而 consensual 只需要同意。

entries.definition: Allowed by a rule or an authority; permissible is about permission from above, consensual about agreement between equals.
entries.definitionCN: 为规则或权威所允许；permissible 关乎自上而下的许可，consensual 关乎平辈之间的同意。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Consensus plus -al: the adjective of the shared feeling.
normal.cn: consensus 加 -al：把「共同感受」变成形容词。

normal.en: The family runs consensus, consensual, consensually, consent, consenting.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 consensus、consensual、consensually、consent、consenting。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark its fields: a consensual contract, a consensual relationship, consensual reality.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出它的领域：合意合同、双方自愿的关系、共同认定的现实。

normal.en: The medical phrase consensual reflex survives from the oldest sense of the root.
normal.cn: 医学上的「同感反射」一语，源自这个词根最古老的一义。

normal.en: The opposite is non-consensual, common in law and in policy.
normal.cn: 相反的说法是 non-consensual，在法律与政策文本中很常见。

abstract.en: Picture two signatures on one sheet with nobody standing behind the pen.
abstract.cn: 想象一张纸上有两个签名，笔后没有站着任何人。

abstract.en: Picture a door that opens only when both handles are turned.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇只有两个把手同时转动才开的门。

abstract.en: Picture two people letting go of a rope at the same moment.
abstract.cn: 想象两个人同时松开同一条绳。

examples.en: A consensual separation avoids the cost and bitterness of a trial.
examples.cn: 合意分居省去了诉讼的花费与怨气。

examples.en: The guild's standards are consensual rather than legally enforced.
examples.cn: 行会的标准靠约定，而非靠法律强制。

examples.en: Consensual decision-making can stall when one member refuses to move.
examples.cn: 只要有一名成员不肯动，共识决策就可能卡住。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「con（共同）+ sens（感觉）+ ual」——大家感觉一样、都点头 → 合意的

root: 拉丁 consensus「一致」+ -alis（关系形容词词尾）→ 英语 consensual；词根 sentire「感受」，com- 表「共同」，故本义为「一同感受而同意」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all rest on a yes that was freely given: to a contract, to a relationship, to a group norm, to a shared reality, to a clinical reaction, to participation, or to a definition.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都建立在一个自由给出的「愿意」上：对合同、对关系、对群体规范、对共同认定的现实、对临床反应、对参与，或对一个定义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two signatures on one sheet, with no third person standing behind the pen.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张纸上有两个签名，笔后没有第三人站着。

branches.en: THE FREELY GIVEN YES: what rests on agreement, and the person who was not pressed.
branches.cn: 自由的愿意：建立在同意之上的安排，以及没有被压的人。

branches.en: LAW WITHOUT FORM: consent alone makes the contract binding.
branches.cn: 无需形式的法律：仅有同意就使合同生效。

branches.en: BOUNDARIES DRAWN BY AGREEMENT: sexual consent, and a term fixed by usage rather than proof.
branches.cn: 靠同意划出的边界：性方面的同意，以及靠用法而非证明定下的术语。

branches.en: THE WHOLE BODY: consent spreads from two parties to every department.
branches.cn: 整个机构：同意从两方扩展到每个部门。

branches.en: SHARED INNER AND OUTER LIFE: a community's reality, and one side of a body answering the other.
branches.cn: 内与外的共享：群体的现实，以及身体一侧回应另一侧。

intro.en: Consensual is a Latin noun plus a Latin adjective ending; both parts recur throughout English academic vocabulary.
intro.cn: consensual 是一个拉丁名词加一个拉丁形容词词尾，两部分在英语学术词汇中反复出现。

latinIntro.en: Latin sentire supplies the root, consensus supplies the noun, and -alis supplies the relational adjective ending.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 sentire 提供词根，consensus 提供名词，-alis 提供关系形容词词尾。

items.example: The prefix makes the feeling shared.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀使感受成为共享的。

items.example: The root carries the idea of feeling.
items.exampleCN: 词根带着「感受」的意思。

items.example: The word arrived from Latin whole.
items.exampleCN: 这个词整体来自拉丁语。

items.example: The ending turns a noun into a relation.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把名词变成关系形容词。

items.example: The contract is consensual.
items.exampleCN: 这是一份合意合同。

items.example: The terms were consensually adopted.
items.exampleCN: 条款经双方同意获得通过。

items.example: She gave consent in writing.
items.exampleCN: 她书面表示同意。

items.example: The law targets non-consensual sharing of images.
items.exampleCN: 该法律针对未经同意传播影像的行为。

items.example: The phrase has a technical sense.
items.exampleCN: 这个短语有技术上的含义。

definition_zh: 在……之后；继……之后（较正式）
definition_en: after a particular event or time, used in formal, legal and technical writing
core_image: 竣工石碑立在路旁，压路机从碑后一路碾过去
scene: 验收会议结束之后，工程队才把最后一段路面铺完。 Subsequent to the inspection, the crew paved the last stretch.
sceneCN: 这里取第 1 个义项（在……之后，表时间先后）；句意为检查之后，施工队才铺完最后一段路面。

pos.zh: 介词性短语：在……之后；继……之后
相关形容词：随后的；后来的

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁语现在分词「随后而来的」经法语进入英语，义为「随后的；后来的」
由该形容词加副词词尾构成，义为「随后；其后」
由表示「在下、随后」的前缀与表示「跟随」的词干加名词词尾构成，义为「后继；子序列」
由表示「跟随」的拉丁词干加形容词词尾构成，义为「继起的；继续的」
与上述词干同源的名词，义为「序列；次序」，并非由本词派生

senses.title: After an event in time
senses.definition: later than a stated event or point in time
senses.definitionCN: 晚于某个指明的事件或时点
senses.example: Subsequent to the hearing, the court issued a written ruling.
senses.exampleCN: 听证之后，法院发布了书面裁决。
senses.why: The Latin participle means following after, so the phrase places one event behind another.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁分词意为「随后而来的」，因此这个短语把一件事放到另一件事之后。

senses.title: Formal substitute for after
senses.definition: used in place of the plainer preposition in formal prose
senses.definitionCN: 在正式文字中替代更朴素的介词
senses.example: Subsequent to the merger, the two brands were kept separate.
senses.exampleCN: 合并之后，两个品牌仍各自保留。
senses.why: Legal and technical writing like a heavier connective, and this phrase is the standard one.
senses.whyCN: 法律与技术写作偏爱更厚重的连接词，这个短语就是标准选择。

senses.title: Immediately following in order
senses.definition: marking the next item or step in an ordered series
senses.definitionCN: 标示有序系列中的下一项或下一步
senses.example: Subsequent to the first test, a second sample was taken.
senses.exampleCN: 第一次测试之后，又取了第二份样品。
senses.why: Sequence is the word's core, so the phrase can mark order as well as simple time.
senses.whyCN: 「序列」是这个词的核心，所以这个短语既能标记时间，也能标记次序。

senses.title: After a date in contracts
senses.definition: used in contracts to fix the moment when a term begins to apply
senses.definitionCN: 在合同中确定条款开始适用的时刻
senses.example: Subsequent to the expiry date, the licence is void.
senses.exampleCN: 在到期日之后，许可证即失效。
senses.why: A contract must say clearly what happens after a date, and the phrase marks that side of it.
senses.whyCN: 合同必须清楚写明某一日期之后会发生什么，这个短语标记的就是那一面。

senses.title: In a later stage of a process
senses.definition: used of a stage that follows an earlier treatment or step
senses.definitionCN: 用于某项处理或步骤之后的后续阶段
senses.example: Subsequent to drying, the boards are sanded twice.
senses.exampleCN: 干燥之后，板材要打磨两遍。
senses.why: Production is a chain of stages, and the phrase names the link that comes later.
senses.whyCN: 生产是一串阶段，这个短语点出较后的一环。

senses.title: Following as a result
senses.definition: used when what follows is treated as a consequence of what came before
senses.definitionCN: 用于把随后发生的事当作前事的后果
senses.example: Subsequent to the leak, the plant was shut for a week.
senses.exampleCN: 泄漏之后，工厂停产一周。
senses.why: The plain time meaning shades into cause when the later event is clearly produced by the earlier one.
senses.whyCN: 当后事明显由前事造成时，单纯的时间义就带上因果色彩。

senses.title: Later in a scholarly account
senses.titleCN: 学术叙述中的时间推进
senses.definition: used in historical or scientific writing to move the account forward
senses.definitionCN: 用于历史或科学写作，把叙述向前推进
senses.example: Subsequent to this period, pottery styles changed quickly.
senses.exampleCN: 这一时期之后，陶器样式变化很快。
senses.why: Scholarship needs to mark periods in order, and the phrase carries the reader to the next one.
senses.whyCN: 学术写作需要按顺序标记时期，这个短语把读者带到下一个时期。

senses.title: Afterwards in a formal report
senses.titleCN: 正式报告中的事后说明
senses.definition: used in reports to record what was done after an earlier stage
senses.definitionCN: 在报告中记录某一阶段之后所做的工作
senses.example: Subsequent to the survey, three recommendations were drafted.
senses.exampleCN: 调查之后，起草了三项建议。
senses.why: Reports move from what was found to what was done next, and the phrase marks the second half.
senses.whyCN: 报告从发现写到随后所做之事，这个短语标记后半段。

intro.en: Subsequent comes from Latin subsequens, the present participle of subsequi, to follow after, from sub, under or close behind, and sequi, to follow. French carried the adjective into English, and the phrase subsequent to was built on it in modern formal prose.
intro.cn: 这个词出自拉丁语现在分词「随后而来的」，其动词意为「跟随在后」，由表示「在下、紧随」的前缀与表示「跟随」的词构成。法语把该形容词传入英语，这个短语则是近代正式文字在此基础上构成的。

items.en: Sequi meant to follow, and it supplies the core of the word.
items.cn: 这个词意为「跟随」，是这个词的核心来源。

items.en: Sub meant under or close behind, and here it adds the sense of coming after.
items.cn: 这个词意为「在下、紧随其后」，在这里增添「之后」的意思。

items.en: The verb and its participle named what follows on; classical Latin used them of time and of logic alike.
items.cn: 这个动词及其分词指随后而来者；古典拉丁语中既用于时间，也用于逻辑。

items.en: French passed the adjective to English, where its first date is not precisely recorded.
items.cn: 法语把这个形容词传入英语，其在英语中的确切首见年代未见明确记载。

items.en: English used it for what comes later in time or in a sequence.
items.cn: 英语用它指在时间或次序上较后的事物。

items.en: The prepositional phrase belongs to modern legal and technical writing and replaces the plainer preposition.
items.cn: 这个介词短语属于现代法律与技术写作，用来替代更朴素的近义介词。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin verb of following or its word family; the second group lists other ways of saying after.
note.cn: 第一组共享表示「跟随」的拉丁动词或其词族；第二组是表示「在……之后」的其他说法。

entries.definition: The adjective inside the phrase, meaning coming later.
entries.definitionCN: 短语内部的形容词，义为随后的。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning afterwards, used without a following object.
entries.definitionCN: 义为随后的副词，使用时后面不接宾语。

entries.definition: A noun for a later item or, in mathematics, a sequence drawn from another.
entries.definitionCN: 指后继项的名词，在数学中指从另一序列中取出的子序列。

entries.definition: A rare adjective from the same stem, meaning following on.
entries.definitionCN: 由同一词干构成的罕见形容词，义为继起的。

entries.definition: A noun from the same stem, meaning order or a series, not derived from this word.
entries.definitionCN: 同词干名词，义为次序或序列，并非由本词派生。

entries.definition: The plain everyday preposition that the phrase replaces in formal prose.
entries.definitionCN: 朴素的日常介词，正式文字中用该短语替代它。

entries.definition: A preposition or adjective marking what comes next.
entries.definitionCN: 标记随后之事的前置词或形容词。

entries.definition: A comparative phrase that compares two times directly.
entries.definitionCN: 比较级短语，直接比较两个时间。

entries.definition: A phrase stressing that one event came right behind another.
entries.definitionCN: 强调一件事紧接另一件事而来的短语。

entries.definition: An adverb meaning after that, used without naming the starting point again.
entries.definitionCN: 义为「其后」的副词，不再重复起点。

normalIntro.en: Sub means close behind and sequi means to follow, so the phrase is a follower standing right behind an event.
normalIntro.cn: 前半意为紧随在后，后半意为跟随，所以这个短语就是一个紧站在事件后面的跟随者。

normal.en: A completion stone beside the road, and the roller moving on past it.
normal.cn: 竣工石碑立在路旁，压路机从碑后一路碾过去。

normal.en: Sub means under or close behind, and the word as a whole means following after.
normal.cn: 前半意为在下或紧随，整个词的意思就是跟随在后。

normal.en: In contracts it marks the date from which a term starts to run.
normal.cn: 在合同里它标出条款开始生效的那个日期。

normal.en: In reports it moves the reader from findings to what was done next.
normal.cn: 在报告里它把读者从发现带到随后所做的工作。

normal.en: A verb after it becomes a gerund, just as with its plainer synonym.
normal.cn: 它后面的动词要变成动名词，和更朴素的近义介词一样。

abstract.en: To say subsequent to is to insist that time has a direction.
abstract.cn: 说「在……之后」，就是在坚持时间有方向。

abstract.en: What follows an event is often what the event produced.
abstract.cn: 跟随在事件之后的东西，往往正是该事件的产物。

abstract.en: Formal prose pays for exactness with a longer phrase.
abstract.cn: 正式文字用更长的短语来换取精确。

examples.en: Subsequent to the hearing, the court issued a written ruling.
examples.cn: 听证之后，法院发布了书面裁决。

examples.en: Subsequent to the expiry date, the licence is void.
examples.cn: 在到期日之后，许可证即失效。

examples.en: Subsequent to the survey, three recommendations were drafted.
examples.cn: 调查之后，起草了三项建议。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「萨布塞昆特 图」——「萨布」在下，「塞昆特」是跟随，跟在前事之后的：在……之后

root: 拉丁语现在分词「随后而来的」，由表「在下、紧随」的前缀与表「跟随」的动词构成，经法语进入英语；短语为近代正式说法，确切首见年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one direction, later than a point, and change the setting: plain time, formal prose, ordered sequence, contracts, processes, consequence, scholarship and reports.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享一个方向，即晚于某一点，只是场景不同：单纯时间、正式文字、有序序列、合同、流程、因果、学术与报告。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a completion stone beside the road, with the roller moving on past it.
core.cn: 核心意象：竣工石碑立在路旁，压路机从碑后一路碾过去。

branches.en: TIME AFTER: the phrase marks a later point and stands in for the plainer word.
branches.cn: 时间在后：标示更晚的时点，替代更朴素的介词。

branches.en: ORDER AND STAGE: next in sequence, or a later step in a process.
branches.cn: 次序与阶段：序列中的下一步，或流程的后续阶段。

branches.en: DATE AFTER: contracts fix the moment when a term starts to run.
branches.cn: 日期在后：合同确定条款开始生效的时刻。

branches.en: RESULT AFTER: what follows is treated as a consequence.
branches.cn: 结果在后：随之而来的事被当作后果。

branches.en: THE LATER ACCOUNT: scholarship and reports move the narrative forward.
branches.cn: 后来的叙述：学术与报告把叙述向前推进。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Latin present participle to a native preposition. The items below show the family and the constructions it enters.
intro.cn: 这个短语把拉丁现在分词与本土介词接在一起。下列条目展示它的词族与它进入的结构。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries are the verb subsequi, its simple verb sequi and the prefix sub; the English adjective and phrase were built on the participle.
latinIntro.cn: 列出的拉丁词条是该动词、其简单动词与前缀；英语的形容词与短语都是在分词基础上构成的。

items.example: It adds the sense of coming after.
items.exampleCN: 它增添「之后」的意思。

items.example: It is the core of the word.
items.exampleCN: 它是这个词的核心。

items.example: It is the direct source of the English adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它是英语形容词的直接来源。

items.example: It supplies the meaning of the phrase.
items.exampleCN: 它提供这个短语的意义。

items.example: The adverb ending lets it stand without an object.
items.exampleCN: 副词词尾使它不必带宾语。

items.meaning: a later item; a derived sequence
items.example: The noun ending names the thing that follows.
items.exampleCN: 名词词尾指随后的事物。

items.example: A rare adjective from the same stem.
items.exampleCN: 由同一词干构成的罕见形容词。

items.example: It shares the stem but is not derived from the phrase.
items.exampleCN: 它与本词共享词干，但并非由这个短语派生。

items.example: The phrase takes a noun or a noun phrase.
items.exampleCN: 这个短语接名词或名词短语。

items.example: A verb must become a gerund after the preposition.
items.exampleCN: 介词后的动词必须变成动名词。

由同族词干加名词词尾构成，义为「后继；子序列」

与同族词干同源的名词，义为「序列；次序」

definition_zh: 使最大化；使增至最大；充分利用；把……发挥到极致
definition_en: to make something as great, large, or effective as it can possibly be
core_image: 把一只旋钮拧到刻度盘最右端、直到再也拧不动的顶点
scene: 这里指「使最大化」。 The plant manager turned every dial to its limit to maximize output before the export deadline.
sceneCN: 这里 maximize 是「把产量推到最高」（第 3 个义项：把产出、效率推到最高）；句意：出口截止日前，厂长把每一个旋钮都拧到极限，以把产量推到最高。场景要点：车间里的控制台、一排拧到头的旋钮、堆到天花板的成品箱。

pos.zh: 使最大化；使增至最大
充分利用；把……发挥到极致

collocations.zh: 把成功的机会做到最大

derivatives.zh: 最大值；最大限度；最大的
最大的；达到最大限度的
最大化；最大化过程
追求最大化的人；最大化者
达到最高水平；最大值；最大的（口语缩略）

senses.title: Reach the mathematical maximum
senses.definition: to find or reach the highest value of a function, quantity, or variable
senses.definitionCN: 求取或达到函数、数量、变量的最高值
senses.example: To maximize the function, set its derivative to zero.
senses.exampleCN: 要使这个函数取最大值，把它的导数设为零。
senses.why: Latin maximus names the top point of a scale. The verb makes an object arrive at that point, so the mathematical sense is the image in its plainest form.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 maximus 指刻度上的顶点。这个动词让对象抵达那个点，因此数学义是这幅意象最朴素的形态。

senses.title: Profit: make the return as large as possible
senses.definition: to make profit, revenue, or financial return as large as the situation allows
senses.definitionCN: 在条件允许的范围内把利润、收入或财务回报做到最大
senses.example: The firm cut staff and raised prices to maximize profit.
senses.exampleCN: 公司裁减员工并提高价格，以使利润最大化。
senses.why: Profit is a quantity on a dial. Turning that dial to the right end is the business version of the same gesture, and it is the sense that dominates business writing.
senses.whyCN: 利润是刻度盘上的一个量。把这只旋钮拧到最右端，就是同一个动作在商业里的版本，也是商业写作中最常见的义项。

senses.title: Output and efficiency: run everything at full capacity
senses.definition: to make production or efficiency as high as the equipment and time allow
senses.definitionCN: 在设备与时间允许的范围内把产量或效率做到最高
senses.example: The mill maximized output by running three shifts.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂实行三班倒，把产量推到最高。
senses.why: Output is what a machine yields. Maximizing it means no capacity is left unused, so the top of the scale is also the point of full employment.
senses.whyCN: 产量是机器产出的东西。把它最大化，意味着没有一寸产能被闲置，因此刻度的顶点也是“全部投入使用”的那一点。

senses.title: Impact and effect: make it land as hard as possible
senses.titleCN: 影响与效果：让冲击达到最远
senses.definition: to make the effect or influence of something as strong and wide as possible
senses.definitionCN: 把某事物的效果或影响力做到最强、最广
senses.example: The campaign was designed to maximize its impact on young voters.
senses.exampleCN: 这场宣传活动旨在把对年轻选民的影响做到最大。
senses.why: Effect is a force that travels. Pushing it to its greatest reach applies the same top-of-scale image to influence rather than to a number.
senses.whyCN: 效果是一种会传播的力量。把它推到最远的射程，就是把同一个“刻度到顶”的意象用在影响力上，而不是用在数字上。

senses.title: Chance and probability: make the odds as good as possible
senses.titleCN: 机会与概率：把胜算做到最大
senses.definition: to make the likelihood of a desired result as high as possible
senses.definitionCN: 把期望结果出现的可能性做到最高
senses.example: Apply early to maximize your chance of getting a place.
senses.exampleCN: 尽早申请，以把获得名额的机会做到最大。
senses.why: Probability is a number between zero and one. Maximizing it moves that number toward one, the upper end of its own small scale.
senses.whyCN: 概率是零到一之间的数。最大化就是把这个数推向一，也就是它自己那一小段刻度的上端。

senses.title: Use resources fully: leave nothing idle
senses.titleCN: 利用资源：不让任何一份闲置
senses.definition: to use a resource, space, or opportunity as fully as possible
senses.definitionCN: 把资源、空间或机会尽可能充分地用尽
senses.example: The new timetable maximizes the use of the existing trains.
senses.exampleCN: 新的时刻表把现有列车的利用率做到最高。
senses.why: A resource has a capacity. Maximizing means every unit of it is put to work, so the scale is measured in unused capacity rather than in output.
senses.whyCN: 资源有容量。最大化意味着它的每一个单位都被投入使用，因此这把尺子量的是“还剩多少没用”，而不是产量。

senses.title: Computing: enlarge a window to fill the screen
senses.titleCN: 计算机：把窗口放到满屏
senses.definition: to enlarge a window on a screen until it fills the available display area
senses.definitionCN: 把屏幕上的窗口放大到占满可用的显示区域
senses.example: Double-click the title bar to maximize the window.
senses.exampleCN: 双击标题栏即可把窗口最大化。
senses.why: A window has a size scale whose ceiling is the screen. The command drives the window to that ceiling, making the metaphor visible as a button.
senses.whyCN: 窗口有一个尺寸刻度，它的天花板就是屏幕。这个命令把窗口推到那层天花板，让比喻变成了一个可见的按钮。

senses.title: Biology: make fitness as high as possible
senses.titleCN: 生物学：把适应度推到最高
senses.definition: in evolutionary biology, to increase reproductive fitness to the highest level available in an environment
senses.definitionCN: 在演化生物学中，把繁殖适应度提高到环境所允许的最高水平
senses.example: Natural selection maximizes fitness in a given environment.
senses.exampleCN: 自然选择会把适应度在特定环境中推到最高。
senses.why: Evolutionary fitness is a score attached to a trait. Selection pushes that score toward its highest attainable value, exactly as a dial is turned to its stop.
senses.whyCN: 演化适应度是附在某个性状上的分数。选择把这个分数推向可达到的最高值，正像把旋钮拧到它的止点。

senses.title: Push a feature to an extreme, often at a cost
senses.titleCN: 把某一特征推到极端，往往付出代价
senses.definition: to make one feature or quantity as extreme as possible, usually by sacrificing something else
senses.definitionCN: 把某一特征或数量做到尽可能极端，通常以牺牲其他方面为代价
senses.example: The design maximizes contrast and ignores comfort.
senses.exampleCN: 这个设计把对比度做到最大，却不顾舒适度。
senses.why: When one quantity is driven to its top, everything else is subordinated to it. The word then carries a warning about single-minded extremes.
senses.whyCN: 当一个量被推到顶端，其他一切都得服从它。于是这个词带上了一层警告：只顾一头的极端做法。

intro.en: Maximize is a transparent English coinage of 1802, built on maximum plus -ize; the Latin pieces behind maximum are well documented. Dates are those given by standard etymological references.
intro.cn: maximize 是 1802 年由英语自造的词，构词清楚：maximum 加 -ize；maximum 背后的拉丁语成分有明确记载。年代采用通行词源资料给出的说法。

items.en: First recorded in English meaning 'to make as great as possible, raise to the highest degree'. It is an English formation from maximum + -ize, and Bentham is the first attested user.
items.cn: 英语中最早记录于 1802 年，意为“使尽可能大、提高到最高程度”。它是由 maximum 加 -ize 构成的英语自造词，边沁是最早可考的使用者。

items.en: Maximum entered English from French maximum and directly from Latin maximum, the neuter form of maximus 'greatest'. The noun supplied the base for the later verb.
items.cn: maximum 于 1740 年经法语 maximum 并直接由拉丁语 maximum 进入英语，后者是 maximus“最大的”的中性形式。这个名词为后来的动词提供了词基。

items.en: Latin maximus is the superlative of magnus 'great, large, big', and it belongs to the same scale as minor and minimus at the other end.
items.cn: 拉丁语 maximus 是 magnus“大的、巨大的”的最高级，它与另一端的 minor、minimus 同属一把尺子。

items.en: Maximus goes back to PIE *mag-samo-, the superlative form of *meg- 'great', the root also behind magnify, magnitude and magnate.
items.cn: maximus 可追溯到原始印欧语 *mag-samo-，即 *meg-“大”的最高级形式；该词根也是 magnify、magnitude、magnate 的来源。

items.en: Jeremy Bentham used maximize repeatedly in his utilitarian writing. The twin minimize is recorded in the same year and with the same author, so the two verbs were coined as a matching pair.
items.cn: 杰里米·边沁在功利主义写作中反复使用 maximize。与之配对的 minimize 记录于同一年、同样出自他手，因此这两个动词是一套成对造出来的。

items.en: British spelling is maximise. Maximization, maximizer and the clipped max (as a verb by 1986) complete the family. Maximize is an English verb, not a Latin one, even though every part of it looks Latin.
items.cn: 英式拼写为 maximise。maximization、maximizer 以及缩略的 max（1986 年起作动词）补足了词族。maximize 是英语动词而非拉丁语动词，尽管它的每个部件看起来都像拉丁语。

note.en: The first group separates the noun, the derived noun, the clipping and a look-alike with a different origin. The second group compares maximize with optimize, with plain increase, and with its two opposite poles, minimize and minimum.
note.cn: 第一组区分名词、派生名词、缩略词以及一个来源不同的形近词；第二组把 maximize 与 optimize、普通的 increase，以及它的两个对立端点 minimize、minimum 作比较。

entries.definition: the greatest amount or degree possible. It is the noun that maximize was built from, not a synonym of the verb.
entries.definitionCN: 可能的最大数量或程度。它是构成 maximize 的名词词基，而不是这个动词的同义词。

entries.definition: a short statement of a general truth or rule of conduct, from Latin maxima propositio. It looks like maximum but belongs to a different noun.
entries.definitionCN: 关于普遍真理或行为准则的简短格言，来自拉丁语 maxima propositio。它形似 maximum，却是另一个名词。

entries.definition: the act or process of maximizing. It names the process, while maximum names the end point.
entries.definitionCN: 最大化的行为或过程。它命名过程，而 maximum 命名终点。

entries.definition: informal short form of maximum, and by 1986 a verb meaning 'to reach the maximum level'. It is a clipping, not a separate root.
entries.definitionCN: maximum 的口语缩略形式，1986 年起也作动词，意为“达到最高水平”。它是缩略形式，不是另一条词根。

entries.definition: to make the best possible arrangement within given limits. It looks for the best compromise among competing factors, while maximize pushes one quantity to its ceiling.
entries.definitionCN: 在既定限制内做出尽可能好的安排。它在多个相互竞争的因素之间寻找最佳折中，而 maximize 把一个量推到它的天花板。

entries.definition: to make larger in amount. It says nothing about a ceiling: you can increase a number without ever reaching its maximum.
entries.definitionCN: 使数量变大。它不涉及天花板：你可以让一个数变大，却始终没到它的最大值。

entries.definition: to reduce to the smallest possible amount. It is the exact opposite pole: one verb turns the dial to the right, the other to the left.
entries.definitionCN: 使降到尽可能小的量。它正是对立的那一端：一个动词把旋钮向右拧，另一个向左拧。

entries.definition: the smallest amount or degree possible. It is the floor of the same scale whose ceiling is maximum.
entries.definitionCN: 可能的最小数量或程度。它是同一把尺子的底端，而 maximum 是顶端。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: maximum + -ize, the Latin superlative maximus, the magnus family, and the matched pair maximize / minimize.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：maximum 加 -ize、拉丁最高级 maximus、magnus 词族，以及成对的 maximize／minimize。

normal.en: Maximum is the top of a scale and -ize means 'to make'. Maximize is simply 'to make maximum'.
normal.cn: maximum 是刻度的顶端，-ize 意为“使……”。maximize 就是“使达到最大”。

normal.en: Maximus is the Latin superlative of magnus 'great'; the same root gives magnify, magnitude and magnate.
normal.cn: maximus 是拉丁语 magnus“大”的最高级；同一词根还给出 magnify、magnitude、magnate。

normal.en: Maximize and minimize were both recorded in 1802, both in Bentham: one drives to the top of the scale, the other to the bottom.
normal.cn: maximize 与 minimize 都记录于 1802 年，都出自边沁：一个把刻度推到顶，一个推到低。

normal.en: In business writing maximize collocates with profit, efficiency, output and returns — quantities that can be read off a dial.
normal.cn: 在商业写作里，maximize 常与 profit、efficiency、output、returns 搭配——都是能从刻度盘上读出来的量。

normal.en: In computing, maximize is the button that makes a window fill the screen; the screen is the ceiling of that scale.
normal.cn: 在计算机里，maximize 是让窗口占满屏幕的那个按钮；屏幕就是那把尺子的天花板。

abstract.en: Picture a dial with a hard stop at the right end. You can turn it as far as the stop and no further; that stop is what maximum means.
abstract.cn: 想象一只右端有硬止点的旋钮。你能拧到止点，再也不能多拧一格；那个止点就是 maximum 的含义。

abstract.en: A maximum is a ceiling, not a direction: maximizing tells you where to stop, not how to get there.
abstract.cn: 最大值是天花板，不是方向：maximize 告诉你该停在哪里，却没告诉你该怎么走到那里。

abstract.en: When one quantity is maximized, others are usually spent: maximum contrast costs comfort, maximum output costs rest.
abstract.cn: 当一个量被最大化，其他量通常被花掉：最大的对比度要付出舒适，最大的产量要付出休息。

examples.en: Farmers use every hectare to maximize the harvest.
examples.cn: 农民用尽每一公顷土地，把收成做到最大。

examples.en: The software maximizes screen space by hiding the toolbar.
examples.cn: 这款软件通过隐藏工具栏把屏幕空间用到最大。

examples.en: Negotiators tried to maximize the settlement without losing the deal.
examples.cn: 谈判者试图在不丢单的情况下把和解条件做到最好。

dict_mnemonic.text: “麦克西麦子”——麦克把麦子一层层堆到仓顶，堆到再也放不下一粒 → maximize 最大化、推到顶

root: 由 maximum“最大限度”加 -ize“使……”构成，maximum 又来自拉丁语 maximus“最大的”，核心是“把某物推到刻度的最右端”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of maximize, all from one gesture: a dial is turned to the far right until it will go no further, whether the scale measures a function, a profit, an output, a chance, or a window.
sensesIntro.cn: maximize 的九个义项都来自同一个动作：把旋钮一路拧到最右端，直到再也拧不动——无论这把尺子量的是函数、利润、产量、机会还是一扇窗口。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dial turned to the far right until it stops at the top of its scale.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只旋钮被拧到最右端，停在刻度的顶点。

branches.en: MEASURED QUANTITIES: functions and probabilities sit on numeric scales, and maximizing moves the value to the top of that scale.
branches.cn: 可测的量：函数与概率都落在数值刻度上，最大化就是把取值推到这段刻度的顶端。

branches.en: PRODUCTION: profit and output are the business dials, and maximizing runs them at full capacity.
branches.cn: 生产：利润与产量是商业里的旋钮，最大化就是让它们满负荷运转。

branches.en: FORCE AND EXTREME: impact is a force pushed to full reach; driving one feature alone turns the word critical.
branches.cn: 力量与极端：影响是一种被推到最远的力量；只把某一特征推到顶，就让这个词带上了批评意味。

branches.en: RESOURCES: every unit is put to work, so the measure becomes the absence of idle capacity.
branches.cn: 资源：每个单位都被投入使用，于是衡量的对象变成了“没有闲置产能”。

branches.en: DEVICES AND FITNESS: a window grows to the screen's ceiling, and fitness rises to the highest value selection can reach.
branches.cn: 设备与适应度：窗口长到屏幕这层天花板，适应度升到选择所能达到的最高值。

intro.en: Maximize is built from a complete noun plus a living suffix, so its parts are easy to see: maximum + -ize. The same Latin superlative also supplies a large family of size words.
intro.cn: maximize 由一个完整名词加一个活后缀构成，部件一眼可见：maximum 加 -ize。同一个拉丁最高级还供应了一大群表示“大小”的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin maximus 'greatest' is the superlative of magnus 'great'. Both are ordinary Latin adjectives, and maximum is the neuter form used as a noun; the PIE superlative suffix *-samo- is preserved in maximus.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 maximus“最大的”是 magnus“大的”的最高级。两者都是普通拉丁形容词，maximum 是作名词用的中性形式；原始印欧语最高级后缀 *-samo- 保留在 maximus 里。

items.meaning: to make as great as possible
items.meaningCN: 使尽可能大；最大化（-ize 构成动词）
items.example: They maximized the grant by matching it with local funds.
items.exampleCN: 他们用地方资金配套，把拨款的作用做到最大。

items.meaningCN: 最大量；最大限度（-um 为中性最高级词尾）
items.example: The tank holds a maximum of forty litres.
items.exampleCN: 这个罐子最多装四十升。

items.meaningCN: 最大的；达到最大限度的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: The drug was given at its maximal safe dose.
items.exampleCN: 这种药按最大安全剂量给予。

items.meaning: the process of making something as great as possible
items.meaningCN: 最大化；最大化过程（-ation 构成过程名词）
items.example: Profit maximization was not the only goal of the reform.
items.exampleCN: 利润最大化并不是这场改革的唯一目标。

items.meaningCN: 追求最大化的人或物（-er 表示行为者）
items.example: As a maximizer, she never settles for the second-best option.
items.exampleCN: 作为一个凡事求最大的人，她从不接受次优选项。

items.meaning: the maximum; to reach the maximum level
items.meaningCN: 最大值；达到最高水平（maximum 的缩略）
items.example: He maxed out his credit card before the trip.
items.exampleCN: 出发前他把信用卡刷到了额度上限。

items.example: The report advises firms to maximise energy efficiency.
items.exampleCN: 报告建议企业把能效做到最大。

items.meaning: a short rule of conduct or general truth
items.meaningCN: 格言；行为准则（来自拉丁语 maxima propositio，与 maximum 同形不同源）
items.example: The maxim 'less is more' guided the whole design.
items.exampleCN: “少即是多”这句格言指导了整个设计。

items.meaningCN: 放大；使显得更大（magni- 大 + -fy 使）
items.example: The lens magnifies the print for easy reading.
items.exampleCN: 这片透镜把字放大，便于阅读。

items.meaningCN: 巨大；重要性；量级（magni- 大 + -tude 状态）
items.example: Few understood the magnitude of the loss.
items.exampleCN: 很少有人明白这次损失有多大。

items.meaning: a powerful person in business or industry
items.meaningCN: 巨头；大亨（拉丁语 magnates“大人物”）
items.example: A shipping magnate funded the new museum.
items.exampleCN: 一位航运巨头出资建了这座新博物馆。

latinEntries.structure: neuter of maximus, used as a noun
latinEntries.meaningCN: 最大者；最大量（maximus 的中性形式作名词）

definition_zh: 威望；声誉；声望；由地位或成功带来的影响力
definition_en: the respect and admiration that a person, group or institution receives because of status, success or perceived quality
core_image: 剧院门口的海报上，一个名字被印得比剧名还大，路人抬头时先看见那个名字
scene: 剧院门口的节目单上，一位演员的名字排在最上方，字号比剧名还大。 The university's prestige attracts students from across the country.
sceneCN: 这里指「因地位与成就而获得的崇高声望」（第 1 个义项：高声望带来的普遍敬重）；句意为这所大学的声望吸引了全国各地的学生。可辨识物件：节目单、演员名字、剧院门廊、海报、路灯。

pos.zh: 威望；声誉（常作不可数）
由声望带来的影响力或优势
（旧用法）迷惑人的幻象；魅力

collocations.zh: 声望商品；彰显身份的商品

derivatives.zh: 有声望的；令人敬重的
以有声望的方式
声望性；令人敬重的特质
手法魔术；戏法（同出拉丁「幻象」词根）
手法魔术师
声望定价（以高价标示品质）

senses.title: High standing in others' eyes
senses.titleCN: 在他人眼中的崇高地位
senses.definition: the respect and admiration a person or institution enjoys because of status, achievement or perceived excellence
senses.definitionCN: 个人或机构因地位、成就或被认可的优秀而享有的敬重与仰慕
senses.example: The university's prestige attracts students from across the country.
senses.exampleCN: 这所大学的声望吸引了全国各地的学生。
senses.why: The word first named a glamour cast over the eyes; that dazzle later settled into lasting respect.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指投在眼前的魅惑；那种眩目后来沉淀为持久的敬重。

senses.title: Reputation earned by success
senses.definition: a reputation built by visible achievement, prizes or a record of good work
senses.definitionCN: 由可见成就、奖项或良好记录建立的声誉
senses.example: The prize added prestige to an already famous laboratory.
senses.exampleCN: 这项奖为一家本已闻名的实验室增添了声望。
senses.why: Honour attaches to the thing that has repeatedly proved itself, so success becomes the evidence behind prestige.
senses.whyCN: 荣誉附着在反复证明自身的事物上，因此成功成为声望背后的证据。

senses.title: A rank in the social scale
senses.definition: the relative social value assigned to an occupation, group or role
senses.definitionCN: 社会赋予某种职业、群体或角色的相对价值
senses.example: Occupational prestige rankings place doctors near the top and cleaners near the bottom.
senses.exampleCN: 职业声望排名把医生放在接近顶端，把清洁工放在接近底端。
senses.why: Sociology turned the word into a measurable rank: how much respect a position commands in a survey.
senses.whyCN: 社会学把这个词变成可测量的等级：某个职位在调查中能获得多少敬重。

senses.title: Goods that signal standing
senses.definition: products bought mainly because their ownership displays wealth, taste or status
senses.definitionCN: 主要因拥有者能借此展示财富、品味或地位而购买的产品
senses.example: The brand sells prestige goods rather than ordinary appliances.
senses.exampleCN: 这个品牌卖的是彰显身份的商品，而非普通家电。
senses.why: If respect can be attached to a name, then a name on a product can transfer that respect to its buyer.
senses.whyCN: 如果敬重可以附着在一个名字上，那么印在商品上的名字就能把这份敬重转给买家。

senses.title: A high price as a quality signal
senses.definition: a pricing strategy that keeps a price high so that cost itself suggests exclusivity
senses.definitionCN: 故意维持高价、让价格本身暗示稀缺与优越的定价策略
senses.example: Prestige pricing keeps the watch expensive because the price is part of the message.
senses.exampleCN: 声望定价让这款表保持高价，因为价格本身就是信息的一部分。
senses.why: Marketing made the dazzle calculable: the number on the tag does what the poster once did.
senses.whyCN: 营销把这种眩目变得可计算：价签上的数字做了海报曾经做的事。

senses.title: The accent that carries authority
senses.titleCN: 带权威感的方言或口音
senses.definition: a language variety that listeners treat as educated, powerful or socially superior
senses.definitionCN: 被听者视为有教养、有权力或社会地位更高的一种语言变体
senses.example: The prestige dialect of the capital shapes school textbooks.
senses.exampleCN: 首都的威望方言塑造了学校教科书。
senses.why: Speech carries status too, so the variety spoken by those with standing becomes the one others imitate.
senses.whyCN: 言语同样携带地位，因此有地位者所说的变体成为他人模仿的对象。

senses.title: A nation's standing abroad
senses.definition: the international respect a country holds, often used to justify diplomatic or military action
senses.definitionCN: 一国在国际上所受的敬重，常被用来为外交或军事行动辩护
senses.example: The summit was staged to restore national prestige after the border dispute.
senses.exampleCN: 这场峰会被安排出来，是为了在边境争端之后恢复国家威望。
senses.why: States borrow the personal word: a country can be seen to lose face as an individual can.
senses.whyCN: 国家借用了个人层面的词：一个国家也像个人一样会被看作丢了脸面。

senses.title: An old word for a dazzling illusion
senses.definition: in older usage, a spell, trick or illusion that deceives the eyes
senses.definitionCN: 旧时用法中指欺骗眼睛的魅惑、戏法或幻象
senses.example: In the old usage, prestige named a spell cast over the eyes.
senses.exampleCN: 在旧用法中，这个词指投在眼前的魅惑。
senses.why: The Latin source meant a blinding trick; the modern sense of respect is a later softening of that dazzle.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁来源意为使人目盲的戏法；现代的敬重义是那种眩目后来软化的结果。

intro.en: Prestige came through French from Latin praestigium 'illusion, delusion', from praestringere 'to bind or blind', built on prae- 'before' and stringere 'to bind, tighten'. The modern sense of standing developed in the nineteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: prestige 经法语来自拉丁 praestigium「幻象、迷惑」，再往上出自 praestringere「绑住、使目盲」，由 prae-「在前」与 stringere「绑紧」构成。现代的声望义在十九世纪发展出来。年代均为约数。

items.en: Stringere meant 'to bind, tighten, graze'. Its pre-Latin origin is reconstructed rather than directly attested.
items.cn: stringere 意为「绑紧、收紧、擦过」。它在拉丁语之前的来源属于重构，而非直接有据。

items.en: Prae- 'before' plus stringere produced praestringere, 'to bind in front, to blind or dazzle'.
items.cn: prae-「在前」加 stringere 构成 praestringere「在前绑住、使目盲、使目眩」。

items.en: The noun praestigium named an illusion or juggler's trick, something that deceives the sight.
items.cn: 名词 praestigium 指幻象或戏法，即欺骗视觉之物。

items.en: Old French prestige kept the sense of a deceptive glamour, and English adopted the word in the seventeenth century as a term for illusion.
items.cn: 古法语 prestige 保留了「骗人的魅力」之义，英语在十七世纪引入该词，用作「幻象」的名称。

items.en: By the nineteenth century the dazzle had become admiration: prestige now meant the impression of power and distinction a person or institution makes.
items.cn: 到十九世纪，眩目变成了敬慕：prestige 开始指一个人或机构给人留下的权力与卓越印象。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Latin source of stringere is a reconstruction, and no single first citation marks the shift from illusion to standing, so the dates here are approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：stringere 在拉丁语之前的来源属于重构形式；从幻象义到声望义的转变也没有唯一的最早书证，因此这里给出的年代均为约数。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same blinding root; group two holds nouns for the respect a person or institution commands.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「使目盲」词根的词；第二组是表示人或机构所受敬重的名词。

entries.definition: Describing something that commands respect; it is the adjective formed from the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 描述享有敬重的事物；是由这个名词构成的形容词。

entries.definition: Sleight of hand, from the same Latin noun for a trick; it keeps the old sense of deceiving the eyes.
entries.definitionCN: 手法戏法，同出表示戏法的拉丁名词；保留了「欺骗眼睛」的旧义。

entries.definition: A conjurer who performs sleight of hand; the person who makes the illusion.
entries.definitionCN: 表演手法戏法的魔术师；制造幻象的人。

entries.definition: Means in a manner that earns respect, usually describing an institution's style or reputation.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「以令人敬重的方式」，通常描述机构的风格或声誉。

entries.definition: A person's rank or position within a group; prestige is the respect that may accompany that rank.
entries.definitionCN: 个人在群体中的等级或位置；prestige 是可能伴随该等级而来的敬重。

entries.definition: The general opinion held about someone's character or work; it can be good or bad, while prestige is always favourable.
entries.definitionCN: 他人对某人品格或工作的总体看法；可好可坏，而 prestige 总是正面的。

entries.definition: One's position relative to others in a profession or community.
entries.definitionCN: 在某职业或共同体中相对于他人的位置。

entries.definition: The ability to change decisions or opinions; prestige can produce influence, but the two are not the same.
entries.definitionCN: 改变决定或意见的能力；声望可以带来影响力，但两者并不等同。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real blinding root, the real derivatives and the real social phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的「使目盲」词根、真实的派生词与真实的社会搭配。

normal.en: The Latin source is a trick that blinds the eyes; from that dazzle the modern word for respect grew.
normal.cn: 拉丁来源是使眼睛目盲的戏法；现代的敬重义正是从那种眩目生长出来。

normal.en: The family runs prestige, prestigious, prestigiously, prestigiousness and the older pair prestidigitation and prestidigitator.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 prestige、prestigious、prestigiously、prestigiousness，以及保留旧义的 prestidigitation 与 prestidigitator。

normal.en: The social phrases are national prestige, occupational prestige and prestige dialect.
normal.cn: 社会搭配有国家威望、职业声望与威望方言。

normal.en: The marketing phrases are prestige goods and prestige pricing.
normal.cn: 营销搭配有声望商品与声望定价。

normal.en: The same root is visible in the older word for sleight of hand, which still means deceiving the eye.
normal.cn: 同一词根可见于表示手法戏法的旧词，那个词至今仍指欺骗眼睛。

abstract.en: Picture a poster where one name is printed larger than the play itself.
abstract.cn: 想象一张海报，一个名字印得比剧名还大。

abstract.en: Picture a price tag so high that the number itself starts to speak about quality.
abstract.cn: 想象一张价签高得让数字本身开始替品质说话。

abstract.en: Picture a stage magician whose hand is faster than the eye, leaving only admiration behind.
abstract.cn: 想象一位舞台魔术师，手比眼睛更快，最后只留下赞叹。

examples.en: The award brought prestige to a department long ignored by funders.
examples.cn: 这个奖项为一个长期被资助方忽视的院系带来了声望。

examples.en: Prestige pricing works only when buyers already trust the name.
examples.cn: 声望定价只有在买家已经信任该品牌时才奏效。

examples.en: Children quickly learn which accent carries prestige in their town.
examples.cn: 孩子们很快学会镇上的哪种口音带有威望。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「预先」加「绑紧」——先把你眼睛绑住，让你只看见光环 → 威望、声望

root: prestige 经法语来自拉丁 praestigium「幻象、戏法」，源头是 praestringere「在前绑住、使目盲」= prae-「在前」+ stringere「绑紧」。stringere 的更深来源属于重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one shift: a blinding illusion becomes a lasting glow around a name. The glow is then read as personal standing, earned reputation, social rank, expensive goods, a price signal, a respected accent, a nation's image and finally the old illusion itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一次转变展开：使人目盲的幻象变成名字周围持久的光晕。这层光晕依次被读作个人地位、赢得的声誉、社会等级、昂贵商品、价格信号、受敬重的口音、国家形象，最后回到那个旧有的幻象本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a name printed larger than everything around it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个名字被印得比周围一切都大。

branches.en: FROM SPELL TO RESPECT: the old blinding trick survives as the glow that makes a name admired.
branches.cn: 从魅惑到敬重：古老的障眼戏法留存为让名字受仰慕的光晕。

branches.en: EARNED GLOW: prizes and records turn admiration into evidence.
branches.cn: 赢来的光：奖项与记录把仰慕变成证据。

branches.en: RANK AND ACCENT: a survey can rank a job, and a city accent can carry the same rank in speech.
branches.cn: 等级与口音：调查可以给职业排名，城市口音也能在言语中携带同样的等级。

branches.en: THE PRICE TAG: a product or a number borrows the glow and sells it onward.
branches.cn: 价签：商品或数字借来这层光，再把它卖出去。

branches.en: NATIONAL FACE: a country can lose or restore the same standing an individual holds.
branches.cn: 国家脸面：一个国家也会失去或恢复个人所拥有的同一种地位。

intro.en: The word can be read from a Latin prefix meaning 'before', a Latin verb for binding, the noun of illusion built from them and the modern derived family.
intro.cn: 这个单词可以按表示「在前」的拉丁前缀、表示绑紧的拉丁动词、由它们构成的名词以及现代派生词族逐段读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin prae- and stringere give praestringere and praestigium; the noun for a trick then produced both prestige and the older word for sleight of hand.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 prae- 与 stringere 构成 praestringere 与 praestigium；表示戏法的名词随后同时衍生出 prestige 与表示手法魔术的旧词。

items.example: The prefix places the action in front of the eyes.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把动作放在眼睛前面。

items.structure: stringere, strinxi, strictum (Latin verb, third conjugation)
items.example: The verb supplies the image of something pulled tight.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供把某物拉紧的意象。

items.meaning: to bind in front; to blind, dazzle
items.meaningCN: 在前绑住；使目盲、使目眩
items.example: The Latin verb described a glare that stopped the sight.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁动词描述一种挡住视线的强光。

items.example: The noun named a trick that deceived the eyes.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指欺骗眼睛的戏法。

items.example: The institute's prestige drew visiting scholars.
items.exampleCN: 该研究所的声望吸引了访问学者。

items.meaningCN: 享有声望的；极受敬重的
items.example: She won a prestigious fellowship.
items.exampleCN: 她赢得了一项极具声望的研究奖金。

items.example: The journal is prestigiously edited.
items.exampleCN: 这份期刊的编辑水准享有盛誉。

items.meaningCN: 声望性；令人敬重的特质
items.example: Rankings measure the prestigiousness of a school.
items.exampleCN: 排行榜衡量一所学校的声望。

items.example: The hall applauded his prestidigitation.
items.exampleCN: 大厅为他的手法戏法鼓掌。

items.example: The prestidigitator never showed his hands.
items.exampleCN: 这位魔术师从不让人看清他的手。

latinEntries.meaning: to bind in front; to blind

definition_zh: v. 默许，纵容；共谋，暗中串通
definition_en: to let something wrong happen, or to plot it quietly
core_image: 两个人交换一个眼色，然后各自转开脸
scene: 经理对偷运睁一只眼闭一只眼。 The manager connived at the smuggling.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：connive 指默许；句意是经理对偷运睁一只眼闭一只眼。

pos.zh: 默许；共谋

derivatives.zh: 默许；共谋
暗中谋划的
密谋
串通

senses.title: Look the other way
senses.definition: to let a wrong continue without objecting
senses.definitionCN: 不加反对地让错事继续
senses.example: The manager connived at the smuggling.
senses.exampleCN: 经理对偷运睁一只眼闭一只眼。
senses.why: The image is a deliberately closed eye.
senses.whyCN: 意象是故意闭上的眼。

senses.title: Plot together quietly
senses.definition: to work secretly with others on a wrong plan
senses.definitionCN: 与他人暗中谋划错事
senses.example: They connived to cheat the buyers.
senses.exampleCN: 他们串通起来欺骗买家。
senses.why: The closed eye turns into a shared glance.
senses.whyCN: 闭上的眼变成共享的一瞥。

intro.en: Connive is Latin connivere, to shut the eyes.
intro.cn: connive 是拉丁语 connivere，意为闭上眼。

senses.title: True in theory
senses.definition: used to say that something is possible or correct as a matter of theory, whether or not it happens
senses.definitionCN: 表示某事在道理上可行或正确，不论实际是否发生
senses.example: In principle, the two networks can be linked.
senses.exampleCN: 原则上，这两个网络可以互联。
senses.why: A principle is a starting point, and from a starting point a conclusion may follow without being carried out.
senses.whyCN: 原则是起点，从起点可以推出结论，却未必真的去做。

senses.title: Beside theory talk
senses.titleCN: 近义辨析：与理论说法相近
senses.definition: it resembles the phrase about theory, though it points to a rule or a foundation rather than to a model
senses.definitionCN: 它与表理论的说法相近，只是指向规则或根基，而非模型
senses.example: In principle the method is sound; in practice it is too slow.
senses.exampleCN: 这个方法在理论上站得住；实际做起来太慢。
senses.why: Theory suggests a model of how things work, while principle suggests a rule that governs them.
senses.whyCN: 理论暗示事物运作的模型，原则暗示支配事物的规则。

senses.title: Not on principle
senses.definition: the phrase states what is possible in theory, while the look-alike with on states what a person refuses or accepts on moral grounds
senses.definitionCN: 这个短语陈述理论上可能的事，而形近短语陈述某人基于道义理由拒绝或接受什么
senses.example: In principle she accepted the rule, though she disliked it.
senses.exampleCN: 原则上她接受了这条规定，尽管并不喜欢。
senses.why: One frame is about feasibility, the other about conviction, and the prepositions keep them apart.
senses.whyCN: 一个框架谈可行性，另一个谈信念，介词把两者分开。

senses.title: Agreement with a reserve
senses.titleCN: 会议义：原则同意但留保留
senses.definition: in committee language it records approval of an idea while details or costs remain to be settled
senses.definitionCN: 在委员会语言中，记录对想法的认可，而细节或费用仍待敲定
senses.example: The board agreed in principle to the merger.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会原则上同意这次合并。
senses.why: Approval of a principle is cheaper than approval of a budget, which is why the phrase is so useful in meetings.
senses.whyCN: 认可一项原则比批准一笔预算便宜，因此这个短语在会议上十分好用。

senses.title: A rule of law or policy
senses.titleCN: 原则义：法律与政策准则
senses.definition: it can state that a right or a duty exists as a general rule, subject to conditions
senses.definitionCN: 可说明某项权利或义务作为通则存在，但须受条件限制
senses.example: In principle, every citizen may apply for the grant.
senses.exampleCN: 原则上，每位公民都可以申请这项补助。
senses.why: A general rule covers everyone on paper, and conditions decide what happens in fact.
senses.whyCN: 通则在纸面上覆盖所有人，条件决定事实上如何。

senses.title: The level of a law of nature
senses.definition: in science it marks what follows from a law or a mechanism, before engineering limits are counted
senses.definitionCN: 在科学中，标出由定律或机理推出的事，尚未计入工程限制
senses.example: In principle the reaction releases energy at room temperature.
senses.exampleCN: 原则上该反应在室温下就释放能量。
senses.why: A mechanism may allow something that a real apparatus cannot deliver, and the phrase keeps that gap open.
senses.whyCN: 机理允许的事，真实装置未必做得到，这个短语把那个差距留着。

senses.title: Concession, then caveat
senses.titleCN: 让步义：先认可再提条件
senses.definition: it concedes the general case before the speaker adds a condition or a cost
senses.definitionCN: 先承认一般情形，随后补上条件或代价
senses.example: The plan is acceptable in principle, subject to cost review.
senses.exampleCN: 这个方案原则上可以接受，但须视成本评审而定。
senses.why: The frame makes a concession sound generous while keeping a door open for refusal.
senses.whyCN: 这个框架让让步显得大度，同时为拒绝留着一扇门。

senses.title: Not the head of a school
senses.titleCN: 辨义：不表校长或负责人
senses.definition: the related adjective and noun can name a school head, but the phrase states feasibility only
senses.definitionCN: 相关形容词与名词可指校长，但短语只陈述可行性
senses.example: In principle marks a theoretical stand, not a school head.
senses.exampleCN: 原则上这一说法标的是理论立场，不是学校校长。
senses.why: English split the two spellings, and only the noun with the narrower meaning entered this phrase.
senses.whyCN: 英语把两种拼写分了工，只有词义较窄的那个名词进入了这个短语。

intro.en: Principle comes from Latin principium, a beginning or foundation, from princeps, first or chief, built on primus, first, and capere, to take. The Latin chain is secure; the phrase is modern.
intro.cn: principle 出自拉丁语 principium「开端、基础」，源于 princeps「居首者」，由 primus「第一」与 capere「取」构成。拉丁语链条清楚；短语属近代。

items.en: Primus meant first in order, and it stands behind primary and prime as well.
items.cn: primus 意为次序上的第一，也支撑着 primary 与 prime 等词。

items.en: Capere meant to take or seize, and its compounds cover capture, reception and acceptance.
items.cn: capere 意为拿取、抓取，其复合词涵盖捕获、接收与接受。

items.en: The compound named the one who takes the first place, hence a chief or a leader.
items.cn: 这个复合词指占据首位的人，因此指首领。

items.en: The noun moved from a beginning in time to a foundation on which reasoning rests.
items.cn: 这个名词从时间上的开端转为推理所依托的基础。

items.en: English keeps principle for a rule and principal for a chief or a school head.
items.cn: 英语用前者指原则，用后者指首领或校长。

items.en: The theoretical qualifier belongs to modern discussion; first dates are approximate.
items.cn: 这个理论性限定语属于近代讨论，首见年代为约数。

note.en: The first group shares the form or the root but means a rule, a refusal or a head; the second group are phrases of theory and feasibility.
note.cn: 第一组共用形式或词根，却指规则、拒绝或负责人；第二组是表理论与可行性的短语。

entries.definition: It means because of a conviction, not because something is possible.
entries.definitionCN: 意为出于信念，而非因为某事可行。

entries.definition: The look-alike noun names a person or a main sum.
entries.definitionCN: 形近名词指负责人或本金。

entries.definition: It contrasts a model with actual practice.

entries.definition: It names what really happens, the usual partner of the frame.
entries.definitionCN: 它指真正发生的情况，常与本短语配对。

entries.definition: A single adverb for what follows from theory.
entries.definitionCN: 由理论推出的单词副词。

entries.definition: It means as recorded or planned, before reality tests it.
entries.definitionCN: 意为按记录或计划，尚未经现实检验。

entries.definition: It states what normally happens, not what is possible.
entries.definitionCN: 陈述通常发生的事，而非可能的事。

entries.definition: It marks a statement made at a general level.
entries.definitionCN: 标出在一般层面作出的陈述。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real first-taker root, the split between principle and principal, and the real pairing with practice.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想用真实的居首取位词根、原则与校长的分工，以及与实践的真实配对。

normal.en: The root is the first taker, so a principle is where reasoning starts.
normal.cn: 词根是居首取位者，因此原则是推理起步之处。

normal.en: Two spellings split the work: a rule on one side, a chief on the other.
normal.cn: 两种拼写分担功能：一边是规则，一边是首领。

normal.en: Theory gives a model, while principle gives a governing rule.
normal.cn: 理论给出模型，原则给出支配规则。

normal.en: The phrase usually faces its partner, practice, across a semicolon.
normal.cn: 这个短语常与搭档「实践」隔一个分号相望。

normal.en: In meetings it records approval of an idea before the bill arrives.
normal.cn: 在会议上，它在账单到来前先记下对想法的认可。

abstract.en: Like a straight line drawn on a plan, before the boulder on site is seen.
abstract.cn: 像图纸上画的直线，工地上的巨石尚未看见。

abstract.en: Like a rule written at the top of a page, with conditions pencilled below.
abstract.cn: 像写在页首的规则，条件用铅笔注在下面。

abstract.en: Like a door marked open on a map, which may still be locked in fact.
abstract.cn: 像地图上标着开启的门，实际上可能仍锁着。

examples.en: In principle, the two systems can share one database.
examples.cn: 原则上，两个系统可以共用一个数据库。

examples.en: The committee approved the idea in principle.
examples.cn: 委员会原则上同意了这个想法。

examples.en: In principle the repair is simple, though it needs a crane.
examples.cn: 原则上这次修理很简单，只是需要一台吊车。
