sensesIntro.en: Eight senses separate feasibility in theory, the near twin about theory, the contrast with a moral stance, committee approval with a reserve, legal and policy rules, scientific mechanism, concession with a condition, and the exclusion of a school head.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项区分：理论可行性、与理论说的近义辨析、与道义立场的对照、会议中的保留式同意、法律政策准则、科学机理、带条件的让步，以及排除校长义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a straight line drawn on a plan, while a boulder on the site forces a detour.
core.cn: 核心意象：图纸上画出的一条直线，而工地上的巨石逼出一条绕行。

branches.en: THE THEORY: what follows from a rule or a mechanism before limits are counted.
branches.cn: 理论：由规则或机理推出的事，尚未计入限制。

branches.en: THE NEAR TWIN: a model of how things work differs from a rule that governs them.
branches.cn: 近义辨析：事物运作的模型不同于支配它们的规则。

branches.en: THE CONTRAST: feasibility is not a moral conviction.
branches.cn: 对照：可行性不同于道义信念。

branches.en: THE RESERVE: approval of an idea can be given before details or costs are settled.
branches.cn: 保留：在细节或费用敲定前先认可想法。

branches.en: THE RULE AND THE LIMIT: general rights are stated, and no school head is meant.
branches.cn: 规则与边界：陈述普遍权利，且不指校长。

intro.en: The phrase rests on a Latin noun of beginning and foundation built from the words for first and to take.

latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 primus「第一」加 capere「取」，给出 princeps「居首取位者」与 principium「开端」。

definition_zh: 黏合力；凝聚力；（语言学）篇章衔接；（群体）团结
definition_en: the force or quality by which parts stick together, whether molecules, group members or sentences
core_image: 细管里的水柱被自己内部的力量拉住，高出杯口也不落下
scene: 把细管插进水里，水柱自己爬了上来，高出杯口却不肯落下。 Water climbs the narrow tube because cohesion holds the molecules together.
sceneCN: 这里 cohesion 指物质内部分子彼此黏合的力量（第 1 个义项：物理黏合力）；句意为水能爬上细管，是因为黏合力把分子拉在一起。

pos.zh: 黏合力；凝聚力（不可数，指黏合的状态或力量）
（语言学）衔接（不可数，指篇章内部的连接关系）

derivatives.zh: 黏合；连贯（由拉丁 cohaerere「黏在一起」进入，核心是「彼此附着」，是本词的基础动词）
有黏合力的；有凝聚力的（由「凝聚力」一词的形容词形式而来，由状态转指性质）
连贯的；一致的（由拉丁词根加表共同的前缀，构成另一形容词形式，由「粘住」转指「说得通」）
连贯性（由基础形容词加表状态的名词后缀而来，由性质转指状态，常与 cohesion 对照）
黏附（由拉丁词根加表朝向的前缀而来，由「黏住」转为「附着到别的表面」）

senses.title: Physical sticking
senses.definition: the attraction that holds molecules of the same substance together
senses.definitionCN: 把同种物质的分子拉在一起的那种吸引力
senses.example: Cohesion pulls the water into a rounded drop on the leaf.
senses.exampleCN: 黏合力把水在叶面上拉成一颗圆润的水珠。
senses.why: The oldest sense is literal: things of one kind cling to one another, as water molecules do.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项是字面的：同类之物彼此附着，就像水分子那样。

senses.title: Social unity
senses.definition: the strength of the bonds that keep a community or society together
senses.definitionCN: 使一个共同体或社会保持一体的纽带强度
senses.example: Cohesion in the village survived the closure of the mine.
senses.exampleCN: 矿井关闭之后，村子里的凝聚力仍然存在。
senses.why: The physical image transfers to people: what holds molecules together becomes what holds neighbours together.
senses.whyCN: 物理意象被移用到人身上：把分子拉住的力量，变成把邻里拉住的力量。

senses.title: Group and team cohesion
senses.definition: the degree to which members of a group are attached to it and to one another
senses.definitionCN: 一个群体的成员对群体及彼此依附的程度
senses.example: The coach measured cohesion before the final match.
senses.exampleCN: 教练在决赛前测量了团队凝聚力。
senses.why: Psychology made cohesion a variable: something a group can have more or less of, and something that can be built.
senses.whyCN: 心理学把凝聚力变成变量：一个群体可以多一点或少一点，也可以被刻意建设。

senses.title: Textual cohesion
senses.definition: the ties of reference, substitution and conjunction that make a text hold together
senses.definitionCN: 由照应、替代与连接构成、使篇章连成一体的各种联系
senses.example: Cohesion in the paragraph comes from repeated pronouns and linkers.
senses.exampleCN: 这一段的衔接来自重复出现的代词与连接词。
senses.why: Linguists borrowed the word for the surface links between sentences: text also has a kind of glue.
senses.whyCN: 语言学者借用了这个词来表示句子之间的表面连接：文本也有一种黏合剂。

senses.title: Cohesive devices
senses.definition: the specific words and structures, such as pronouns and ellipsis, that create those ties
senses.definitionCN: 造成这些联系的具体词与结构，如代词与省略
senses.example: The essay lists cohesion devices before it asks students to write.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇文章先列出衔接手段，再让学生动笔。
senses.why: Once the concept exists, it can be broken into parts that teachers can name and test.
senses.whyCN: 概念一旦存在，就能被拆成教师可以命名与检测的部件。

senses.title: Cohesion versus coherence
senses.definition: the difference between surface links and the underlying sense that a text makes
senses.definitionCN: 表面连接与文本整体说得通这层意思之间的区别
senses.example: The paragraph has cohesion but no coherence: the links lead nowhere.
senses.exampleCN: 这段有衔接却没有连贯：连接词通向不了任何地方。
senses.why: Glue is not meaning; a text can be tightly linked and still say nothing, so the pair must be distinguished.
senses.whyCN: 胶水不等于意义；文本可以连接紧密却什么也没说，因此必须区分这两个概念。

senses.title: Alliance cohesion
senses.definition: the willingness of partners or coalition members to stay together under disagreement
senses.definitionCN: 伙伴或联盟成员在分歧之下仍愿意留在一起的程度
senses.example: Cohesion among the allies weakened when the funding ended.
senses.exampleCN: 资金终止后，盟友之间的凝聚力削弱了。
senses.why: Politics applies the word to agreements between bodies, where unity is tested by competing interests.
senses.whyCN: 政治把这个词用到团体间的协议上，其团结受到彼此竞争的利益的检验。

senses.title: A measured target
senses.definition: an index or policy aim expressing how united a group or society should be
senses.definitionCN: 表达一个群体或社会应有多团结的指数或政策目标
senses.example: The programme reports cohesion as a score for each district.
senses.exampleCN: 该项目把凝聚力作为每个城区的分数来报告。
senses.why: Measurement turns a bond into a number, and a number can become a target to be managed.
senses.whyCN: 测量把纽带变成数字，而数字可以变成被管理的目标。

intro.en: Cohesion comes from Latin cohaesus, the past participle of cohaerere 'to stick together', built on com- 'together' and haerere 'to cling'. English borrowed the noun in the seventeenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: cohesion 来自拉丁 cohaesus，即 cohaerere「黏在一起」的过去分词，由表示「共同」的前缀加 haerere「附着」构成。英语在十七世纪借入这个名词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Haerere meant 'to stick, cling, be fixed'. It also lies behind adhere and hesitation, where being stuck turns into a pause.
items.cn: haerere 意为「黏住、附着、固定」。它也是 adhere 与 hesitation 的来源，其中「被粘住」转成了「停顿」。

items.en: Cohaerere added com- 'together' to haerere, giving 'to stick together, be connected'. Its participle is cohaesus.
items.cn: cohaerere 在 haerere 前加表示「共同」的前缀，得到「黏在一起、相互连接」。其分词是 cohaesus。

items.en: The noun cohaesio named the state of being stuck together; it could describe both bodies and arguments.
items.cn: 名词 cohaesio 命名黏在一起的状态，既能描述物体，也能描述论证。

items.en: English cohesion appears in the seventeenth century, first in physical and philosophical writing, then in social description.
items.cn: 英语 cohesion 在十七世纪出现，先见于物理与哲学写作，后进入社会描述。

items.en: Halliday and Hasan made cohesion a central term of text linguistics in 1976, listing reference, substitution, ellipsis, conjunction and lexical ties.
items.cn: 韩礼德与哈桑在一九七六年把 cohesion 变成篇章语言学的核心术语，列出照应、替代、省略、连接与词汇衔接。

items.en: Source uncertain: the pre-Latin origin of haerere is not established, and the exact date of the English noun's first use varies between dictionaries.
items.cn: 来源不确定：haerere 在拉丁语之前的来源未得到证明；这个英语名词首次使用的确切年代，各词典说法不一。

note.en: Group one separates words built on the same stick root; group two holds terms for unity and connection.
note.cn: 第一组区分同一「黏住」词根的词；第二组是团结与连接的术语。

entries.definition: Logical consistency, especially of an argument or text; it is about intelligibility, not glue.
entries.definitionCN: 逻辑上的一致性，尤指论证或文本；它关乎可理解性，而非黏合。

entries.definition: Attachment of one substance to a different surface; the prefix means 'to', not 'together'.
entries.definitionCN: 一种物质附着到另一种表面；前缀意为「朝向」，而非「共同」。

entries.definition: Holding together; it describes the quality, while cohesion names the state or force.
entries.definitionCN: 有黏合力的；形容词描述性质，cohesion 命名状态或力量。

entries.definition: To hold together or be consistent; it names the process that cohesion results from.
entries.definitionCN: 黏合；前后一致。它命名产生凝聚力的过程。

entries.definition: Active support among people with shared interests; it is cohesion in action.
entries.definitionCN: 有共同利益者之间的主动支持；它是行动中的凝聚力。

entries.definition: The state of being one whole; it is broader and less mechanical than cohesion.
entries.definitionCN: 成为一个整体的状态；比凝聚力更宽，也更少机械意味。

entries.definition: The process of combining parts into one system; cohesion is the resulting hold, integration is the making.
entries.definitionCN: 把部分合成一个系统的过程；凝聚力是结果性的黏合，整合是制造过程。

entries.definition: Agreement of parts with one standard over time; it concerns regularity rather than sticking.
entries.definitionCN: 各部分长期符合同一标准；它关乎规律性，而非黏合。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin verb, its real relatives and real technical uses.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁动词、其真实同族词与真实的技术用法。

normal.en: Cohesion is sticking together; adhesion is sticking to something else.
normal.cn: cohesion 是黏在一起；adhesion 是黏到别的东西上。

normal.en: The family runs cohere, cohesion, cohesive, coherent, coherence.
normal.cn: 词族包括 cohere、cohesion、cohesive、coherent、coherence。

normal.en: Cohesion is glue, coherence is sense: a text can have one without the other.
normal.cn: cohesion 是胶水，coherence 是意义：文本可以有其一而无其二。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the range: social cohesion, group cohesion, cohesion and coherence, molecular cohesion.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出范围：社会凝聚力、群体凝聚力、衔接与连贯、分子黏合力。

normal.en: The noun is uncountable: more cohesion, less cohesion, never 'cohesions'.
normal.cn: 这个名词不可数：凝聚力多一些、少一些，不说「几个凝聚力」。

abstract.en: Picture water rising in a narrow tube because it holds on to itself.
abstract.cn: 想象水在细管里上升，因为它拉住了自己。

abstract.en: Picture a paragraph whose pronouns all point back to one another and to nothing else.
abstract.cn: 想象一段文字，所有代词都指回彼此，却不指向任何别的什么。

abstract.en: Picture an alliance held together only by the funding that is about to end.
abstract.cn: 想象一个联盟，只靠那笔即将终止的资金维系。

examples.en: Surface tension and cohesion explain why the insect can walk on water.
examples.cn: 表面张力与黏合力解释了昆虫为何能在水面上行走。

examples.en: The teacher marked cohesion separately from argument.
examples.cn: 老师把衔接与论证分开评分。

examples.en: Economic shock can destroy the cohesion of a small town in a single year.
examples.cn: 经济冲击能在一年之内摧毁一个小镇的凝聚力。

dict_mnemonic.text: co-（共同）+ haerere（黏住）+ -sion（状态）＝ 彼此黏住的状态；记「水爬细管，字连成段」。

root: 源自拉丁 cohaerere「黏在一起」的过去分词 cohaesus，再由名词 cohaesio 进入英语；该动词由前缀表「共同」加 haerere「附着」构成，haerere 更早来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from molecular attraction to social unity, team psychology, textual ties, cohesive devices, the contrast with coherence, alliance politics and measured targets.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从分子吸引，移到社会团结、团队心理、篇章联系、衔接手段、与连贯的对照、联盟政治与被测量的目标。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: water holding itself up inside a narrow tube.
core.cn: 核心意象：水在细管里把自己托住。

branches.en: MOLECULES: the literal attraction of like to like.
branches.cn: 分子：同类相吸的字面力量。

branches.en: PEOPLE AND PARTNERS: neighbours held together, and allies held through disagreement.
branches.cn: 邻里与伙伴：被拉住邻里，以及在分歧中仍被拉住的盟友。

branches.en: THE TEAM: cohesion becomes a variable a coach can build and measure.
branches.cn: 团队：凝聚力变成教练可以建设与测量的变量。

branches.en: THE TEXT: surface links between sentences, then the named devices that create them.
branches.cn: 文本：句子之间的表面连接，再是造成这些连接的具名手段。

branches.en: GLUE VERSUS SENSE, AND THE SCORE: links without meaning, and a bond turned into a number.
branches.cn: 胶水与意义，以及分数：没有意义的连接，和被变成数字的纽带。

intro.en: Cohesion is a Latin noun of sticking; its stem builds a compact family of verbs, adjectives and nouns.
intro.cn: cohesion 是表示「黏合」的拉丁名词；其词干构成一个紧凑的动词、形容词与名词词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin com- and haerere, through cohaerere and cohaesus, supply every morpheme. The related ad- form gives adhesion.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁表示「共同」的前缀与 haerere，经 cohaerere 与 cohaesus，提供全部语素。相关的表示「朝向」的形式给出 adhesion。

items.example: The chapters cohere around one question.
items.exampleCN: 各章围绕一个问题连成一体。

items.example: Cohesion depends on shared rituals.
items.exampleCN: 凝聚力依赖共享仪式。

items.example: The group remained cohesive under pressure.
items.exampleCN: 这个群体在压力下仍保持凝聚。

items.example: She gave a coherent account of the night.
items.exampleCN: 她对那晚作了连贯的陈述。

items.example: The essay lacks coherence after page three.
items.exampleCN: 这篇文章从第三页起就缺乏连贯。

items.meaning: to stick to; to follow a rule
items.example: Members adhere to the same code.
items.exampleCN: 成员遵守同一套准则。

items.example: Adhesion failed in the damp air.
items.exampleCN: 在潮湿空气中黏附失效了。

items.example: He answered without hesitation.
items.exampleCN: 他毫不犹豫地回答。

definition_zh: 算法的；由算法驱动的；按固定步骤运作的
definition_en: relating to, produced by, or organized according to an algorithm
core_image: 一排排数据流沿看不见的轨道被分拣进不同的槽口
scene: 一排排数据流沿看不见的轨道被分拣进不同的槽口，槽口上方没有一只手在操作。 The ranking of search results is now largely algorithmic rather than editorial.
sceneCN: 这里 algorithmic 指由算法而非人工编辑决定的（第 3 个义项：由算法产生的）；句意：搜索结果的排序如今主要由算法决定，而不是由编辑决定。图中可辨识物件：数据流、轨道、槽口、分流闸。

pos.zh: 算法的；由算法产生的；按固定步骤的

derivatives.zh: 算法
按算法地
算法学
十进制算法

senses.title: Relating to an algorithm
senses.definition: concerning the method or the steps of a procedure rather than its raw result
senses.definitionCN: 关于方法或步骤本身，而不是其直接结果
senses.example: The paper explains the algorithmic side of the system, not its hardware.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇论文解释系统的算法层面，而非硬件。
senses.why: the adjective simply tags whatever belongs to an algorithm, so its plainest job is to mark that domain.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词就是给属于算法的事物贴标签，最基本的作用是标出那个领域。

senses.title: Expressed as formal steps
senses.definition: written as a precise sequence that can be checked step by step
senses.definitionCN: 写成可逐步核对的精确序列
senses.example: The solution is algorithmic: it lists the moves instead of arguing for them.
senses.exampleCN: 这个解法是算法式的：它列出步骤，而不是为步骤辩护。
senses.why: to call something algorithmic is to say it can be laid out as checkable steps, not left as intuition.
senses.whyCN: 说某事物是算法式的，等于说它能被铺成可核对的步骤，而非停留在直觉。

senses.title: Produced by a running algorithm
senses.titleCN: 由运行中的算法产生的
senses.definition: generated or selected by a computer procedure rather than by a person
senses.definitionCN: 由计算机程序生成或挑选，而非由人产生
senses.example: Your feed is algorithmic, assembled from your own clicks.
senses.exampleCN: 你看到的信息流是算法生成的，由你自己的点击拼装而成。
senses.why: when the procedure runs on data, its output is naturally described with the adjective, which is how the word entered daily speech.
senses.whyCN: 当步骤在数据上运行，其产物自然用这个形容词来描述，这个词就这样进入日常语言。

senses.title: Governed by rules, not judgment
senses.definition: decided by fixed rules so that individual discretion plays little part
senses.definitionCN: 由固定规则决定，个人裁量几乎不起作用
senses.example: The allocation is algorithmic and cannot be adjusted case by case.
senses.exampleCN: 分配是按算法走的，不能逐例调整。
senses.why: the adjective also criticises systems that hide judgment inside rules, even when no computer is involved.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词也用来批评把判断藏进规则的系统，哪怕根本不涉及计算机。

senses.title: Measured by cost and complexity
senses.titleCN: 按开销与复杂度衡量的
senses.definition: describing the time or memory a procedure needs as its input grows
senses.definitionCN: 描述输入增大时步骤所需时间或内存的变化
senses.example: The algorithmic cost grew faster than the data did.
senses.exampleCN: 算法的开销增长得比数据还快。
senses.why: the study of procedures measures them, and the adjective names that measured property.
senses.whyCN: 对步骤的研究要对它作度量，形容词就指这种被度量的性质。

senses.title: Mechanical and repeatable
senses.definition: carried out the same way every time, with no room for variation
senses.definitionCN: 每次都按同样方式执行，没有变动余地
senses.example: The checking is algorithmic, so two reviewers get identical results.
senses.exampleCN: 核对是按算法做的，所以两位复核者得到相同结果。
senses.why: the defining virtue of a procedure is that it repeats exactly, and the adjective praises or warns about that sameness.
senses.whyCN: 步骤的根本优点是能精确重复，形容词对这种一致性或褒或贬。

senses.title: Generating art from rules
senses.definition: describing art or music whose form is generated by a set of rules
senses.definitionCN: 指形式由一组规则生成的艺术或音乐
senses.example: The gallery showed algorithmic drawings that no hand had drawn.
senses.exampleCN: 画廊展出了并非由手绘出的算法绘画。
senses.why: artists who hand a rule set to a machine produce works whose authorship sits in the rules, hence the adjective.
senses.whyCN: 把规则集交给机器的艺术家，其作者性落在规则上，于是有了这个形容词。

senses.title: Concerning fairness of automated decisions
senses.titleCN: 关于自动决策的公平性
senses.definition: used of the bias, transparency or accountability of automated decisions
senses.definitionCN: 用于指自动决策的偏见、透明度或问责
senses.example: The report examined algorithmic harms in hiring tools.
senses.exampleCN: 报告考察了招聘工具中的算法危害。
senses.why: as automated decisions spread, the adjective became a label for the political question of who answers for them.
senses.whyCN: 随着自动决策扩散，这个形容词成了「谁来负责」这一政治问题的标签。

intro.en: Algorithmic is algorithm plus the adjective ending -ic, which English took from Greek through Latin. The base word itself is an eponym from the mathematician al-Khwarizmi. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: algorithmic 是 algorithm 加形容词词尾 -ic，后者经拉丁语来自希腊语。词基本身是由数学家花拉子米之名转来的词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Algorithm descends from the Latinised name Algoritmi, given to the calculation method taught by al-Khwarizmi in the ninth century.
items.cn: algorithm 出自拉丁化人名 Algoritmi，本是九世纪花拉子米所教计算法的名称。

items.en: The base was later respelled after Greek arithmos, number, by a false association that became permanent.
items.cn: 词基后来因与希腊语 arithmos「数」的错误联系而改拼，这一改动沿用至今。

items.en: The ending -ic goes back to Greek -ikos, meaning relating to, which Latin passed on as -icus and French and English shortened to -ic.
items.cn: 词尾 -ic 可追到希腊语 -ikos「与……有关的」，拉丁语作 -icus 传下，法语与英语缩为 -ic。

items.en: The adjective is recorded in the nineteenth century, when the noun still meant calculation rules; it described anything done by such rules.
items.cn: 这个形容词在十九世纪已有记录，当时名词仍指计算规则，形容词描述按这类规则进行的事物。

items.en: With computers the adjective moved to procedures, complexity, trading and ranking, and later to the social questions raised by automated decisions.
items.cn: 有了计算机之后，这个形容词转向步骤、复杂度、交易与排序，后来又转向自动决策引发的社会问题。

items.en: The base from Algoritmi and the ending from Greek -ikos through Latin -icus are both documented. The earliest use of the English adjective is dated only approximately, and any older Indo-European source for -ikos is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 首见年代不确定：词基出自 Algoritmi，词尾经拉丁语 -icus 出自希腊语 -ikos，两段都有文献依据；英语形容词最早使用的年代只有约数，-ikos 更早的印欧语来源属于重构形式。

note.en: The first group is the same base in other shapes; the second group names neighbouring descriptions of rule-bound and automated behaviour.
note.cn: 第一组是同一词基的其他形式；第二组是与「受规则约束」「自动化」相邻的说法。

entries.definition: The procedure itself; the adjective describes what belongs to or comes from it.
entries.definitionCN: 指步骤本身；形容词描述属于它或由它而来的事物。

entries.definition: By running a procedure; it answers how, while the adjective answers what kind.
entries.definitionCN: 意为按算法执行；副词回答「怎样」，形容词回答「哪一类」。

entries.definition: The study of procedures and their costs; it is a discipline, not a description.
entries.definitionCN: 研究步骤及其开销的学科；它是学科名，不是描述词。

entries.definition: The older word for decimal calculation; it shares the origin but not the computing sense.
entries.definitionCN: 指十进制计算的较早词；同源，但没有计算机义。

entries.definition: Working by itself once set going; it stresses independence from a hand, while algorithmic stresses the rule being followed.
entries.definitionCN: 设定后自行运作；强调无需人手，而 algorithmic 强调所遵循的规则。

entries.definition: Involving calculation by computer; it names the machinery of doing, algorithmic names the method's form.
entries.definitionCN: 指通过计算机计算；它指做的机器手段，algorithmic 指方法的形式。

entries.definition: Built on stated rules, whether or not a machine runs them; algorithmic usually implies execution by a procedure.
entries.definitionCN: 建立在明示规则上，不论是否由机器执行；algorithmic 通常暗示由程序执行。

entries.definition: Done in a fixed, unthinking way; close to one sense of algorithmic, but it carries a stronger tone of dullness.
entries.definitionCN: 以固定、不加思考的方式做；接近 algorithmic 的一义，但更带呆板色彩。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real base noun, the real ending and the real phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的基础名词、真实的词尾与真实搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Algorithm plus -ic: the ending means relating to, so algorithmic means belonging to an algorithm.
normal.cn: algorithm 加 -ic：词尾意为「与……有关」，所以 algorithmic 就是属于算法的。

normal.en: The family runs algorithm, algorithmic, algorithmically and algorithmics.
normal.cn: 同族词有 algorithm、algorithmic、algorithmically 与 algorithmics。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the modern uses: algorithmic trading, algorithmic bias, algorithmic recommendation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出现代用法：算法交易、算法偏见、算法推荐。

normal.en: The base is a person's name, so the adjective literally means in the manner of al-Khwarizmi's rules.
normal.cn: 词基是人名，因此这个形容词字面上就是「按花拉子米的规则来」。

normal.en: Greek -ikos became Latin -icus and English -ic, so the ending simply means relating to.
normal.cn: 希腊语 -ikos 变成拉丁语 -icus 与英语 -ic，词尾意思就是「与……有关」。

abstract.en: Picture a river that chooses its own channels without a digger.
abstract.cn: 想象一条没有挖掘者却自己选道的河。

abstract.en: Picture a judge who never explains, only applies.
abstract.cn: 想象一位从不解释、只作适用的法官。

abstract.en: Picture a painting that keeps painting itself after the artist leaves.
abstract.cn: 想象一幅在画家离开后仍继续画自己的画。

examples.en: Algorithmic sorting decides the order before any editor sees the list.
examples.cn: 算法排序在编辑看到清单之前就决定了顺序。

examples.en: The company publishes an algorithmic audit every year.
examples.cn: 公司每年公布一份算法审计报告。

examples.en: Her algorithmic music is generated from a few simple rules.
examples.cn: 她的算法音乐由几条简单规则生成。

root: al-Khwārizmī 之名 → 拉丁 Algoritmi → algorismus → algorism/algorithm；再加希腊—拉丁形容词词尾 -ic。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from plain attribution to formal steps, generated output, rule-bound decisions, measured cost, mechanical repetition, generative art and finally the fairness of automated choices.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从单纯的归属关系，走到形式步骤、生成产物、受规则支配的决策、被度量的开销、机械重复、生成艺术，最后走到自动选择的公平问题。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: streams of data sliding along invisible rails into slots, with no hand anywhere in the picture.
core.cn: 核心意象：数据流沿看不见的轨道滑进槽口，画面里没有任何一只手。

branches.en: ATTRIBUTION AND FORM: belonging to a procedure, and laid out as checkable steps.
branches.cn: 归属与形式：属于某种步骤，并被铺成可核对的步骤。

branches.en: OUTPUT AND SAMENESS: what the procedure produces, and the exact repetition that makes it trustworthy or cold.
branches.cn: 产物与一致：步骤产出的东西，以及使它可信或冷冰冰的精确重复。

branches.en: RULE OVER JUDGMENT: discretion disappears into fixed rules, even without a machine.
branches.cn: 规则压过判断：裁量消失于固定规则，哪怕没有机器。

branches.en: COST: procedures are compared by the time and memory they need as input grows.
branches.cn: 开销：步骤按输入增大时所需的时间与内存被比较。

branches.en: CULTURE AND POLITICS: rules generate art, and automated choices raise the question of who answers for them.
branches.cn: 文化与政治：规则生成艺术，自动选择则提出谁来负责的问题。

intro.en: The word is a name-derived base plus a Greek adjective ending that reached English through Latin and French.
intro.cn: 这个词是人名来源的词基加一个希腊形容词词尾，后者经拉丁语与法语进入英语。

latinIntro.en: Medieval Latin algorismus supplies the base; Latin -icus supplies the shape of the ending, which English shortened.
latinIntro.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 algorismus 提供词基；拉丁语 -icus 提供词尾的外形，英语再把它缩短。

items.example: The Latin noun is the base of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词是整个词族的词基。

items.example: The Greek word caused the -th- respelling by mistake.
items.exampleCN: 这个希腊词误改了拼写，加进 -th-。

items.example: The noun supplies the meaning the adjective carries.
items.exampleCN: 名词提供形容词所承载的意义。

items.example: The ending turns a thing into a description.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把事物变成描述词。

items.example: Algorithmically means by running the procedure.
items.exampleCN: algorithmically 意为按算法运行。

items.example: Algorithmics studies procedures and their costs.
items.exampleCN: algorithmics 研究步骤及其开销。

items.example: Algorism names the old calculation practice.
items.exampleCN: algorism 指旧的计算做法。

items.meaning: relating to or produced by a procedure
items.meaningCN: 与算法有关的或由算法产生的
items.example: The word now covers trading, art and bias.
items.exampleCN: 这个词如今涵盖交易、艺术与偏见。

items.example: The list is ordered algorithmically.
items.exampleCN: 清单按算法排序。

definition_zh: 细胞膜；质膜；包裹细胞质的磷脂双分子层
definition_en: the thin barrier of lipid and protein that surrounds a cell and controls what enters or leaves
core_image: 显微镜下一枚细胞被荧光勾出细边，染料在边外停住
scene: 显微镜下，一枚细胞被荧光勾出细细的边，染料在边外停住。 The cell membrane lets water through but keeps most dyes outside.
sceneCN: 这里取第 1 个义项（细胞膜）；句意为细胞膜允许水通过，却把大多数染料挡在外面。

pos.zh: 名词短语：细胞膜；质膜

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁表示「皮、膜」的名词构成，义为「膜；薄膜」
由「膜」加形容词词尾构成，义为「膜的；膜状的」
由拉丁表示「小室」的名词构成，义为「细胞；小室」
由「细胞」加形容词词尾构成，义为「细胞的；多孔的」
由表示「在下、次级」的前缀加形容词构成，义为「亚细胞的」
由表示「在内」的前缀加形容词构成，义为「细胞内的」

senses.title: The boundary of a cell
senses.definition: the outer boundary separating the cytoplasm from the surrounding medium
senses.definitionCN: 指把细胞质与周围介质隔开的外边界
senses.example: Every cell membrane separates inside from outside.
senses.exampleCN: 每一层细胞膜都把内与外分开。
senses.why: A cell is a room, and a room needs a wall; the phrase names that wall.
senses.whyCN: 细胞是一间屋子，屋子需要墙，这条短语说的就是那面墙。

senses.title: The phospholipid bilayer
senses.definition: the double sheet of lipid molecules with their heads outward and tails inward
senses.definitionCN: 指脂质分子头朝外、尾朝内排成的双层薄片
senses.example: The cell membrane is a bilayer only a few nanometres thick.
senses.exampleCN: 细胞膜是仅几纳米厚的双分子层。
senses.why: The barrier is not solid but a double layer of molecules, which explains its fluid behaviour.
senses.whyCN: 这层屏障并非实心，而是分子的双层，这解释了它的流动性。

senses.title: A selectively permeable barrier
senses.definition: the property of admitting some substances while excluding others
senses.definitionCN: 指允许某些物质通过、同时排斥另一些物质的性质
senses.example: The cell membrane is selectively permeable to ions.
senses.exampleCN: 细胞膜对离子具有选择性通透。
senses.why: The wall is picky: small neutral molecules pass, charged ones usually need help.
senses.whyCN: 这面墙很挑剔：小的中性分子能过，带电的通常需要帮助。

senses.title: The site of transport proteins
senses.definition: the place where channels, pumps and carriers move substances across
senses.definitionCN: 指通道、泵与载体把物质运送过去的地方
senses.example: Ion channels in the cell membrane open in response to a signal.
senses.exampleCN: 细胞膜中的离子通道会响应信号而开启。
senses.why: Because the lipid layer rejects charge, proteins must supply the doors.
senses.whyCN: 脂质层排斥电荷，因此必须由蛋白质提供门。

senses.title: A signalling interface
senses.definition: the surface where receptors detect hormones, signals or neighbouring cells
senses.definitionCN: 指受体探测激素、信号或邻近细胞的表面
senses.example: Receptors on the cell membrane detect the hormone.
senses.exampleCN: 细胞膜上的受体探测这种激素。
senses.why: A cell must listen before it acts, and the membrane is its ear.
senses.whyCN: 细胞要先听再行动，而细胞膜就是它的耳朵。

senses.title: A shape-giving and anchoring layer
senses.titleCN: 维持形状与锚定的结构层
senses.definition: the layer that gives the cell shape and anchors its internal skeleton and proteins
senses.definitionCN: 指赋予细胞形状、并锚定内部骨架与蛋白的层次
senses.example: The cell membrane anchors the fibres that hold its shape.
senses.exampleCN: 细胞膜锚定维持形状的纤维。
senses.why: A thin skin can still organise everything attached to it.
senses.whyCN: 一层薄膜仍能组织起附着在它上面的一切。

senses.title: A structure compared across cell types
senses.titleCN: 不同细胞类型间的结构比较
senses.definition: the membrane as it appears in bacteria, archaea, plants or animals, with different lipids and additions
senses.definitionCN: 指细菌、古菌、植物或动物细胞中因脂质与附加结构不同而呈现的膜
senses.example: The bacterial cell membrane lacks the cholesterol found in animals.
senses.exampleCN: 细菌细胞膜缺少动物细胞中的胆固醇。
senses.why: The same barrier is built differently in different branches of life, and comparison reveals which parts are essential.
senses.whyCN: 同一道屏障在不同生命分支里造法不同，比较便能显出哪些部件必不可少。

senses.title: A model and a drug target
senses.definition: an artificial or studied membrane used to test transport, or a target for medicines
senses.definitionCN: 指用于测试运输的人工或研究对象膜，或药物作用的靶点
senses.example: Many drugs act on the cell membrane rather than inside it.
senses.exampleCN: 许多药物作用于细胞膜而非细胞内部。
senses.why: If the boundary is where signals arrive, it is also the easiest place to interrupt them.
senses.whyCN: 若边界是信号到达之处，它也是最容易拦截信号的地方。

intro.en: Cell comes from Latin cella, a small room or store, and English applied it to the units of living tissue in the seventeenth century. Membrane comes from Latin membrana, a skin or parchment, generally said to derive from membrum, a limb. The compound cell membrane belongs to nineteenth-century microscopy.
intro.cn: 「细胞」出自拉丁语 cella「小室、储藏间」，英语在十七世纪把它用于活组织的单位。「膜」出自拉丁语 membrana「皮、羊皮纸」，一般认为来自 membrum「肢体」。这条合成短语属于十九世纪的显微观察传统。

items.en: Cella meant a small room, a storeroom or a shrine chamber.
items.cn: 这个词意为小室、储藏间或神庙内殿。

items.en: Microscopists used the room word for the box-like spaces they saw in cork.
items.cn: 显微观察者用这个「小室」词指他们在软木中看到的格子状空间。

items.en: Membrana meant a skin, a thin covering or parchment.
items.cn: 这个词意为皮、薄膜或羊皮纸。

items.en: The word for a limb is generally taken as the base of membrana, though the link is not certain.
items.cn: 表示「肢体」的词一般认为就是「膜」这个词的基底，但这一联系并不确定。

items.en: English took the Latin noun for any thin sheet, anatomical or otherwise.
items.cn: 英语借入这个拉丁名词，指任何薄膜，解剖学内外皆可。

items.en: Microscopists named the boundary they could see at the edge of a cell; the molecular structure was worked out in the twentieth century.
items.cn: 显微观察者为他们在细胞边缘看到的界线命名；其分子结构在二十世纪才被阐明。

note.en: The first group shares the cell or membrane element; the second group names the same barrier technically or names neighbouring structures.
note.cn: 第一组共享「细胞」或「膜」的成分；第二组是同一屏障的技术名称，或相邻结构。

entries.definition: Any thin sheet covering or lining a surface.
entries.definitionCN: 指覆盖或衬在某表面的任何薄膜。

entries.definition: Made of or like a membrane.
entries.definitionCN: 指由膜构成的，或像膜一样的。

entries.definition: The basic unit of living tissue.
entries.definitionCN: 指活组织的基本单位。

entries.definition: Relating to cells or divided into small compartments.
entries.definitionCN: 指与细胞有关的，或分成小格的。

entries.definition: The rigid outer layer of plant and bacterial cells.
entries.definitionCN: 指植物与细菌细胞外层的坚硬结构。

entries.definition: The technical synonym for the membrane around a cell.
entries.definitionCN: 指包住细胞的膜的技术同义词。

entries.definition: The double molecular sheet that makes up most of the membrane.
entries.definitionCN: 指构成膜大部分的分子双层。

entries.definition: All the outer layers of a bacterium, membrane plus wall and capsule.
entries.definitionCN: 指细菌的全部外层，包括膜、壁与荚膜。

entries.definition: The lipid with a charged head that builds the bilayer.
entries.definitionCN: 指带电荷头部的脂质，构成双分子层。

entries.definition: A protein that detects a signal at the membrane.
entries.definitionCN: 指在膜上探测信号的蛋白质。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations follow the room and its thin wall, then the doors and ears built into that wall.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想沿着「房间」与「薄墙」展开，再想到墙上开的门与耳朵。

normal.en: A cell is a room, so its membrane is the wall.
normal.cn: 细胞是一间屋子，细胞膜就是墙。

normal.en: The wall is two layers of lipid, heads out and tails in.
normal.cn: 这面墙由两层脂质构成，头朝外、尾朝内。

normal.en: Charged ions cannot cross alone, so proteins provide doors.
normal.cn: 带电离子不能独自穿过，蛋白质便提供门。

normal.en: The membrane is also the cell's ear, full of receptors.
normal.cn: 细胞膜也是细胞的耳朵，布满受体。

normal.en: Plant cells add a wall outside the membrane; bacteria wrap both in an envelope.
normal.cn: 植物细胞在膜外再加一层壁，细菌则把两者都裹进被膜里。

abstract.en: A boundary is not a prison; it is what makes an inside possible.
abstract.cn: 边界不是监狱，而是让「内部」得以存在的东西。

abstract.en: The thinner the wall, the more carefully it must choose what passes.
abstract.cn: 墙越薄，就越要仔细选择让什么通过。

abstract.en: Every cell listens at its skin before it acts.
abstract.cn: 每个细胞都先在皮肤上倾听，然后才行动。

examples.en: The cell membrane controls the movement of salts into the cytoplasm.
examples.cn: 细胞膜控制盐分进入细胞质的运动。

examples.en: Freeze-fracture reveals proteins embedded in the cell membrane.
examples.cn: 冷冻断裂法显示出嵌在细胞膜中的蛋白质。

examples.en: Some viruses fuse with the cell membrane to enter.
examples.cn: 有些病毒与细胞膜融合而进入。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「塞尔·门布瑞恩」——一间小室（塞尔）外面绷着一层薄膜（门布瑞恩），就是细胞膜：细胞膜、质膜

root: 「细胞」出自拉丁语 cella「小室」，十七世纪被用于活组织单位；「膜」出自拉丁语 membrana「皮、羊皮纸」，一般认为来自 membrum「肢体」，但联系不确定；合成短语属十九世纪显微观察。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses build up from the boundary itself to its molecular sheet, its selectivity, its doors, its ears, its scaffolding, its variation across cells and its use as a model or target.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从边界本身逐步往上：分子薄片、选择性、门、耳朵、支架、在不同细胞中的差异，以及作为模型或靶点的用途。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a glowing thin outline around a cell under a microscope, with dye stopping at the edge.
core.cn: 核心意象：显微镜下一枚细胞被荧光勾出细边，染料在边沿停住。

branches.en: THE WALL AND ITS BUILD: the boundary, and the molecular double sheet that makes it.
branches.cn: 墙与做法：边界本身，以及构成它的分子双层。

branches.en: WHAT PASSES: selective permeability, and the proteins that open the doors.
branches.cn: 什么能过：选择性通透，以及开门的蛋白质。

branches.en: THE EAR: receptors that let a cell hear its surroundings.
branches.cn: 耳朵：让细胞听见周围环境的受体。

branches.en: THE SCAFFOLD: shape and anchoring for the cell's internal fibres.
branches.cn: 支架：为细胞内部纤维提供形状与锚定。

branches.en: THE VARIATIONS AND USES: membranes across cell types, and membranes as models or drug targets.
branches.cn: 差异与用途：不同细胞类型的膜，以及作为模型或药物靶点的膜。

intro.en: The phrase is a Latin room plus a Latin skin, a plain description that later acquired a molecular meaning.
intro.cn: 这条短语是拉丁语的「房间」加「皮」，本是朴素描述，后来才获得分子层面的含义。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies both nouns: the small room and the thin covering.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供两个名词：小室与薄膜。

items.example: It is the source of cell and cellar.
items.exampleCN: 它是「细胞」与「地窖」等词的来源。

items.example: The biological sense dates from the seventeenth century.
items.exampleCN: 生物学义可追溯到十七世纪。

items.example: It is the source of membrane.
items.exampleCN: 它是「膜」一词的来源。

items.example: It is generally taken as the base of the skin word, though not with certainty.
items.exampleCN: 它一般被认为是「膜」词的基底，但并不确定。

items.example: English uses it in anatomy and chemistry.
items.exampleCN: 英语在解剖与化学中使用它。

items.example: It forms membranous, like a membrane.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「膜状的」。

items.example: It gives the technical synonym plasma membrane.
items.exampleCN: 它构成技术同义词「质膜」。

items.example: It names the molecules that build the bilayer.
items.exampleCN: 它指构成双层的分子。

items.example: It forms bilayer, the two-layer structure.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「双层」。

items.example: It forms semipermeable, letting some things through.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「半透的」，即只让部分物质通过。
